Ted Lasso has killed off a fan favourite character who’s been on the show since the very first season

The ninth episode of the Apple TV show’s fourth season unexpectedly waved goodbye to an original star in what the actor has described as “the very best way”.

*Spoilers follow – you have been warned*

Pub landlady Mae Green, played by Annette Badland, died after travelling from Richmond to the Lady Greyhounds away match against Bristol City. After expressing concern about making the lengthy trip, Ted (Jason Sudeikis) invited her to join the team on the team bus.

At the match, she gives up her seat alongside Rebecca (Hannah Waddingham) in the box so she can watch from the crowd, but the excitement becomes too much. Viewers learn that Mae has collapsed when Rebecca (Hannah Waaddingham) is told, and she walks into the locker room to discover from Ted that Mae has died.

Badland told TV Insider that she was “devastated” to learn the news when Sudeikis told her, and immediately asked: “Can she come back as an angel?” prompting Sudeikis to make some changes to the 10th episode.

“She is there as a presence, if not a full-bodied human being,” the actor revealed.

'Ted Lasso' has said goodbye to pub landlady Mae (Annette Badland) ( Apple TV )

Badland has since come to terms with her character’s fate, stating: “It’s what Jason wants to say about the world of human beings, and I think that is terrific.”

She added to Deadline: “That’s what happens. You’re involved with folks, and they disappear. And she loved her life. She made the very best of her life and really relished it. So she went, I suppose, for her, in the very best way.”

Badland also confirmed that Ted Lasso wasn’t originally designed to return for another season, with the cast convinced it would just be three.

“We didn’t think there would be another,” she said. “Jason had said, ‘I’ve got a three-series arc, that’ll be it.” And then to go back, it’s very exciting because it’s a risk, isn’t it?”

Season four follows Ted as he returns to England to coach Richmond FC’s newly launched, second-division women’s team. This meant that the original stars who portrayed the men’s soccer team in the first three seasons do not appear in season four.

This includes a number of fan favorites: Toheeb Jimoh’s Sam Obisanya, Cristo Fernández’s Dani Rojas, Kola Bokinni’s Isaac McAdoo, Billy Harris’s Collin Hughes, and Nick Mohammed’s former AFC Richmond assistant coach-turned-rival-West Ham United coach, Nathan Shelley.

The student protest movement that has spread ​across France is now "out of control", the Paris police chief has said as up to 500 schools are set to remain closed on Monday.

Riot police clashed with high school students across France on Friday and unions called for teachers to strike as President Emmanuel Macron's government battled to contain increasingly violent protests ⁠over classroom conditions and funding.

Up to 500 schools in the country will be totally or partly closed on Monday, the education minister said. Edouard Geffray added that 24 schools had been “burned or ransacked” since the start of the movement.

The Paris police chief urged demonstrators to return to peaceful action and warning that authorities would respond firmly ⁠to violence and vandalism.

Since ​Monday, ⁠around 5,000 people, mostly teenagers, have been arrested nationwide and dozens injured.

Agathe Foucault, a spokesperson for the ⁠national police, told RTL radio on Saturday that more than ​600 ⁠police officers had also been ‌injured.

open image in gallery Students hold a placard which reads as 'Finance Minister, review your finances' (L) and 'Angry young people, but not fascists' (R), during a gathering amid a nationwide protest movement over school conditions in Saint-Denis, north of Paris, on October 4, 2026 ( AFP/Getty )

Teachers and members of the public have been attacked, while damage to property is estimated in the tens ‌of millions of euros.

Paris police chief Patrice ‌Faure, in an open letter published on X ahead of planned renewed protests from next Tuesday, said those who had launched the movement no ⁠longer controlled it and called on students to abandon school blockades and unrest in favour of peaceful forms of protest.

Here's what to know about the France protests

The start of the protests

Protests first erupted in the Paris region in mid-September. Teachers and students mobilized against a lack of staff at a lycée, or high school, in Creteil, in the southeastern outskirts of the French capital. From there, class strikes, blockades and demonstrations spread to other Paris suburbs and then nationwide, with protests even in high schools of smaller towns.

Hundreds of schools have had to close because of damage or attacks that targeted staff, according to the education minister. More than 170 pupils and 65 staff members have suffered injuries, he says.

What the protestors want

From the outset, pupils focused on perceived inequalities in the school system, saying that teaching, facilities and opportunities for advancement aren't as good for students in disadvantaged neighborhoods — despite the promise of France's national motto: "Liberty, Equality, Fraternity."

Placards held up by the first protesters in Creteil read "Too many inequalities, we're disgusted," "Education is a right, not a privilege," and "Sorry to bother, it's for our future," according to photos posted by Clémence Guetté, the district's lawmaker at the National Assembly, France's parliament.

Pupils elsewhere complained that during summer heat waves, they roast in classrooms without air-conditioning, and they freeze in winter. French media broadcast videos of scampering rats, collapsed ceilings, leaks, broken furniture and other woes filmed in dilapidated schools.

"The public needs to know that conditions for studying are no longer what they were for us," said Sophie Bordy, a 50-year-old literature teacher in Paris. "It has deteriorated significantly."

open image in gallery A high school student throws a tear gas canister as he protests to demand more resources for schools, in Lille, France, Wednesday, Sept. 30, 2026. (AP Photo/Jean-Francois Badias) ( AP )

Still, spending on education is one of the costliest items in the state budget that Macron's government is proposing for 2027. It earmarked 65.5 billion euros ($74 billion) for schools, more than the 63.4 billion euros for defense.

Pupils also complain of long hours. In high schools, classes often start at 8 a.m. and can last to the early evening. French high schoolers' compulsory school hours are among the highest in Europe, according to European Union figures.

"I see the teachers more than my family," read one young girl's placard photographed by Le Parisien newspaper.

Strong far-left support

Guetté, the lawmaker who posted photos of herself meeting with the first protesters in Creteil, bullhorn in hand, is a rising star of the far-left France Unbowed party. Other France Unbowed lawmakers and elected officials also quickly identified with the protests, meeting with pupils and backing their demands.

France Unbowed leader Jean-Luc Mélenchon urged party members and supporters to protect pupils from the police, by putting themselves in between the two sides.

Mélenchon has denounced what he called the "savagery" of police officers who have liberally used tear gas and their batons to break up crowds. Police riot-control projectiles are suspected in some facial injuries that young protesters suffered.

Critics of Mélenchon accuse France Unbowed of stoking and manipulating the pupils for political gain. Mélenchon, a fiery anti-capitalist, says his party supports the movement but isn't organizing it and wants it to be non-violent.

Mélenchon, 75, is making his fourth run for the French presidency and is wooing young voters. They tended to vote less than other age groups in the last presidential election in 2022 but could potentially help Mélenchon qualify for the decisive second-round runoff in May — a success that has always escaped him — if he can mobilize them to turn out.

"What we want is for this country's young people to emerge from this episode with their heads held high, having won something and learned something, and to remember it when they cast their ballots," Mélenchon said Thursday.

News.title: Brilliant Hamilton storms to podium despite another Ferrari blunder
News.content:
One of the big talking points heading into the weekend has been the cooling vests drivers wear under their overalls (as opposed to the jacket-like ones they wear when they’re out of their cars). Russell told us in our Brits media session on Thursday that Mercedes had decided to forego the vests here, since the technology was not yet refined. The system works by pumping a coolant through thin tubes stitched into the vest.

Drivers have complained that the connecting valve to the pump, which was originally placed on the side of the vest, proved uncomfortable when combined with the high G-forces experienced in an F1 car. On some vests the connector has been moved to find a more comfortable position, but the thick material and tubing have also proved cumbersome under the driver’s fireproof overalls. There are also concerns over the reliability of some systems and the possibility that a failure will mean the vest will have the opposite effect and work as a heat insulator.preferring to spend that money instead on car upgrades. The money to develop the vests comes out of the budget cap.

But Russell added that the FIA should make the tech mandatory and develop it themselves, describing this race as like being in a “sauna”.The Briton’s comments prompted a sarcastic response from Verstappen - who doesn’t wear the vests either, out of choice - who said Russell “shouldn’t make a fuss”.

“I don’t need it,” Verstappen said. “Maybe I suffer a bit less from the heat.. I find a Finnish sauna at 85 degrees a lot hotter... You shouldn’t make a fuss. Yes, it is hot, but that’s part of it. You have to train for that.”

The Dutchman added: “When I was 18, I had a bit more trouble with these conditions. But after that, I started training more in the heat, such as in the sauna and a steam room, so that I can handle the sweating better and the fact that your head gets very hot. Maybe I should take him (Russell) to the sauna a few times.”

These two have history, of course. They’ve sniped at each other for years. In 2024, in Qatar and Abu Dhabi, it reached a peak when Verstappen described Russell as being “two-faced” and said he had lost all respect for him. Russell responded by saying Verstappen was “a bully”. Earlier this year, the Mercedes driver said Verstappen could always retire from the sport and drive sports cars if he didn’t like the regs.

News.title: Rees-Zammit taunts Pollock as Bristol outplay Northampton
News.content:
Good afternoon and welcome to Telegraph Sport’s live coverage of Bristol Bears vs Northampton Saints from the Gallagher Prem, with both teams looking to build on winning starts following the opening weekend of action.

Last season’s champions Northampton kicked off their title defence with an emphatic 59-26 victory over a new-look Newcastle Red Bulls outfit at Franklin’s Gardens.

While Henry Pollock’s new cornrow hairstyle was the centre of attention at kick-off, the limelight was soon stolen by Tommy Freeman and James Pater, who both notched hat-tricks for Phil Dowson’s side.

Of 19-year-old full-back Pater, who starts on the bench today, Dowson said afterwards: “He doesn’t let the occasion get to him. He has an incredible skill set, great speed and ability to manoeuvre away from defenders.”

Bristol, meanwhile, began their season with an impressive 34-24 victory away at Sale Sharks, with Pat Lam’s side ensuring Courtney Lawes’s return to the English game was a disappointing one.

Louis Rees-Zammit was operating in his favoured wing position and got Bristol off to a strong start with two tries in the opening 23 minutes, offering Lam hope of a fruitful campaign from the Welshman.

“When you look at our wingers in the past, they scored a lot of tries and Louis is a world-class finisher,” the Bristol director of rugby said. “You get the ball to him in space and you create the opportunity, there’s a good chance he’ll finish it.”

Northampton will be hoping for a repeat of the meeting between the sides at Franklin Gardens in May when they thumped Bristol 94-33, but they have not won at Ashton Gate since 2021.

Both teams have made a pair of changes following their opening-weekend victories, with England international Ellis Genge among the players to drop out after spraining his wrist against Sale.

News.title: Sublime England thrash Croatia in best performance for a decade
News.content:
We came out of the World Cup wondering if Tuchel really had an idea of how he can get England over the line. After last Saturday’s defeat by world and European champions Spain, followed by Tuesday’s win over the Czech Republic we still did not know.

But here the standard was set – it was an exhilarating example of the football England are capable of. On display we saw the speed, the movement, the passes under pressure, the ambition, the control and aggression. This was the full package. Bottle it. Bag it. Believe it.

Croatia have an ageing team and are in transition, but they were left looking callow. It looked as though it was men against boys. There were plenty of boys in the stands, with 6,200 children allowed in for what was supposed to be a behind-closed-doors fixture – Croatia’s punishment for crowd trouble.

Their new head coach Slaven Bilic would doubtless have been relieved that the match was not played in front of the usual, passionate, partisan crowd. Even then some of the kids booed and left early. Bilic looked shell-shocked. As well he might.

News.title: Russell must do something wacky now after disappointing Bahrain GP qualifying
News.content:
The screens in the media centre here in Sepang tell me that the air temp right now is 32.8C and the track temp is 58C. It feels even hotter. Lots of chat about cooling vests this week, which are optional. George Russell is among the drivers who isn’t using one, which is interesting a) because Russell has suffered badly from heat in the past (Qatar, Singapore) and b) because he says Mercedes chose to put the development money into car upgrades instead.

It’s an interesting admission. Not everyone is sold on the idea of cooling vests. Ferrari and McLaren will definitely be using them this weekend, for instance. Max Verstappen won’t as he doesn’t like them. Russell thinks the FIA should just develop the tech themselves and it shouldn’t be part of the budget cap.

“Our team have put a lot of emphasis this year on the cockpit temperature,” he said. “We won’t be running the cooling vest because we haven’t put the resource into making it robust enough. I feel we need the FIA just to step in and say ‘Here’s some money extra in the cost cap or there’s an external company who’s going to develop it for everybody’. Because we should all be wearing it. When it works, it works great. So, I would like to wear it this week, and I would like to wear it next week. But the team asked me...look, we can develop it, and we can put the money towards it...[but at a cost].

He added: “The top itself is not expensive ..you’ve got to effectively make a system where you can fit a block of dry ice or actual ice, and then has the airflow to circulate the cool water throughout. If that system isn’t robust enough, then suddenly you have no circulation, and then you get hot. You get ambient temperature circulating. The vest is one-design, but the system that circulates the water is different [at different teams].”

News.title: Bath complete revenge mission on Exeter despite imperious Feyi-Waboso
News.content:
Bath held off a furious comeback from Exeter, led by the irrepressible Immanuel Feyi-Waboso, to avenge their Gallagher Prem semi-final defeat here in June.

It felt as if lightning might strike Bath twice. Once again Exeter overturned a 26-10 half-time deficit, to manufacture a second-half lead thanks to a pair of blistering finishes by Feyi-Waboso. Four months ago, Bath failed to take a drop goal in the closing stages, but this time with the reassuring presence of Finn Russell at fly-half, they kept their cool.

The Scotland playmaker twice sent penalties deep into the Exeter 22 from where Stephen Varney conceded a yellow card and penalty try before Bath replacement Ted Hill powered through a thicket of Exeter tacklers.

“Finn is one of the best 10s in the world and I thought he had a very good game,” Johann van Graan, the Bath head of rugby, said. “His decision making is above most players in the world and I thought that came through tonight.”

Despite the appearance of yet another high-scoring shoot-out, both teams defended with real bite, although Bath struggled to lay a finger on Feyi-Waboso who ended up in a scrap with a fan in the stands here when he was a spectator in May. He exacted a measure of revenge beating eight defenders and carried for 132 metres.

“Manny still needs game time,” Rob Baxter, the Exeter director of rugby, said. “When he’s on the ball, you see something incredible, but it is his ability to get on the ball again. He is just getting his game minutes and match fitness up.”

News.title: FTSE 100 tumbles amid bond market sell-off
News.content:
Thanks for joining me. House prices fell unexpectedly last month as mortgage borrowers prepare for a jump in interest rates.

Typical property values declined by 0.2pc during September, reversing 0.2pc growth in August, according to the Nationwide house price index.

The figure was much worse than analysts had forecasts, with most expecting prices to remain steady.

Over the course of the year to September, the rate of house price growth halved from 1.6pc to 0.8pc, which was the weakest rate since December 2025.

The value of the average home has fallen to £274,251 over concerns the Bank of England is on the cusp of raising interest rates, making borrowing more expensive for mortgage holders.

Money markets indicate there is an 84pc chance policymakers will raise rates from 3.75pc to 4pc in November in an effort to bring down inflation caused by the Iran war energy shock.

Robert Gardner, chief economist at Nationwide, said:“Market activity and house prices have remained subdued in recent months, in part reflecting the uncertain economic backdrop.

“Geopolitical tensions remain high, with the conflict in the Middle East exerting upward pressure on energy prices, fanning inflation concerns.

News.title: Chewing tobacco killed 250,000 people in one year, study shows
News.content:
Chewing tobacco killed around a quarter of a million people in 2023, with use of the product remaining stubbornly high, according to research.

The smokeless tobacco, which is placed between the cheek and lower gum, is particularly popular in south Asia. It is flavoured and sometimes sweetened, and users often spit out unwanted juices while chewing. It is often viewed as safer than smoking but it is a major cause of stroke, as well as head and neck cancer.

Chewing tobacco is different to white snus or nicotine pouches, which contain no tobacco. These white pouches are also made up of flavourings and sometimes sweeteners, and deliver a hit of nicotine through the lining of the mouth.

Despite a successful fight against smoking over the last few decades, rates of chewing tobacco use have fallen little and it has often been overlooked in tobacco control efforts, researchers point out. In a study published in the Lancet Global Health, researchers from the Institute for Health Metrics and Evaluation in the US estimate that 241 million people aged 15 years and older used chewing tobacco in 2023.

Researchers looked at data on use in 204 countries between 1990 and 2023 and found that there was no significant decrease in the number of users of chewing tobacco over that period. And in 24 countries there was a significant uptick in the number of people using the product. Researchers estimate that about one in five men and one in 10 women in south Asia chewed tobacco in 2023.

Bangladesh has seen the biggest increase in the number of people using the product with 15 million new users between 1990 and 2023. Nepal, Madagascar and Yemen also saw increases in the number of users.

In India 105 million people chew tobacco regularly, accounting for just over two thirds of users globally. Historically, Indians would chew paan, tobacco in its raw form which was mixed with betel leaf and areca nut, a mild stimulant. But the use of chewing tobacco exploded in the 1980s when manufacturers began grinding these into a powder and selling them in packets known as gutkha. This was banned in 2012 but is still widely available. Chewing tobacco is also popular in Pakistan, China and Vietnam.

News.title: Esther Rantzen dies aged 86
News.content:
Dame Esther was a vocal supporter of the Assisted Dying Bill, claiming in March that most people “want and need” the right to end their own lives.

When the bill was defeated in the House of Commons in September, as MPs voted 286 to 270 against the legislation, she called it a “tragic day”. The bill would have allowed those with less than six months to live to seek medical assistance to end their lives.

In 2024, she said that she had joined the Dignitas assisted-dying clinic in Switzerland.

Writing for The Telegraph at the beginning of September, Rebecca Wilcox, Dame Esther’s daughter, said her mother was “too ill now to travel to Dignitas as she had planned and paid for”.

Earlier this month, Dame Esther said in a statement that it was too late for her to “buzz off” to the clinic in Switzerland and said Britain’s current laws on assisted dying are “messy and cruel”.

In a final message shared by her family, the presenter said she had been “immensely lucky” for the support she had received from the public, which she said had enabled her “to live such a long and happy life”.

She added: “Sadly, all good things come to an end, as they say. So I particularly wanted to say goodbye and thank you so very, very much. Perhaps I will see you eventually, on the other side. I do hope so. With very good wishes, as ever, Esther.”

SIR ALEX FERGUSON has opened up on his health and dementia fears in a rare interview.

The 84-year-old Manchester United legend has explained that his own footballing experiences have left him concerned about his future.



He has gone to great lengths to support his brother Martin’s journey with dementia, including buying a house in Glasgow to be closer to him.

Ferguson has also become a major supporter of dementia charities, including Formula 1 legend Jackie Stewart‘s Race Against Dementia.



He told The Observer: “I worried about that myself because I headed the ball a lot.”

“All footballers did. Dementia’s a challenge for anyone getting older. You worry about it a lot. I always say to myself: ‘I’m 84. If I get to 85, I’ll be all right.'”

Ferguson has drawn inspiration from former professional boxer Jake LaMotta, who had 106 fights and still lived until the age of 95.

LaMotta was portrayed in Martin Scorsese’s 1980 film Raging Bull.

The legendary manager has also explained that dementia charity Playlist for Life has helped to enhance his brother Martin’s quality of life.

Sir Alex added: “He recognises me, which is great. In Glasgow, they started a music thing, and the idea is that you give them a box with all your favourite songs in it. They can just press a button to play them, and it brings all the memories back.”

Is it ageing or dementia? Dementia – the most common form of which is Alzheimer’s – comes on slowly over time. As the disease progresses, symptoms can become more severe. But at the beginning, the symptoms can be subtle or mistaken for normal memory issues related to ageing. The US National Institute on Aging gives some examples of what is considered normal forgetfulness in old age, and dementia disease. You can refer to these above. For example, it is normal for an ageing person to forget which word to use from time-to-time, but difficulties having conversation would be more indicative of dementia. Katie Puckering, Head of Alzheimer’s Research UK’s Information Services team, previously told The Sun: “We quite commonly as humans put our car keys somewhere out of the ordinary and it takes longer for us to find them. “As you get older, it takes longer for you to recall, or you really have to think; What was I doing? Where was I? What distracted me? Was it that I had to let the dog out? And then you find the keys by the back door. “That process of retrieving the information is just a bit slower in people as they age. “In dementia, someone may not be able to recall that information and what they did when they came into the house. “What may also happen is they might put it somewhere it really doesn’t belong. For example, rather than putting the milk back in the fridge, they put the kettle in the fridge.”

This was met with a generous £100,000 donation to the charity, with Ferguson submitting a playlist featuring songs from Frank Sinatra, the Beatles, and Elvis Presley.

However, he has remained in good spirits as he continues to support United from the stands.

Sports.title: Cristiano Ronaldo's wife deletes fake Sir Alex Ferguson quote after dig at Portugal boss
Sports.content:
Cristiano Ronaldo's wife deletes fake Sir Alex Ferguson quote after dig at Portugal boss

Cristiano Ronaldo is at the centre of a row involving Portugal manager Jorge Jesus - and his wife Georgina Rodriguez unwittingly posted fake Sir Alex Ferguson quotes about the situation

View 3 Images Georgina Rodriguez deleted the Instagram post swiftly (Image: Justin Setterfield/Getty Images)

Cristiano Ronaldo's wife swiftly deleted a social media post criticising Portugal manager Jorge Jesus which used fake quotes from Sir Alex Ferguson.

‌



‌



Ronaldo has caused a storm in Portugal after abandoning the national team in the middle of their current Nations League international break. The Al-Nassr star fell out with Jesus after being left on the bench for a 2-1 win over Norway and has left his international career in major doubt.

‌



The 41-year-old held a crisis meeting with the Portuguese FA before leaving and posting a statement on social media which promised he would "tell all" about what had happened "in time".

‌



His disagreement with veteran manager Jesus, who also coached him at Al-Nassr last season, has dominated the build-up to Portugal's second match against Norway on Sunday night. And Rodriguez's post to her 78million Instagram followers grabbed the attention of fans.

Rodriguez shared a post claiming to quote former Manchester United manager Ferguson. It read: "If Jorge Jesus knew in his heart that he had no intention of using him, then why did he call him up in the first place? To make a point? That’s not authority, that’s insecurity."

In a caption, Rodriguez added: "I don’t know how this man (Jesus) can carry the name of Christ." It was only online for a matter of minutes before disappearing from her Instagram story on Saturday night. It is unclear why she deleted the post, but the quotes from Ronaldo's ex-United manager Ferguson are fake.

Ronaldo had stayed in Europe over the past few days, hinting that a bridge could be built between Portugal's all-time record goalscorer and the manager. But he is reportedly planning to take a private jet back to Saudi Arabia and focus on club football in Riyadh.

“The focus has to be on the national team above all else,” Jesus told a press conference on Saturday. “Regarding Norway, what we have to do well is for our people to also be in tune with the flag and the objective. Ronaldo is a symbol of the national team and of Portugal. After the game, there is plenty of time to talk about that.”

‌

Meanwhile, Bruno Fernandes revealed he had spoken to Ronaldo, but would continue to toe the line. “I had a conversation with Cris," the Manchester United captain said. "What I told him is that the most important thing, regardless of what happens, is that he will never cease to be the greatest symbol of our national team and country, for everything he has done in Portugal and around the world.

“He has a reserved place not only among the best of all time, but also in the hearts of the Portuguese people. We cannot divide ourselves; the national team is one, and all parties should resolve their issues behind closed doors."

World's largest stadium twice the size of Anfield takes shape in £28billion build

The world's largest stadium is set to open its doors for the first time next summer

View 3 Images The Trong Dong Stadium is set to look like this and hold 135,000 spectators (Image: TRONG DONG STADIUM)

Extraordinary images have emerged showing the building works for what is set to become the world’s largest stadium. Construction of the 135,000-seater VinFast Trong Dong Stadium in Hanoi, Vietnam, began nine months ago.

‌



‌



The stadium, named after and modelled on a traditional Vietnamese bronze drum, will have the largest capacity out of any stadium in the world, capable of hosting more than twice the number of Liverpool’s home, Anfield. It is hoped that it will open its doors by July 2027.

‌



It is being built at the centre of the broader Olympic Sports City development, which Reuters reports will cover around 22,200 acres on the outskirts of Hanoi. The total cost of the project is reportedly around $38billion (£28.8bn).

‌



Construction teams are working non-stop shifts to meet a demanding schedule. The reinforced concrete structure must be completed by December 2026, after which the installation of the dome system, electrical systems and finishing work will begin.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

The retractable roof is reportedly scheduled to be in place by May 2027, with the goal of opening the completed stadium in July 2027, one year ahead of the original target date of August 2028.

‌



Recent images of the building site show the ambitious project taking shape, with several cranes visible as the eye-catching vision comes to life. The colossal stadium already features steel columns, understood to be hydraulic jacking towers weighing more than 15,000 tonnes and rising 80 metres.

View 3 Images The project is currently nine months in as part of the Olympic Sports City development (Image: VTCNEWS)

Their function is to lift the steel arch modules, which will form the stadium's retractable dome, from the ground. Once completed, it will be the largest roof of its kind in the world.

‌



Designs suggest it will have a circular gold dome shaped like a trong dong drum, with a diameter of 408 metres. Its architecture reproduces the motifs of Dong Son bronze drums, considered a symbol of ancient Vietnamese culture.

They represent "the spirit of community, strength, and longevity," according to the project's architects. The stated intention is for the stadium to become "an architectural and cultural icon representing Vietnam in the new era."

View 3 Images The stadium will have the largest capacity in the world (Image: Trong Dong Stadium)

Article continues below

Vietnamese authorities are hoping that the facility will enable them to bid to host events on the scale of the World Cup or the Olympic Games.

The projected capacity of 135,000 will easily surpass other football stadiums. The biggest football ground in the world is currently the Rungrado 1st of May Stadium in Pyongyang, North Korea, which can host around 114,000.

Morocco’s Hassan II Stadium (115,000), is second. The ground is currently under construction for the 2030 World Cup.

Sports.title: 'I played with Robbie Fowler and Michael Owen – I know who was better Liverpool striker'
Sports.content:
'I played with Robbie Fowler and Michael Owen – I know who was better Liverpool striker'

Robbie Fowler and Michael Owen have both had their say on the long-running debate

View 2 Images Michael Owen and Robbie Fowler disagree on the subject (Image: ODD ANDERSEN, AFP via Getty Images)

Steven Gerrard has reluctantly settled a debate over who was the best player - Robbie Fowler or Michael Owen. The argument over which of the two Liverpool striking legends was superior has rumbled on for years, with both Fowler and Owen themselves having had their say.

‌



‌



Fowler once told Simon Jordan's Up Front show that he was the better player, saying: "He was quicker than me, but in every other element of being a striker, I genuinely think I was better than him.

‌



"He could say the exact opposite but that is just my opinion and my self-confidence. I was better in every aspect of being a striker.‌ Michael wasn't the best player at Liverpool when I played, but I remember him coming through at the club and you could see that he was different class."

‌



As you might expect, Owen begged to differ, citing his record with both the Reds and England. He said: "I would expect him to say that.

FOLLOW OUR LIVERPOOL FB PAGE! Latest Reds news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

"Listen, when I played for Liverpool, who did the manager pick? When I played for England, who did the manager pick? I mean, I don't have to say it – it was said for me."

‌



Man Utd legend makes 'worried' claim about Liverpool star with Premier League prediction READ MORE :

Angry Jurgen Klopp clashes with reporters again as his Germany tactics questioned READ MORE :

Gerrard grew up idolising Fowler, watching him from The Kop before eventually lining up alongside him. Yet having spent more time on the pitch with Owen, the former Liverpool captain leans towards the ex-Real Madrid and Newcastle striker.

Gerrard told Open Goal: "[They're] very different. I would say Fowler was a better natural finisher. But in terms of sort of like fear, in terms of pace, movement... [Owen was superior]. I had a real top connection with Michael Owen; it was like we were just on a wavelength together.

‌



"Both had a period [when they were exceptional]. Up until Michael did his hamstring, he was world-class and up there with the best strikers in the world."

The Anfield legend, who made his Reds debut in 1998, went on to say: "I didn't play with Robbie when he was getting 30 goals a season. I came a bit later when he'd had his injuries and he wasn't the player he was when he was 18 to 23.

View 2 Images Steven Gerrard is better qualified than most to answer the question (Image: Getty Images)

Article continues below

"I used to pay and watch him on The Kop and Robbie Fowler and Jamie Redknapp were my two heroes. Steve McManaman as well. I had the shirts with their names on, then you're sitting with them [in the dressing room] and they sort of become your mates."

While few are better qualified than Gerrard to weigh up the qualities of both players, this particular argument looks set to rumble on for years to come.

Sports.title: Meet the FA Cup minnows 'bigger than most Premier League teams' in Middle Eastern nation
Sports.content:
Meet the FA Cup minnows 'bigger than most Premier League teams' in Middle Eastern nation

National League South outfit Salisbury are making waves in Kuwait as well as the FA Cup

View 4 Images Salisbury FC are huge in Kuwait (Image: Salisbury FC)

A team playing in the sixth tier of English football are currently making waves in Kuwait. Salisbury FC, a phoenix club set up in 2014 in the wake of Salisbury City being thrown out of the Football Conference and placed in administration, recently embarked on a five-day trip to the Middle Eastern country.

‌



‌



There, they faced one of the nation’s most successful teams, Al Qadsia, on Wednesday - a club which has won more than 50 trophies. The Wiltshire outfit lost the friendly 3-2 and flew home on Thursday ahead of playing Dulwich Hamlet in the FA Cup third qualifying round.

‌



Salisbury wrapped up a surreal week by securing an emphatic 5-0 win to reach the furthest stage in the tournament since their reformation. They are now one win away from the first round proper, when League One and League Two sides join the fray.

‌



But there is a good reason why a team currently sitting third in the National League South has such ties with a Middle Eastern nation, where they are claimed to have a larger following than most Premier League clubs.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

In June 2025, Kuwaiti businessman Ali Alhamad bought the club. Alhamad, who has worked in manufacturing, the oil and gas industry, real estate, hospitality and cryptocurrency throughout his career, said after his takeover: "There is huge potential with the club, all over.

‌



"The city, the people that attend, it's a beautiful stadium, the people are wonderful. The main goal is creating a sustainable, well-run, community football club which serves Salisbury right."

The recent visit to Kuwait was part of Alhamad’s growing efforts to bring commercial growth to the club, while the non-league players were also able to soak up a completely different experience in a new environment.

View 4 Images Salisbury owner Ali Alhamad is a Kuwaiti businessman (Image: Salisbury FC)

‌



The players are said to have surprised the owner with how eager they were to embark on the trip, having reportedly agreed to go within an hour. As shown on the club’s official Instagram page, they were able to visit local restaurants and wear traditional clothing. They also met local schoolchildren, who were delighted to take pictures with them.

The links with Kuwait extend far beyond the pitch, with four of Salisbury’s sponsors being Kuwaiti, including the front of shirt sponsor. On Instagram the official Arabic account of Salisbury FC has more than 14,000 followers - only slightly less than their official English profile.

Alhamad said: "I would even go further than saying that Salisbury in Kuwait is bigger than many of the Premier League teams in the UK.

‌



4 View 4 Images Salisbury faced Kuwaiti giants Al Qadsia at their 22k-capacity stadium (Image: Salisbury Football Club) 4 View 4 Images The players met local Kuwaiti children (Image: Salisbury Football Club)

"So I am not exaggerating when I do say that it is a huge name in Kuwait but what's more important than the size is we are contributing a lot to the local community here in Kuwait and to the children and the future of the football in Kuwait.

‌



"Salisbury really is an integral part of opening those avenues and helping the youth here to be better in all the aspects we're looking for."

The owner went on to note that, while non-league is an unknown commodity in Kuwait, he hoped the match will have educated fans about how high the standard of football still is.

He added: "People are not properly educated in the fact that the non-league is actually a really high quality and that is also an indirect goal of mine with this match.

Article continues below

"We're here to show them, you're belittling playing the sixth tier of English football, the second step of the English non-league."

Sports.title: Man City charges: Appeal in question, Andy Burnham comments, Rui Pinto latest
Sports.content:
The latest news and opinion on the Manchester City charges after the club officially appealed the guilty verdict on all but one of the 115 charges levelled at them

Good morning and welcome to our live blog on Manchester City's extraordinary 115 charges case. City were found guilty of all charges except one relating to non-cooperation with the Premier League investigation.

It's now been over a week since the story of the guilty verdict first broke, and there have been a lot of developments since then. Earlier this week, the Premier League released a bombshell statement confirming the verdict.

The statement confirmed that the independent commission found that City had arranged 'sham contracts' and relied on 'sham agreements' to artificially inflate the club's revenues by £900million and reduce its costs.

City hit back with a strong statement of their own, reiterating that they have 'irrefutable evidence' that proves their innocence. They have now confirmed their appeal

The club released a short statement on Friday , revealing it had appealed the independent commission's guilty verdict and maintained their innocence, despite strong statements from the Premier League and FA. They claimed the ruling included 'clear material errors, of law, principle and fact and is unsafe.'

Prime Minister Andy Burnham has also waded into the mess, with reports claiming a punishment for Manchester City could impact the UAE's interest in future major investments in the United Kingdom. That follows on from the former Mayor of Manchester saying he would be "really concerned" to lose City's investors, after working closely with them on development projects in Manchester.

Sports.title: Record-breaking England win over Croatia is a message to rivals as Euro 2028 mission set
Sports.content:
Record-breaking England win over Croatia is a message to rivals as Euro 2028 mission set

CROATIA 0-7 ENGLAND: Thomas Tuchel's side made it back-to-back wins away from home as Harry Kane, Jude Bellingham, Anthony Gordon, Bukayo Saka and Morgan Rogers each got on the scoresheet

View 3 Images England ran riot in Rijeka (Image: Stringer/Anadolu via Getty Images)

This was the performance to finally stop the World Cup hangover. Nearly three months after THAT defeat to Argentina, England have finally moved on.

‌



‌



England were absolutely sensational in Rijeka with a stunning seven-goal demolition of Croatia to bring back the feel good factor again. Let’s be honest, a lot of England fans wanted Thomas Tuchel to be sacked after the World Cup semi final capitulation.

‌



It will still live long in the memory because England had victory in their grasp - and they blew it. And more specifically, the manager blew it.

‌



Tuchel gaslit the players and, for a while, it felt as if the manager would struggle to get them back onside as well. It was always going to take time to forgive and, while we might never forget, this was a performance to start a new chapter.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

‌



The scoreline should make the rest of Europe sit up and take notice. It is a clear sign that England are back on track under Tuchel. This was the sort of performance that makes you believe they can win the Euros.

Yes, yes, yes, we’ve heard it all before. But playing like this, they are a match for anyone. England were incredible. Yes, Croatia were absolutely awful but England were fast, slick and ruthless. They kept a clean sheet, had a strong midfield duo of Elliot Anderson and Alex Scott while the forward line was magnificent.

Jude Bellingham was the best player on the pitch by some distance as he scored and provided three assists. Bellingham is in the best form of his life. He was fresh, strong and brilliant at the World Cup and has, without doubt, the capacity to be England’s best-ever player.

‌



To get that sort of accolade, England will have to win a trophy but with Bellingham in their starting XI, they have got every chance of doing that. Harry Kane looks hungry and determined as he is scoring goals for fun. Two more pushed him to 89 and just 11 away from reaching 100. That landmark will keep him focused.

Was this the best performance in Thomas Tuchel's England reign? Have your say in the comments section.

View 3 Images Thomas Tuchel faced calls to be sacked after the World Cup (Image: Eddie Keogh - The FA/The FA via Getty Images)

‌



Tuchel joked after the Czech Republic game that it would take him just 13 games to get the 13 he needed. But he looks set to do it in double quick time. At 33, he is showing age is just a number. Anthony Gordon now looks a guaranteed starter for England and has taken his game to a new level since the World Cup and his move to Barcelona.

Gordon has real pace, looks way more dangerous and incisive and has added goals to his game. Three in as many appearances. Bukayo Saka looked so much sharper against Croatia and hopefully that performance will have done him the power of good.

The talent is there but he needs some confidence to really help his consistency for club and country. On his day, Saka is the best right winger for club and country. There is also a real depth because the likes of Morgan Rogers, Morgan Gibbs-White and Eberechi Eze come on and make a difference.

‌



Beyond Spain - and they are still the team to beat - there are not many countries with so much depth. Maybe France. But they have weaknesses in certain areas. But this was the performance - pass and move, movement and cohesion - to bring back the vibes which Tuchel created before and during the World Cup.

View 3 Images Jude Bellingham was outstanding with one goal and three assists (Image: Carl Recine/Getty Images)

Croatia went into the England game in 13th place in the FIFA rankings. They are live rankings so it moves quickly, but they are not your usual whipping boys. England destroyed them.

‌



During the World Cup, England fans had a spring in their step and a belief. That disappeared after the Argentina game and it felt like it would be a long way back for Tuchel.

The radio phone-ins were baying for blood and the shock jocks fuelled the calls for Tuchel to go. Once you lose the fans, you could argue there is no way back.

Article continues below

But this was back to the England that Tuchel promised. Fast, entertaining and thrilling. The shame of it was there was only 100 England fans in Rijeka.

What a farce from UEFA that England fans get punished for Croatia’s racism. What a joke. More should have been allowed in to watch what was definitely a big moment for England and a turning point for Tuchel.

Sports.title: 'I stood between Jurgen Klopp and Pep Guardiola - their behaviour said it all'
Sports.content:
'I stood between Jurgen Klopp and Pep Guardiola - their behaviour said it all'

Jurgen Klopp and Pep Guardiola were responsible for iconic Premier League battles between Liverpool and Manchester CIty

View 2 Images Jurgen Klopp and Pep Guardiola had an iconic rivalry (Image: Robbie Jay Barratt - AMA/Getty Images)

Former Premier League referee Graham Scott has given an insight into the dynamic between Pep Guardiola and Jurgen Klopp. The iconic managers oversaw a rivalry between Manchester City and Liverpool as both sides battled for the league title.

‌



‌



Their duels increasingly came to the fore as Klopp established the Reds as challengers, first taking the title race to the wire in the 2018/19 season. Guardiola’s City side narrowly finished first by a solitary point. Liverpool responded by storming to the Premier League trophy the following year.

‌



The two world-class managers added another chapter to their storied rivalry in the 2021/22 season, with City once again clinching top spot by just one point. Guardiola’s side celebrated a fourth consecutive league triumph as Klopp stepped down from his Liverpool post in 2024 but their title battles provided fans with lasting memories.

‌



The footballing world was recently rocked by City being found guilty of all financial charges brought by the Premier League, spanning from 2009 to 2018, though the club have appealed the verdict. While Guardiola has offered a supportive message to City fans, Liverpool icon Klopp refused to celebrate the outcome. Klopp’s response may not have surprised former Premier League official Scott, who sensed the pair’s mutual respect while working as a fourth official.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

“I actually found that when, I mean, the real elite managers, obviously Klopp and Pep absolutely were, that there was so much respect there,” Scott said on the Undr the Cosh podcast. “You could feel the respect between them. They were never actually going to go at each other.

‌



“When a big team is at home, somehow, the manager of a lower-placed team, they’re all big clubs, but the lower-placed team can be a little bit cowed and respectful. They’re quieter than they are when they’re at home and they’ve got their own environment. When they’re at home to the big clubs, they tend to be a bit more like that.

“Generally, Pep and Jurgen Klopp would have been so full of respect for each other that they wouldn’t have got into a proper bun fight.”

View 2 Images Graham Scott shared what he observed between Klopp and Guardiola as an official (Image: Robbie Jay Barratt - AMA/Getty Image)

‌



JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

Former Liverpool boss Klopp recently gave his thoughts on the City verdict. The new Germany manager offered a fresh stance, having previously vowed to celebrate if the Reds were retrospectively awarded titles.

He said: “Of course I've heard about that, but I haven't given it much thought. I can only wait and see. I have big respect for Pep Guardiola and City's style of football; they played fantastic football and were a top class opponent for us.”

‌



Despite City securing six Premier League crowns in seven seasons, Klopp holds a slight advantage in his overall head-to-head record with Guardiola. The two legendary coaches faced each other on 30 occasions in all competitions, with the 59-year-old earning 12 victories to his rival’s 11.

“I will sleep better [when Klopp goes]. The games we play before against Liverpool were almost a nightmare,” Guardiola said about Klopp choosing to leave Liverpool in 2024. “Of course he will be missed. It was a shock [to hear the news]. I felt when I heard it that a part of Man City … we will lose something. We cannot define our period here without him … without Liverpool. Impossible.

“They have been our biggest rivals. And personally he [Klopp] has been the best rival I ever had in my life – in Dortmund when I was in Bayern, then here. I think the Premier League are going to miss him – the charisma, the personality and especially the way his teams play.”

Sports.title: Djokovic creates more history with epic Zverev win at China Open
Sports.content:
Novak Djokovic rolled back the years to defeat French Open and US Open champion Alexander Zverev 4-6 6-4 6-4 to reach the semi-finals of the China Open on Sunday.

The 39-year-old Serbian created a new piece of tennis history with the best start in men's singles at a tour-level event in the Open Era as he moved to 32-0 in Beijing.

With his victory, Djokovic moved past Rafael Nadal for the best start at a single event, with Nadal having won his first 31 matches at the French Open.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of Djokovic's epic victory against Zverev in Beijing

Djokovic is a record six-time champion in Beijing and had won all 29 of his previous matches at the tournament before returning this year for the first time since 2015, when he defeated Nadal in the final to claim his sixth title.

"I had a terrible start. Two double faults at the beginning. It was quite cold and honestly, I didn't feel warmed up, but my fault," Djokovic said.

"I gave him an early break and then it was hard to come back in the first set. I had a couple of break points when he was serving for the set at 5-4, but didn't use them, but I kind of felt already from midway through the first set that I was starting to get a good rhythm, at least one my serve and on serve plus one."

Meeting for the first time in ​nearly 16 months, Djokovic struggled to contain the German's power in the early stages as Zverev claimed the ​opening set, but the Serb gradually ⁠worked his way into the ⁠match and refused to let his opponent pull away.

The turning point came late ‌in the second set when Djokovic broke at 5-4 to level the match, shifting the momentum in his ‌favour after a tightly contested battle.

With little separating the pair in the third, the Serbian struck again at 5-4 on the Zverev serve, securing the decisive break ⁠to seal victory.

The pair had not met ​since last year's French Open, where ​Djokovic won in four sets, and this encounter ​again highlighted the Serb's ability to deliver under ⁠pressure despite a season disrupted by physical issues.

With the win, Djokovic moved a step closer to a seventh ⁠China Open title and an elusive ​first trophy of the year, while denying Zverev ​another opportunity to strengthen his bid for the world No 1 ranking.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of Daniil Medvedev against Francisco Cerundolo at the China Open

Djokovic's next assignment will be a meeting with Daniil Medvedev, who earlier overcame Francisco Cerundolo 7-6 (7-4) 6-3.

He is just the third man in ATP history (since 1973) to earn a top-three win after turning 39 years of age, after Ken Rosewall and Jimmy Connors.

"To be honest, these are the kind of moments that I still play for, compete for," Djokovic said.

"The motivation is big obviously when you are feeling good and competing at par with the best players in the world, in front of 15,000 people of course. These are the kind of moments that define dreams, I think, of every tennis player. It's been a struggle this year, to be honest, for different reasons, but I'm still there, still grinding, still making the youngsters work for their money. I'm just glad to push it through."

Longest undefeated streaks in tennis tournaments (singles)

Monica Seles: 34-0 at the Australian Open



Novak Djokovic: 32-0 at China Open



Rafael Nadal: 31-0 at French Open



Zverev vs Djokovic: Tale of the Tape

'Djokovic came up with the answers'

Speaking on Sky Sports Tennis, former British No 1 Annabel Croft described the match as an "incredible contest".

"Some high-quality, absolutely fantastic tennis between two brilliant players. Why would you ever doubt Novak Djokovic even at the age of 39?

"The match got better and better as well, and had some different tactical shifts for Djokovic, who after the long physical points, I thought his legs were tiring, but he came back. He threw in some drop shots, he threw in some serve and volleys early in the second set and just changed things up with the pattern of play.

"Djokovic came up with the answers. It was on a knife edge right to the end but what a finish and what a treat for all those fans in Beijing."

At the Japan Open, top seed Carlos Alcaraz required only 83 minutes on court before he booked a place in the semi-finals after Denis Shapovalov retired when trailing 7-6 (7-3) 2-1.

Sports.title: Russell 'beyond disappointment' as Wolff 'massively annoyed' by engine failure
Sports.content:
Mercedes boss Toto Wolff said he was "massively annoyed" after the late unreliability that delivered a potentially knock-out blow to George Russell's title hopes in the Bahrain Grand Prix.

Mercedes had already been experiencing an unexpectedly difficult weekend on F1's return to Sepang with the team outqualified by both Red Bull and Ferrari despite bringing a long-awaited car upgrade.

Although Red Bull's Max Verstappen proved too fast in Sunday's chaotic, twice-delayed race, Mercedes were still on course for second with Kimi Antonelli and third with George Russell when, with five laps to go during the second Safety Car phase, the latter's car was stopped by a suspected power unit failure.

The retirement cost Russell 15 points and saw the British driver slip 84 points behind team-mate Antonelli in the title race with seven rounds left.

"I'm so massively annoyed, and not in a happy place," a frustrated Wolff told Sky Sports F1.

"First of all, we didn't have the speed that we were hoping to have before the weekend, so there's a lot of homework to be done in order to recover, which I'm sure we will.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Toto Wolff fumes after George Russell Power Unit failure at the Bahrain GP in Malaysia

"Then the race literally, if you consider the fight with Lewis [Hamilton] behind, went against us. We had such an advantage, one VSC, two Safety Cars, you couldn't be more unlucky.

"And to make things worse, a PU failure with a few laps to go until the end for George, which is terrible for his championship and not good at all for our constructors' points.

"So, as much as I love to be here when I look at the pure races, one of my worst experiences, to be honest."

Wolff acknowledged the solid race that Antonelli drove to come home in second but was left concerned by the latest incident of Mercedes unreliability. It was the third engine-related issue to force one of the W17s to retire from a race this season, and the team's fourth reliability-related DNF overall.

"He scored a few more points than Lewis behind him, and I'm happy because he did the job," added Wolff.

"But it's just the overarching topic, the DNFs, that could cost us dearly, also for the remaining seven races.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of the Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia at the Sepang International Circuit

"A championship is quickly turned around against you if you have a DNF, and that can't continue."

Mercedes introduced the first big upgrade onto their car since May's Canadian Grand Prix this weekend but that did not translate into the expected performance in lap time.

Wolff, though, is confident the team are already working through the problems.

"I think we have a good action plan," he said.

"James [Allison] is fully on top of it with his leadership team. That lifts my mood because I know with such a tremendous group of people - in the same way as that HPP [Mercedes High Performance Powertrains] are going to sort it out - but that gives me real relief for the moment to know that they are the best and they are going to find solutions.

"I think we will come back strong."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Kimi Antonelli and Max Verstappen go wheel to wheel on the restart before Verstappen slips through to take the lead

Russell: Title win now 'exceptionally unlikely' this year

For Russell, the late reliability heartache induced an unwanted feeling of deja vu.

"You've almost got to laugh. I'm beyond disappointment," he told Sky Sports F1.

"It's just so many times this season it's happened. It's a real shame, but we just keep on fighting. Just keep on trying to go.

"The podium looked very certain. Solid race, not amazing race, but solid race. Not the first time, so I'm pretty used to this feeling and these questions."

Russell had already admitted for several races that he needed to rely on good fortune to beat Antonelli to this year's world title having fallen over 60 points off the pace since the summer break.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player George Russell believes winning his first World Championship title this year is exceptionally unlikely after another DNF

The Briton had appeared to give himself a glimmer of hope with a dominating win last week on the streets of Baku, in a race his team-mate finished fifth after crashing in qualifying, but the 84-point deficit he now heads to Singapore trailing by represents the biggest of the season.

Asked if the reality of Sunday's DNF meant he now had to concede that his title ambitions were over for this year, Russell replied: "I don't need to say I think it's gone or whatever, but of course, it's exceptionally unlikely.

"That's just the reality I knew if I wanted to come back I needed luck on my side. Unfortunately, I've had luck not on my side.

"A three-point loss being behind Kimi turned into an 18-point loss. Of course, if the issue was on the other side it would have been an 18-point gain.

"It's a real shame, but that's just how it is."

Antonelli satisfied with 'maximum result' behind Verstappen

Although Antonelli was unable to go toe-to-toe with Verstappen for victory, Russell's late retirement means the 20-year-old Italian has clearly now moved a significant step closer to becoming the sport's youngest-ever world champion this year with a points lead back in excess of three race wins.

"Max has been very, very quick all weekend," said Antonelli, who has fallen 11s behind the Red Bull driver before the late Safety Car wiped out Verstappen's lead.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Kimi Antonelli says it hasn't been easy to understand Mercedes' upgrades after Max Verstappen's Red Bull won in Malaysia and George Russell suffered a late engine issue

"Red Bull, they've been doing a great job, and we've just been struggling more than previous races. I think we're still trying to understand the new package because also this track, with such a rough tarmac and high temperatures, it made our life more difficult.

"And probably next week in Singapore, we hopefully will have a better read on the package and also understanding what set-up needs to be run. But I think today, with the pace we had, P2 was the maximum we could have achieved."

Sports.title: 'I said it was wet!' - Hamilton reveals debate over disastrous Ferrari tyre choice
Sports.content:
Lewis Hamilton said he was pushing to start on intermediate tyres before the choice of a slick compound led to a disastrous beginning to the Bahrain Grand Prix for Ferrari.

Hamilton had qualified second on the grid at the Sepang International Circuit - with Malaysia hosting the race amid ongoing conflict in the Middle East - but his hopes of victory were blown as Ferrari chose to start both him and team-mate Charles Leclerc on soft slick tyres in the hope that the wet track would quickly dry out once the cars took to it.

Max Verstappen, who won the race for Red Bull from pole position, and third-placed starter Kimi Antonelli were among the 14 out of 22 drivers that started on the intermediate tyre, with that group gaining a huge advantage as the slick-tyre runners dropped more than a minute off the lead in the opening stages.

Hamilton ultimately produced a remarkable comeback, having at one stage dropped to 18th, to claim a podium in third, but was left with "mixed emotions" after the race over the decision made following the rain delay at the start of the race.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of the Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia at the Sepang International Circuit

The seven-time world champion confirmed to Sky Sports F1 that he believed he had the pace to compete for victory, and said: "It's a mixed emotion. On one side I'm really grateful to have got back to the podium.

"And then on the other side, with the debates that we were having in the background, to then see the covers come off the car ahead and the one behind, them on wets and us on slicks, and the track being so tricky and dangerous at the beginning, it was definitely… my heart sank, and I was like, 'that's the race over'."

Speaking in the post-race press conference, Hamilton added: "There was such a long wait and we were debating on what tyre to go on to. And I said, 'look, there was a lot of spray on the laps to the grid'.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Watch Hamilton drop to P15 as Mercedes claim the lead at the Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia

"And I went into the pit lane, I looked at the ground, I was like, 'it's still wet'. I went to the pit wall and I was like, 'it's still wet'. And they're like, 'yeah, but because it's been so long, it's definitely going to dry up real quick and maybe we're already in the crossover'.

"So, anyways, as a team, we ended up taking that soft and when we were at the end of the pit lane and these two took off their blankets and they're on inters, we were in trouble."

'Not going to the casino with those guys'

Hamilton then had to take matters into his own hands to avoid the initial mistake being compounded as the Ferrari pit wall attempted to call him in to move onto intermediate tyres on lap five.

Hamilton rejected the call, insisting that the team had made "a gamble" that they must now stick with in the hope the track dried out.

The decision paid off as the track drying and a Safety Car caused by Valtteri Bottas spinning his Cadillac into the gravel brought Hamilton back into play, before he began to surge through the field.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Hamilton recovers from P15 to podium places

Hamilton said: "We just had to stick with it. Like, we've made the decision and live with it. And I think then, through that, as everyone's overtaken me, they're like, 'we stop'.

"Because I know we've already made another 26 seconds. What's the difference from that with one minute 40 [seconds] or whatever I was down? So I was just, 'let's just wait it out for the track to dry'.

"And once it did, it felt good that I was catching people. The car felt great then after that. Really good pit stops from my guys in the garage and then good strategy. But for us to get back to the podium, I never thought that that was going to be the case. But, of course, I'm really grateful that we managed to get back here."

Asked about his choice to "gamble" and what he will say to ensure better decisions are made in future, Hamilton replied: "Yeah, not going to go to the casino with the guys."

Vasseur: Not easy to understand exact situation

Ferrari team principal Frederic Vasseur praised an overall "strong performance" from his team and bemoaned the difficulty of the decision they faced at the start.

Leclerc, who Ferrari did switch onto intermediates in the early stages, also produced a strong recovery drive to finish behind Hamilton in fourth.

"Overall, it's a good result. If you consider that we were 21 and 22 on lap one, it's a very strong performance," Vasseur said, exaggerating slightly how far back his drivers fell at the start.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player A chaotic formation lap halted the race start at the Bahrain GP

"The choice of the tyres, you can discuss at length. But I think 50 per cent of the cars went for slick, 50 for inters - from the pit lane you don't have the global picture of the track, and it's not easy to understand what is the exact situation, but, for sure, we were on the wrong side.

"Charles had contact on lap one and we had to pit to change the nose. To come back from this position to finish P3, P4, it's a strong result for the team.

"Now we have to do the next step, but I'm quite happy with the Sunday afternoon, at least after 4.30pm we did a good job."

Sports.title: Verstappen wins 'absolutely wild' Bahrain GP
Sports.content:
Max Verstappen overcame a chaotic, twice-delayed, rain-affected race to claim his first win of the 2026 season at the Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia, while Kimi Antonelli strengthened his title bid with second place as George Russell retired late on.

Formula 1's return to Sepang after a nine-year absence produced the most remarkable race day of the season, with heavy rain before the start finally delivering the campaign's first wet-weather action at its 16th round.

The start time was twice pushed back by delays before the 55 laps were twice disrupted by Safety Cars. Verstappen beat Antonelli to victory, while Lewis Hamilton stunningly fought back from dropping to 18th after a Ferrari tyre-strategy gamble backfired to claim third place.

"That is one of the craziest Formula 1 races I have ever seen," said Sky Sports F1's Martin Brundle after the chequered flag fell almost three and a half hours after the scheduled race-start time.

"That was absolutely wild."

Russell was running third behind Mercedes team-mate Antonelli with five laps to go but was forced to retire during the race's second Safety Car when a suspected power-unit failure stuck his car.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player George Russell is OUT with a Power Unit failure in the closing stages if the Bahrain GP in Malaysia.

A week after a dominant victory in Baku appeared to offer him a glimmer of hope in the championship race, Russell's deficit to Antonelli has widened to a season-high 84 points with only seven rounds remaining.

The Singapore Grand Prix - featuring the season's final Sprint - immediately follows live on Sky Sports F1 from this Friday.

Although he lost the lead to the Mercedes drivers from pole when the race eventually got under way, Verstappen fought back to reclaim first place and had built a lead of more than 10 seconds over Antonelli before the day's second Safety Car was deployed with nine laps left after Alex Albon's stranded Williams took time to recover.

But Verstappen, who had been dominant all weekend, made no mistakes when racing resumed and claimed his first win since last year's season-ending Abu Dhabi Grand Prix and the 72nd victory of his career.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Chaotic formation lap halts race start at Bahrain GP in Malaysia.

Hamilton had started alongside his old title rival on the front row and felt he could have challenged Verstappen for the win had Ferrari not made the decision to start on slick tyres on a drying but still-too-wet track.

That decision quickly proved flawed as Hamilton and Leclerc plummeted towards the back of the field and more than one minute off the lead behind those who had played it safer with by choosing the intermediates.

But a timely first Safety Car on lap nine closed the pack back up and, having crucially told the Ferrari pit wall to wait for conditions to come back towards them on the drying track rather than cutting their loses by pitting for intermediates - as team-mate Leclerc had done - Hamilton showed consistently blistering pace to work his way back up the order.

Hamilton overtook Red Bull's Isack Hadjar after the late restart to secure third and end Ferrari's five-race podium drought, with Leclerc also soon passing the Frenchman to take fourth following his own recovery drive after his additional early stop.

Bahrain GP Result: Top 10 1) Max Verstappen, Red Bull



2) Kimi Antonelli, Mercedes



3) Lewis Hamilton, Ferrari



4) Charles Leclerc, Ferrari



5) Isack Hadjar, Red Bull



6) Oscar Piastri, McLaren



7) Liam Lawson, Racing Bulls



8) Fernando Alonso, Aston Martin



9) Lando Norris, McLaren



10) Arvid Lindblad, Racing Bulls

Oscar Piastri finished sixth for McLaren, who had also gambled by fitting dry tyres to their cars for the start.

Lando Norris had been running close behind his team-mate in seventh but, just moments after Russell had pulled up to retire on inside of the pit straight under the Safety Car, misjudged his braking and slithered through the gravel at Turn One, dropping to ninth.

Liam Lawson drove strongly to seventh for Racing Bulls, backed up by team-mate Arvid Lindblad in 10th, while Fernando Alonso claimed a season-best eighth for Aston Martin to cap their best weekend of a troubled season so far.

How a remarkable race day unfolded on dramatic Sepang return

Tropical conditions are an ever-present threat in Malaysia, and after staying away for most of the race weekend, the rain finally arrived with a vengeance on Sunday - just as drivers prepared to head to the dummy grid, 40 minutes before the formation lap.

While the downpour was initially restricted to the pit-straight area of the track, the rain widened and worsened and, with strikes of thunder and lightning overhead adding to the increasingly gloomy scene, Race Control soon announced that the 8am BST scheduled start was to be delayed.

A 40-minute wait followed and, with conditions now steadily improving, cars were released back to the track from the pit lane for at least two exploratory formation laps behind the Safety Car with a view to starting the race.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Intense rain delays the start of the Bahrain GP in Malaysia.

But then the situation took an increasingly surreal turn, forcing another delay.

Halfway through the first controlled-speed lap behind the Safety Car, polesitter Verstappen reported that his Red Bull was struggling for power over the team radio.

Then second-placed Hamilton suffered more fundamental throttle problems in his Ferrari, sending him tumbling down the order as other cars moved past.

As the issues continued to spread, the field began to bunch up and split apart, with drivers battling software glitches in their highly complex 2026 power units. Hamilton eventually came to a halt on the backstraight before managing to get going again, while Ferrari-powered Haas and Cadillac cars also stopped briefly.

With all of this unfolding as the remaining runners approached the end of their second Safety Car lap, Race Control had little choice but to suspend the start procedure. Cars were sent back to the pit lane in a bizarre order, with stranded and struggling machinery adding to the chaos.

An even longer delay followed as the cars were painstakingly restored to their original grid positions and teams worked through a series of engine software tweaks issued by the FIA after what the governing body later said was an "unprecedented" glitch.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player SkyPad ANALYSIS of Lewis Hamilton's P15 to podium recovery drive!

Meanwhile, the rain had finally stopped, and the track was drying rapidly - but the big question remained: was it dry enough for slick tyres?

The answer soon became clear.

When a new race start time was confirmed, 13 of the 22 drivers - including both Ferraris and McLarens - gambled on slicks, while the rest, including Verstappen and both Mercedes, opted to stay on intermediates.

It was a gamble that quickly began to unravel. During the lap to the grid, the track proved too slippery for slicks, with Piastri and both Audis among the first to dive back into the pits for intermediates.

Then came the dramatic start. Verstappen, despite making the right tyre call, was immediately jumped by both Mercedes, with Kimi Antonelli leading George Russell into Turn One.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Verstappen takes lead from Antonelli on restart 🤯

But Verstappen still appeared quickest in the conditions and, having already passed Russell on lap six, the Red Bull driver was back at the front swiftly after the first Safety Car intervention - called on lap nine when Valtteri Bottas spun off in the Cadillac - when he overtook Antonelli through the first sequence of corners.

Russell followed through to take second away from Antonelli into turn four, but the Italian was back ahead of his team-mate and title rival by lap 21, by which time Verstappen was four seconds up the road.

That gap only widened thereafter until the late Safety Car bunched the field for the closing laps, but there was still no stopping Verstappen.

"It's a really nice one [win] after the year we've had and the progression we have made," said Verstappen.

"I'm incredibly proud of everyone. Just super nice to win here.

"It's incredible. To win our first race in our first year with our own power unit is pretty impressive."
