Sports.title: Wolff calls Mercedes’ Sepang race “one of my worst experiences” | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Mercedes team principal Toto Wolff was deeply unhappy with their performance in today’s race.

The two W17s hit the front of the field immediately after the start. However Andrea Kimi Antonelli fell to second place behind Max Verstappen at the finish and George Russell retired shortly before the finish.

Antonelli increased his championship lead over Russell and Lewis Hamilton, though the latter recovered from a significant delay at the start of the race to salvage third place.

“I’m so massively annoyed and not in a happy place,” Wolff told Sky.

Mercedes introduced a significant upgrade for their car this weekend but appeared to gain little from it. “First of all, we didn’t have the speed that we were hoping to have before the weekend,” said Wolff. “So there’s a lot of homework to be done in order to recover, which I’m sure we will.

“Then the race literally went – if you consider the fight with Lewis behind – went against us. We had such an advantage. Two VSCs or one VSC, two safety cars. I mean, you couldn’t be more unlucky.”

Russell’s retirement – his third in a grand prix this season – leaves him 84 points behind Antonelli in the championship fight.

“To make things worse, a PU failure with a few laps to go to the end with George which is terrible for his championship and not good at all for our constructor points,” Wolff continued. “So as much as I love to be here when I look at the pure races, one of my worst experiences to be honest.”

Sports.title: Verstappen takes first win of 2026 in Malaysia after power unit faults delay start | 2026 Bahrain GP in Malaysia report
Sports.content:
Max Verstappen claimed his first victory of 2026 in a heavily delayed race at the Sepang International Circuit.

Andrea Kimi Antonelli finished second and took another step towards clinching the championship as his team mate George Russell retired in the final laps.

The start was originally pushed back by 40 minutes when a downpour hit the track during the build-up. But once the cars headed out to begin their formation laps a software problem struck several of them, causing them to slow to a crawl.

Race control abandoned the attempt to start the race and summoned the cars back to the pits for an even longer delay while the FIA hurriedly distributed a software change to rectify the problem.

By the time the race began, almost an hour and 40 minutes after the original start time, the track had dried significantly again. However, to the surprise of many drivers, it had not dried sufficiently for slick tyres to be viable.

Those drivers who started on intermediates therefore benefited while their rivals on slicks sank to the tail of the pack. The Mercedes drivers rocketed from third and seventh on the grid to the front of the field on their intermediate tyres, while pole-winner Verstappen on the same compound fended off the fast-starting Liam Lawson.

Lewis Hamilton started on the front row alongside Verstappen but his soft slicks were overwhelmed by the conditions and he immediately fell out of the top 10. Within a few laps he was a minute adrift.

Advert | Become a RaceFans supporter and go ad-free

Verstappen drove past George Russell with little difficulty to take second place on lap six. He swiftly gained on Andrea Kimi Antonelli but had to delay his efforts to pass when Valtteri Bottas spun off at turn 14, triggering a Safety Car deployment.

The interruption came just in time for those still on slicks who were getting perilously close to being lapped. Antonelli led the field at the restart but Verstappen immediately picked him off to regain a lead he never looked like losing.

Russell also got ahead of his team mate at the restart, as Antonelli complained his power unit was clipping. Soon afterwards Antonelli told Mercedes “I have more pace”, and by lap 21 he proved his point by driving past his team mate, who did not try to resist him at turn four.

Antonelli was unable to make any impression on Verstappen. His efforts were not helped when he ran wide at the final corner and hit the pit lane entry bollard. He avoided any damage or a penalty, but lost time.

Hamilton opted not to pit during the first Safety Car period and found good grip from his soft tyres when the race resumed. He quickly worked his way past the midfielders, as well as the two McLarens, and began to close on Isack Hadjar’s fourth-placed Red Bull.

Advert | Become a RaceFans supporter and go ad-free

Red Bull brought Hadjar in for a fresh set of tyres, prompting a reaction from Ferrari and eventually those ahead of them. Now on the medium rubber, Hamilton could no longer get close enough to threaten the Red Bull.

The situation appeared set until Alexander Albon stopped with a gearbox problem on lap 43. The car was jammed in gear, causing a lengthy delay, during which the Safety Car was deployed and most drivers took the opportunity to pit again.

Disaster struck Russell shortly before the restart. His Mercedes came to a stop approaching turn one, the team reporting a power unit problem. Lando Norris, potentially distracted by the stopping Mercedes, almost ran into the back of his team mate. He drove through the gravel trap at turn one and lost several places.

Verstappen’s restart was much more successful than Antonelli’s and he kept the Mercedes at arm’s length until the finish. Hadjar’s car was no match for the soft-tyred Ferraris, however. First Hamilton, then Leclerc easily drove past him.

Oscar Piastri collected sixth, resisting Lawson in a late scrap between the pair. Fernando Alonso made excellent use of Honda’s upgraded power unit to hold off the recovering Norris and Arvid Lindblad took the final point for Racing Bulls.

Sports.title: Tyson Fury Calls Anthony Joshua A Usyk Warm-Up
Sports.content:
Tyson Fury is already looking past Anthony Joshua toward a trilogy bout with Oleksandr Usyk. He treats their December 11 Cardiff clash like tune-up work for a champion who already beat him twice.

That gives Joshua a golden opportunity to wreck everything. A loss completely ruins any market for another Usyk meeting, especially after Fury spent weeks dismissing Joshua as light work.

“I don’t have any intention of retiring after Joshua. I’m using this bum as a warm-up for Usyk,” Fury told Sky Sports.

Fury wants the Usyk trilogy in New York. He also points to his activity this year, including fights with Arslanbek Makhmudov and Mariusz Wach, as evidence that he will enter the Joshua bout ready.

Staying active helps Fury shake off ring rust, but Joshua brings threats none of those recent opponents offered. Joshua carries genuine power. Fury cannot afford to look past him or script future dates while dodging heavy artillery. A single defensive lapse ends all talk of a third Usyk clash instantly.

Joshua hits hard enough to test whether Fury still has elite reflexes over 12 rounds. Usyk is an entirely different animal. He relies on rapid footwork, awkward southpaw angles, non-stop punching. Fury could beat Joshua easily, but that does not solve the tactical problems that cost him against Usyk twice.

Winning in Cardiff gives Fury a huge name to brag about. It proves nothing about how a third fight with Usyk would turn out.

Fury’s trash talk is pure fight promotion. He degrades Joshua to sell the Cardiff gate while teasing an even bigger event down the line. His bravado sells tickets, but talk alone proves nothing about the reality inside his training camp.

If Fury wins, he could try to sell a big victory, but Usyk still holds two decisions over him. The champion would need serious motivation to face a boxer he conquered twice.

Sports.title: Ryan Garcia and Teofimo Lopez Managers Meet
Sports.content:
Teofimo Lopez’s manager Keith Connolly has met with Ryan Garcia’s manager Lupe Valencia and teased a “mega fight.” However, making Garcia–Lopez could require Teofimo to give up his WBA welterweight title, with Jack Catterall’s mandatory defense due.

The money fight can happen without two belts. The question is whether Teofimo can take his WBA championship into it while Catterall insists on getting his opportunity.

“Met up with Lupe Valencia today in San Diego for coffee,” Connolly wrote on Instagram, in a screenshot shared by Dan Rafael. “Boxing fans get ready Mega Fight coming.”

Connolly did not identify the matchup or announce an agreement, but meeting with Ryan’s manager and posting that caption gives Garcia–Lopez speculation something more substantial than another exchange of callouts.

It does nothing to settle the Catterall situation.

Teofimo and Catterall have until October 22 to negotiate a deal for their WBA title fight before the organization can move toward a purse bid. Catterall has made clear he won’t step aside, leaving Teofimo’s team with an obligation that a separate agreement with Ryan would not erase.

Unless the WBA grants permission for Garcia–Lopez to go ahead first, Teofimo could have to sacrifice his belt to pursue it. The deadline itself would not automatically strip him, but signing for Ryan would still leave the mandatory unresolved.

From a business perspective, losing the WBA title might be a price Teofimo is willing to pay. Ryan offers a commercially attractive opponent, and his WBC championship would give Teofimo another title to chase if the fight proceeds as a sanctioned defense.

That would change the promotion from a welterweight unification to a challenge for Ryan’s belt, without necessarily reducing the fighters’ interest in making it.

Connolly’s post suggests there is something to watch. Until the Catterall obligation is addressed, though, the two-title billing remains uncertain.

Sports.title: Eddie Hearn Offered To Stage Bentley–Hernandez In Ghana
Sports.content:
Denzel Bentley had an offer from Eddie Hearn to defend his WBO middleweight title against Yoenli Hernandez in Ghana before choosing Zuffa Boxing. Hearn revealed that Bentley requested a meeting with Matchroom, opening discussions about a route that would have included fulfilling his mandatory obligation.

Bentley instead signed a multi-fight Zuffa agreement and will face Shane Mosley Jr. on November 7 at London’s Copper Box Arena. That provides a different opponent and promotional future, although his WBO title situation remains unresolved.

“Denzel Bentley asked for a meeting with us,” Hearn told the post-fight press conference in Birmingham. “He was going to fight the mandatory in Ghana on our Ghana show. He chose to accept a little bit more money and … vacate the belt. … You blow the belt for nothing, for an extra 50 grand. I mean, it’s just madness.”

Hearn did not disclose Matchroom’s total offer or the terms beyond staging the Hernandez defense in Ghana. His £50,000 comparison therefore gives only part of the financial picture. A multi-fight agreement also requires Bentley to consider future purses, opponents and opportunities.

Hearn believes Bentley would beat Hernandez. I would favor the Cuban, whose pressure, combination punching and power could make the mandatory a demanding defense. Bentley would need to produce enough offense to discourage Hernandez while avoiding prolonged exchanges that suit the challenger.

That difference in how the fight is viewed helps explain the decision. Hearn sees a title Bentley should retain; Bentley may see a dangerous obligation alongside an alternative that offers greater financial security.

There is also a qualification to Hearn’s claim about vacating. Bentley has reportedly petitioned the WBO to approve Mosley as a voluntary defense, with his title at risk if permission is refused.

The Ghana proposal shows Bentley had another option. Whether it was the better one depends on more than the immediate purse difference Hearn described.

Sports.title: Andy Lee Reveals Ben Whittaker’s COVID Before Wallace Fight
Sports.content:
Ben Whittaker’s trainer, Andy Lee, said the unbeaten light heavyweight had COVID the week before facing Conor Wallace. Whittaker offered a different explanation for his difficult finish in Birmingham on Saturday: the fight had been “too easy,” and he lost concentration.

Dan Rafael reported Lee’s disclosure after Whittaker’s points victory, adding that both sides were discussing a rematch. The illness claim provides context for Whittaker’s performance, although how much it affected him remains unclear.

Whittaker sounded eager to face Wallace again rather than leave the late rounds as the final impression of their IBF eliminator.

“I think we should do it again and I’ll beat him down even better,” Whittaker said afterward. “If I’m honest, it was too easy. I took my eye off the ball a little bit and he come up with a good shot. That’s boxing. But what did I do? I dug it out and I won.”

That explanation reflects how comfortably Whittaker controlled much of the contest, but it understates the danger Wallace created late. Whittaker was hurt and had to survive an opponent who kept pressing after spending the earlier rounds struggling to reach him.

Lee’s account and Whittaker’s explanation can both be true. An interrupted preparation could have left him below his best, while lapses in concentration gave Wallace opportunities. However, the reported illness cannot tell us which mistakes came from his physical condition and which came from his decisions.

Calling the fight easy also gives Whittaker something to prove in a return bout. Winning the early rounds comfortably is only part of the job. Maintaining distance, following instructions and avoiding unnecessary exchanges become more valuable when an opponent starts landing.

A rematch would give Wallace another opportunity after his strong finish and allow Whittaker to show whether he can sustain his early control over 12 rounds.

For a fighter pursuing a world title, that would be useful evidence. Whittaker proved he could survive trouble on Saturday. Facing Wallace again would test whether he can prevent it.

Sports.title: Eddie Hearn Rejects Dana White’s Fury–Joshua Production Claim
Sports.content:
Eddie Hearn claims Sela has denied in writing that Dana White will handle television production for Tyson Fury vs. Anthony Joshua. However, Hearn remains open to negotiating White’s involvement and expects to meet him in Los Angeles next week.

That leaves White’s role unresolved. Hearn is challenging his claim to an existing production role while asking what Joshua and Matchroom would receive in exchange for agreeing to his participation.

“After that video, I spoke to Sela and I said, ‘Have you seen this video?’” Hearn told the post-fight press conference in Birmingham. “And they said, ‘Yes, and it is completely untrue.’ And they told me that in writing. … He cannot do that under the contract.”

That is Hearn’s account of Sela’s response and the contractual restrictions. The written communication and relevant contract wording were not presented during his remarks.

Hearn also acknowledged that Turki Alalshikh and Netflix want White involved. Their interest gives the proposed Los Angeles meeting a purpose: finding terms that satisfy Joshua’s side while allowing White a place in the event.

For Hearn, the question is what that participation adds. He asked what would be in it for Joshua and Matchroom, suggesting that permission could depend on a tangible benefit rather than simply accommodating the wishes of the other parties.

He conceded that the public dispute has helped the promotion. That creates an incentive to reach an agreement, particularly if an appearance by White generates more attention. Hearn wants freedom to question him directly if they share a press-conference stage.

The production claim nevertheless concerns a specific responsibility, beyond appearing at promotional events. Hearn’s remarks leave room for White to secure an agreed role later, but challenge the suggestion that television production is already his responsibility.

The proposed meeting could settle that difference. For now, Hearn’s position is that any involvement requires agreement from him and Joshua, with the benefits explained before they give their approval.

Sports.title: Whittaker Holds On To Beat Wallace
Sports.content:
Ben “The Surgeon” Whittaker survived a difficult finish to defeat Conor Wallace by unanimous decision over 12 rounds at Utilita Arena in Birmingham on Saturday. The Matchroom Boxing card, promoted by Eddie Hearn, aired on DAZN.

Whittaker (13-0-1, 9 KOs), the Tokyo Olympic silver medalist from Darlaston, retained his WBC Silver light heavyweight title and secured the IBF mandatory position. Wallace (17-2, 12 KOs), a Northern Irish-born southpaw based in Brisbane, made him work hard to protect the lead he had built.

Whittaker controlled most of the first nine rounds before Wallace hurt him with a lead left to the chin in the tenth. Wallace’s success made the closing rounds increasingly difficult, although Whittaker steadied himself in the 11th.

In the 12th, Wallace hurt Whittaker badly and pressed for a stoppage. Whittaker repeatedly held and struggled to stay upright, with referee Kieran McCann separating the fighters as the home boxer tried to reach the bell. Several falls prompted questions about whether knockdowns should have been called, but none were officially recorded.

Whittaker won by scores of 117-111, 116-112 and 115-113. His early work secured the victory, but Wallace’s late attack exposed defensive weaknesses that will need attention before a world title fight.

Bilal Fawaz stops Eithan James

British and Commonwealth junior middleweight champion Bilal Fawaz (13-1-1, 5 KOs), of London, retained his titles by stopping Northampton’s Eithan James (17-3) at 1:14 of the eighth round of their scheduled 12-round contest.

Fawaz dropped James with a right hand to the chin, then scored another knockdown before referee Ron Kearney ended the fight. James suffered his first stoppage defeat, while Fawaz collected the £5,000 knockout bonus Hearn had offered before the bout.

Hamza Uddin takes Sean Bruce’s British title

Walsall’s Hamza “The Great” Uddin (8-0, 5 KOs) stopped British flyweight champion Sean Bruce (8-3), of Leicester, at 2:49 of round eight to claim the British and vacant Commonwealth titles.

Uddin scored two knockdowns in the fifth round, with Bruce beating referee Victor Loughlin’s counts and continuing to fight. A third knockdown, from a body shot in the eighth, ended the contest. Loughlin waved it off immediately, bringing Bruce’s first British title defense to a close.

Ibraheem Sulaimaan retains English title

Birmingham southpaw Ibraheem “Spider” Sulaimaan defeated Sonny Hardy (12-1, 5 KOs), of Wickford, by unanimous decision after 10 competitive rounds to retain his English super featherweight title.

There was little between them after six rounds, and referee Chris Dean deducted a point from Sulaimaan in the seventh. The champion finished strongly over the final three rounds to secure scores of 97-93, 97-93 and 96-93.

Hardy’s work in the middle rounds made the contest closer than the cards suggested to some ringside observers, with several scoring it narrowly and others favoring the challenger.

Aaron Bowen wins Midlands Area title

Aaron Bowen (9-1, 6 KOs), of Coventry, took the Midlands Area super middleweight title from Klinton Baptiste (5-1) by unanimous decision over 10 rounds.

Bowen repeatedly landed lead right hands from the third round onward, leaving Baptiste’s left eye badly swollen and nearly closed. Baptiste absorbed sustained punishment but lasted the distance as Bowen pursued a stoppage.

The scores were 99-91, 99-92 and 98-92.

Odel Kamara wins professional debut

Liverpool junior middleweight Odel “King” Kamara (1-0, 1 KO), a 2025 World Boxing champion, stopped Greece’s Thodoris Ritzakis (5-6-1) at 2:53 of the third round of their scheduled four-round bout.

Kamara dropped Ritzakis in the opening round, with referee Ryan Churchill administering an eight-count. In the third, Kamara landed a short uppercut in close before Churchill called a halt, with Ritzakis bleeding from the nose.

The stoppage drew criticism from some ringside observers for being premature. Kamara also looked tired early and left openings while loading up on power shots, making this a successful debut with room for improvement.

Harley Burrows stops Matias Ezequiel Herrera

Harley “The Beast” Burrows (3-0, 2 KOs) stopped Argentina’s Matias Ezequiel Herrera (8-9-2, 5 KOs) at 1:24 of round two in a scheduled six-round middleweight contest.

Burrows pressured Herrera and mixed punches to the head and body. With Herrera pinned against the ropes under a sustained attack, referee Ryan Churchill stepped in to end the fight.

Adam Maca overwhelms Rogger Rivera

Adam “The Mac” Maca (7-0, 6 KOs), an Albanian super featherweight based in Brighton, stopped Peru’s Rogger Rivera (3-6, 2 KOs) at 2:56 of round two in their scheduled six-round bout.

Maca overwhelmed Rivera with power shots until referee Chris Dean intervened. The 19-year-old produced another quick finish, suggesting he is ready for opposition that can offer more resistance.

Paige Murray edges Linzi Buczynskyj

Paige “Perfect” Murray (5-0), of Leicester, defeated Bolton’s Linzi Buczynskyj (6-13) over four two-minute rounds.

Murray controlled the opening round but had a point deducted by referee Chris Dean in the second for repeatedly pulling down Buczynskyj’s head. She won the third and fourth rounds to secure a 38-37 decision.

David Diamante served as the ring announcer.

Sports.title: Ben Whittaker Beats Conor Wallace After Late Scare
Sports.content:
Ben Whittaker (13-0-1) survived a desperate final round to defeat Conor Wallace (17-2) by unanimous decision tonight at Utilita Arena in Birmingham, securing the IBF mandatory position at light heavyweight. Whittaker retained his WBC Silver title, but the closing minutes raised questions about his readiness for a world championship fight.

The judges scored it 117-111, 116-112 and 115-113. No knockdowns were officially recorded, although Whittaker’s falls during Wallace’s final-round assault became a disputed part of the result.

Whittaker controlled most of the first nine rounds, building the lead that ultimately protected his unbeaten record. Wallace could not collect enough rounds early, leaving the Northern Irish-born Australian southpaw needing a dramatic turnaround down the stretch.

He began finding more success in the tenth. With his feet planted, Wallace landed shots that disrupted Whittaker’s rhythm, while the home fighter complained to the referee. Whittaker recovered to take the 11th before Wallace launched his strongest attack in the final round.

Wallace hurt Whittaker and pursued the stoppage, forcing him to grab, stumble and wrestle his way through the remaining time. At one point, Whittaker tackled Wallace as he struggled to stay upright.

Bad Left Hook scored the round 10-8 for Wallace and argued that two or three knockdowns could have been called. Those calls never came, and Whittaker reached the bell with his earlier work enough to secure the decision.

The concern for Whittaker is how little control he had once Wallace hurt him. Holding bought him time, but he struggled to regain his balance or produce enough offense to discourage the pursuit. A stronger finisher could make that escape much harder.

Wallace deserves credit for continuing to press after losing much of the early action. His late surge fell short, but it exposed vulnerabilities that Whittaker and trainer Andy Lee need to address before pursuing the IBF belt held by Dmitry Bivol.

Sports.title: Ben Whittaker vs. Conor Wallace Live Results and Fight Updates
Sports.content:
Ben Whittaker (13-0-1) survived a punishing final round to defeat Conor Wallace (17-2) by unanimous decision, retaining his WBC Silver light heavyweight title and securing the IBF mandatory position for Dmitry Bivol’s belt. The scores were 117-111, 116-112 and 115-113 after 12 rounds in Birmingham.

Whittaker controlled much of the early action, but Wallace hurt him badly in the 12th, leaving him grabbing and struggling to stay upright. No knockdowns were officially scored, although several falls drew criticism over whether Wallace should have received knockdown calls during his late push for a stoppage.

Undercard results

Odel Kamara (1-0) stopped Thodoris Ritzakis (5-6-1) in round three of his professional debut tonight in Birmingham, landing a short uppercut before the referee waved it off. Eddie Hearn rates the 22-year-old junior middleweight highly, but Kamara looked wild swinging for the fences and took unnecessary punches from his overmatched opponent.

The stoppage drew ringside criticism for being premature, and Kamara’s power looked less impressive than the result suggests. At 5’8″, he could be better suited to welterweight, although his stocky build leaves a question over whether he can comfortably make 147 pounds.

Hamza Uddin (8-0) stopped Sean Bruce (8-3) at 2:49 of round eight to capture the British flyweight title and vacant Commonwealth belt at Utilita Arena in Birmingham. The 23-year-old from Walsall scored three knockdowns, finishing Bruce with a body shot near the ropes.

Bruce doubled over and went down, prompting referee Victor Loughlin to wave off the contest without starting a count. Uddin picked apart the champion with accurate punching, producing an impressive performance in his first British title fight. Bruce lost his belt in his first defense and could not withstand Uddin’s precision or sustained attack.

Bilal Fawaz (13-1-1) retained his British and Commonwealth junior middleweight titles by stopping Eithan James (17-3) at 1:14 of round eight in Birmingham. A heavy right hand sent James to the canvas near the ropes, and another knockdown brought the referee’s intervention.

The 38-year-old Fawaz delivered the finish just as commentary suggested he was beginning to feel the pace. James suffered his first stoppage defeat, while Fawaz earned the £5,000 knockout bonus Eddie Hearn had offered before the fight.

English super featherweight champion Ibraheem Sulaimaan retained his title with a hard-fought unanimous decision over Sonny Hardy after 10 rounds at Utilita Arena Birmingham. The scores were 97–93, 97–93 and 96–93, moving the Birmingham southpaw to 12–0 and handing Hardy his first defeat at 12–1.

Sulaimaan started quickly, but Hardy pushed him through a difficult stretch in the middle rounds, knocking his gumshield out during one exchange. The champion also had a point deducted before recovering his momentum in the eighth and finishing strongly over the final three rounds. Several ringside observers scored the contest considerably closer than the official judges, with some favoring Hardy.

Aaron Bowen (9-1) captured the Midlands Area super middleweight title with a unanimous decision over Klinton Baptiste (5-1) at Utilita Arena in Birmingham. The scores were 99-91, 99-92 and 98-92 after 10 rounds.

Bowen controlled the fight, catching Baptiste with clean right hands against the ropes and pressing for a stoppage. Baptiste fought with one eye closed for roughly half the contest but lasted the distance without a reported knockdown.

The punishment prompted ringside criticism that his corner should have intervened, although his durability kept Bowen from securing the finish. Bowen earned a clear victory, while Baptiste’s resistance made the closing rounds harder than the wide scores might suggest. Baptiste looked gone on a couple of occasions, but surprisingly, he stayed in there.

Super featherweight Adam Maca (7-0, 6 KOs) stopped Rogger Rivera (3-6, 2 KOs) at 2:56 of round two in their scheduled six-round contest. The 19-year-old unloaded with power shots until referee Chris Dean stepped in to end the fight. It was Maca’s sixth stoppage in seven professional outings.

The teenager produced another impressive finish, but he is making this level of opposition look too easy. Rivera offered little opportunity to assess how Maca handles resistance or adjusts when his power alone cannot settle a fight. Maca looks ready for better opposition that can extend him and give him more to solve.

Harley Burrows stopped Matias Ezequiel Herrera at 1:24 of round two in their scheduled six-round middleweight contest on the Ben Whittaker–Conor Wallace undercard in Birmingham. The 20-year-old southpaw pressured Herrera from the opening bell, mixing punches to the head and body.

Burrows trapped the Argentine against the ropes in the second round and punched through his high guard until referee Ryan Churchill intervened. Herrera had not been knocked down before the stoppage, which drew some ringside criticism for being slightly early. Burrows’ attack was wild at times, but his sustained pressure kept Herrera struggling to find room to respond.

The DAZN broadcast starts at 2:00 p.m. ET / 7:00 p.m. UK, with a subscription required. That is the card’s start time; Whittaker and Wallace fight later in the evening.

Whittaker has a chance to move within reach of a world title shot, but he must first get through Wallace over the scheduled 12 rounds. British title fights involving Sean Bruce and Bilal Fawaz feature on the undercard.

Live results — upcoming

Sean Bruce vs Hamza Uddin: Flyweights, 12 rounds, for Bruce’s British title and the vacant Commonwealth title.

Bilal Fawaz vs Eithan James: Junior middleweights, 12 rounds, for Fawaz’s British title.

Odel Kamara vs Thodoris Ritzakis: Middleweights, four rounds.

Ghana News.title: Hawa Koomson pledges experienced and mature leadership of NPP women’s wing
Ghana News.content:
Newly elected Women’s Organiser of the New Patriotic Party (NPP), Mavis Hawa Koomson, says she will bring experience and maturity to the position as she assumes responsibility for the party’s women’s wing.

Madam Koomson secured victory in the NPP’s national elections after defeating her main contender, Hajia Safia Mohammed, who conceded defeat and congratulated her on the outcome.

She polled 783 votes, while her only contender polled 429 votes.

Speaking to the media after her election, she thanked her supporters and the party’s election committee for their roles in the electoral process.

“I want to thank every person who supported me till today. Their efforts have resulted in this victory,” she said.

She also expressed appreciation to the election committee and other key members of the party for their contributions to the successful conduct of the elections.

When asked what kind of Women’s Organiser she intended to be, she said she would draw on her experience and maturity to lead the party’s women’s wing.

“A woman with experience and maturity,” she said.

Ghana News.title: Young woman found dead at Kasoa Peace Town
Ghana News.content:
A woman believed to be in her twenties was found dead at Akweley Peace Town in Kasoa of the Central Region on Sunday morning, October 4, 2026.

According to residents, they discovered her body suspended from a tree.

Police have since taken the body to a mortuary, with investigations expected to establish the cause of death and the circumstances surrounding the incident.

Some residents said they heard screams around midnight but did not investigate the sounds at the time.

They suggested that the woman might have travelled to the community with people attending a one-week funeral observance. This account has not been confirmed.

Residents also raised concerns about a possible sexual assault and alleged that the scene might have been staged to suggest suicide. These claims remain unverified, and the cause of death has yet to be established.

Ghana News.title: Mahama urges African governments to treat healthcare as an investment, not budget cost
Ghana News.content:
President John Dramani Mahama

President John Mahama has called for a major rethink of healthcare financing in Africa, urging governments and investors to treat the sector as an economic investment rather than merely a cost to national budgets.

According to President Mahama, increased investment in healthcare can drive economic growth, create jobs, strengthen human capital and support macroeconomic stability across the continent.

He made the call at the Health Plenary of the Alamein Africa Forum in Egypt.

President Mahama said African finance ministers and global investors have for years treated healthcare as a social expenditure that should be funded only when resources are available.

“African finance ministers and global investors have made a fundamental error. They have treated health as a line-item cost and a social expenditure in their budgets to be funded only when there is money left over,” he said.

He urged stakeholders to move away from that approach, arguing that healthcare has significant economic potential.

“Health is not a charitable cost. It is an investable high-growth economic sector. It drives human capital, manufacturing, job creation, and macroeconomic stability,” President Mahama stated.

He cited research by the Copenhagen Consensus, which he said found that a targeted package of basic emergency, maternal and newborn care could generate $87 in economic and social returns for every dollar invested.

He also referenced the Lancet Commission, saying declining mortality rates accounted for nearly a quarter of total income growth in developing economies in the early 2000s.

“And so investing in healthcare strengthens our balance sheets rather than depleting resources,” he added.

Africa’s pharmaceutical gap

President Mahama also drew attention to Africa’s heavy dependence on imported medicines and vaccines, describing the situation as both a challenge and an opportunity for domestic investment.

“Africa imports over 70% of its pharmaceuticals and nearly 99% of its vaccines. Each year tens of billions of dollars leave African economies to purchase medicines and vaccines from abroad,” he said.

He noted that the situation is being compounded by declining traditional donor assistance, citing OECD projections that health aid could fall by between 29% and 46% compared with 2024 levels.

President Mahama said the decline in donor support should prompt African countries to mobilise domestic private capital and strengthen local pharmaceutical production.

“The situation presents not only a crisis but also a significant market opportunity for domestic private capital,” he said.

He identified Africa’s growing population as one of the key factors supporting the business case for local pharmaceutical manufacturing.

According to him, Africa’s population is projected to reach 2.5 billion by 2050, while demand for essential medicines, chronic disease management and biologics continues to grow.

President Mahama said African countries must therefore position healthcare and pharmaceutical manufacturing as strategic sectors capable of retaining more economic value on the continent while creating jobs and strengthening health security.

Ghana News.title: Bawumia congratulates John Boadu and new NPP executives, pledges support ahead of 2028
Ghana News.content:
The Leader and Presidential Candidate of the New Patriotic Party (NPP), Dr Mahamudu Bawumia, has congratulated the party’s newly elected National Executives following Saturday’s national executive elections in Kumasi.

In a statement issued on Sunday, October 4, and signed by the Communications Directorate of his office, Dr Bawumia said the election marked the completion of the party’s reorganisation ahead of the 2028 presidential election.

He said the process was conducted in an atmosphere of peace and transparency, adding that the results reflected the will of the party’s delegates.

“The outcome, therefore, reflects the wishes of the delegates of the New Patriotic Party,” the statement said.

Dr Bawumia said the party’s rank and file now expected the John Boadu-led executive to begin preparations for the 2028 elections.

He pledged to provide the necessary support to the new leadership to build an inclusive system capable of harnessing the talents and experience of members across the party.

“In victory or in defeat, no talent should be left out in the 2028 campaign,” he said.

His comments come after he separately assured aspirants who contested the national executive elections that their involvement in the party would not end with the conclusion of the internal contest.

The NPP held its National Delegates Conference at the Baba Yara Sports Stadium in Kumasi on Saturday, October 3, electing a new team of national executives.

John Boadu was elected National Chairman after securing 2,888 votes, defeating Boakye Kyeremateng Agyarko, who polled 2,408 votes. Former National Chairman Paul Afoko obtained 790 votes, while Sammy Crabbe received 41 votes.

Justin Frimpong Kodua retained the position of General Secretary with 4,486 votes.

Other elected executives include Kojo Fosu Boadu as First Vice Chairman, Henry Nana Boakye as Second Vice Chairman, Nana Akomea as Third Vice Chairman, Daniel Nii Kwartei Titus-Glover as National Organiser and Alfred Kwadwo Thompson as National Treasurer.

The new executives are expected to lead the party’s organisational activities over the next four years as it prepares for the 2028 general elections.

Ghana News.title: Prof. Mike Oquaye recounts how he blocked the Special Prosecutor’s attempt to arrest Bawku Central MP
Ghana News.content:
Hon Mahama Ayariga

Former Speaker of Parliament, Prof. Aaron Mike Oquaye, has revealed how he intervened to stop the then Special Prosecutor from pursuing the arrest of Bawku Central MP, Mahama Ayariga, during his tenure as Speaker.

Prof. Oquaye said his intervention was not politically motivated but was aimed at protecting Mr Ayariga’s constitutional rights and upholding parliamentary privilege.

“Honourable Ayariga was wanted by the previous Special Prosecutor during my tenure. I was very, very, very active in stopping the attempts because, you see, it is not a matter of NPP or NDC.

"I was very much insistent on protecting his rights. So much so that I invited the Special Prosecutor for an open meeting, so that we all follow the tenets of the Constitution,” he explained.

He said he further documented his position in a letter to ensure that the matter was formally placed on record.

“I supported it with a letter for the records. It’s there. And Ayariga would not be abused. His rights would not be abused,” Prof. Oquaye stated.

Prof. Oquaye said his position was rooted in the constitutional principle of separation of powers and the protection of Parliament from undue interference by the Executive.

“If you read my ruling... I traced the history of parliamentary privilege, including the infractions that took place even in England, and how it came to be strengthened, and the purpose behind it,” he said.

Prof. Oquaye maintained that parliamentary privilege must be respected if the constitutional separation of powers is to be meaningful. “You cannot have separation of powers in the Constitution if the Executive takes steps to shut up the opposition, and that harassment is not good,” he added.

Ghana News.title: Make health sovereignty a priority for Africa – Mahama
Ghana News.content:
President John Dramani Mahama has urged African leaders to make health sovereignty a priority for their country as part of a broader strategy for the continent to achieve health sovereignty.

He said that it was about time that Africa stopped treating health as a charitable cost and positioned it as an investable, high-growth economic sector.

Speaking at the Alamein Africa Forum on Saturday (Oct 3, 2026) at El Alamein in Egypt, President Mahama added that Africa’s goal must be the health sovereignty and economic and fiscal security of its 1.4 billion people.

"Our goal is health sovereignty, and economic and fiscal security of 1.4 billion African people. For decades, African finance ministers and global investors have made a fundamental error. They have treated health as a line-item cost and a social expenditure in their budgets to be funded only when there is money left over.

"Today, at the Alamein Africa Forum, we are moving beyond that outdated perspective. Health is not a charitable cost. It is an investable, high-growth economic sector," he said.

Health investment

President Mahama underscored the need to invest in health, stating that it drives human capital, manufacturing, job creation and macroeconomic stability while citing global evidence.

"The arithmetic is indisputable. The Copenhagen Consensus showed that a targeted package of basic emergency maternal and newborn care can yield $87 in economic and social returns for every single dollar that is invested. The Lancet Commission established that falling mortality rates accounted for nearly a quarter of total income growth in developing economies in the early 2000s," he said.

He pointed to Africa's dangerous dependency, stating that the continent imports over 70 per cent of its pharmaceuticals and nearly 99 per cent of its vaccines, with tens of billions of dollars leaving African economies annually to purchase medicines abroad.

President Mahama indicated that traditional donor assistance is declining, with OECD projections indicating health aid will decrease by 29 to 46 per cent compared to 2024 levels.

He, however, indicated that governments cannot fund the transition alone and called for private capital, industrial developers, commercial banks and sovereign funds to participate, through initiatives like Business United for Mothers, Babies, and Youth, championed by President Samia Suluhu Hassan of Tanzania.

He urged African leaders and stakeholders to stop treating health as an expense item in their budgets, and build the factories, integrate supply chains, fund innovators, and secure the future of their citizens.

AfCFTA

The President affirmed that the argument for the development of a vibrant local pharmaceutical manufacturing rested on four pillars, including a captive market set to grow to 2.5 billion people by 2050, saving foreign exchange through import substitution, and the single continental market offered by the African Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA).

"The African Continental Free Trade Area and African manufacturing plants do not serve a single country of 10 or 30 million. It serves a single unified market of 1.4 billion consumers," he said.

President Mahama cited the Africa CDC's first pooled tender for maternal and child health products, which by aggregating demand achieved price reductions of more than 30 per cent while ensuring African manufacturers won 50 per cent of product lines.

He said health sovereignty means health security for citizens, high-value jobs and affordability, noting Africa's structural paradox where nearly one million trained healthcare professionals and science graduates remain unemployed despite a shortage of 6 million health workers, according to the WHO.

Continental initiatives

President Mahama pointed to Egypt's elimination of hepatitis C, which dropped prevalence from 10 percent to under 0.5 per cent by negotiating technology transfer and building domestic production through champions like Eva Pharma, and treating 4 million citizens locally, making Egypt the first country recognised by WHO on the path to eliminating hepatitis C.

He also cited Nigeria's African Medical Centre of Excellence in Abuja, pioneered by Afreximbank and King's College Hospital, tackling the $6 billion annual loss to outbound medical tourism.

On Ghana, he said government is implementing the Accra Reset by expanding the National Health Insurance Scheme, introducing the free primary health care programme, establishing the Ghana Medical Trust Fund (MahamaCares), and empowering the Food and Drugs Authority and the National Vaccine Institute to transition Ghana from a consumer to a producer of health products.

To scale up such successes, he announced a new continental enabler.

"Today, we present the Health Investment and National Gateway, acronym HINGE, Enabler. Developed with the African Medicines Agency, Institut Pasteur, Afrochampions, HINGE will become a digital platform that streamlines regulations, clinical validation, and commercialisation into a unified process for innovators and investors," he said.

He added that through the Accra Reset Presidential Council, dedicated task forces and reformed inter-ministerial observatories will track capital flows, enforce policy commitments and dismantle non-tariff barriers across regional value chains.

World.title: Trump pleads not guilty to 34 felony counts
World.content:
News outlets will not be allowed to broadcast former President Donald Trump’s arraignment on Tuesday in a New York state court, a judge said Monday night, but he will allow some photographers to take pictures in the courtroom before the proceedings formally begin.

Acting New York Supreme Court Judge Juan Merchan rejected the request by several media organizations, including CNN, for permission to broadcast the historic proceedings. Trump’s arraignment — like most arraignments in the Manhattan courthouse — is a public proceeding, but news cameras are not usually allowed to broadcast from inside the courtroom.

However, the judge is allowing five pool photographers to take still photos at the beginning of the proceedings “until such time as they are directed to vacate the jury box by court personnel.”

Earlier on Monday, Trump’s lawyers urged the judge to reject the media’s request for live cameras in the courtroom. The Manhattan District Attorney’s office told the judge they didn’t have a position.

The media outlets that tried to get cameras into the courtroom argued that “the gravity of this proceeding … and, consequently, the need for the broadest possible public access, cannot be overstated.”

Trump is now in Manhattan ahead of the arraignment. A grand jury indicted the former president last week.

The arraignment is also expected to bring the unsealing of the criminal charges against Trump, which have not yet been seen by his lawyers or the public.

The indictment stems from Manhattan District Attorney Alvin Bragg’s investigation into hush-money payments, made during the 2016 presidential campaign, to women who claimed they had extramarital affairs with Trump, which he denies.

Trump denies all wrongdoing and his lawyers said last week that they’ll fight to get the charges dropped.

A Ukrainian tank is seen near the frontline area amid the Russia-Ukraine war, in Bakhmut, Ukraine, on April 02. (Muhammed Enes Yildirim/Anadolu Agency/Getty Images)

The Ukrainian military has reported little change to the front lines but heavy fire from Russian forces at various parts of the front line in the Donetsk region.

The General Staff said that more than 45 enemy attacks had been repelled over the past day, with the focus on Lyman, Bakhmut, Avdiivka and Mariinka.

It said there were 17 air strikes and more than 20 strikes by multiple launch rocket systems.

“In the Bakhmut direction, the enemy is trying to take full control over the city of Bakhmut and continues to storm it,” the General Staff said.

West of the city, Ukrainian defense forces repelled about 20 enemy attacks, according to the General Staff.

Oleksandr Syrskyi, commander of Ukrainian Land Forces, posted on Telegram that in Bakhmut he had met with “soldiers and commanders who destroyed the myth of invincibility of the Wagner fighters and Russian paratroopers.”

“The enemy is weakening and trying to cover up its failures with new fakes about the capture of Bakhmut,” Syrskyi said.

Syrskyi referenced the possibility of a future counter-offensive, saying that “the forward movement of our entire army depends on what every soldier is doing right now on their section of the front.”

Some of the most intense fighting is to the northwest and west of the city of Donetsk – as the Russians continue months-long efforts to dislodge Ukrainian defenses in Avdiivka and Mariinka. The General Staff said that some 20 assaults had been repelled.

“There are also some operational successes of our military in the Donetsk area. Our military have taken some positions. They have taken a more strategic and favourable position,” said Oleksii Dmytrashkivskyi, spokesperson for the military in that zone.

He also noted that Russian special forces had been introduced in the area.

“The enemy is trying to attack our positions between Avdiivka and Marinka. These attempts do not stop. It should be noted that the enemy has suffered quite significant losses,” Dmytrashkivskyi said.

He also claimed that the Russians “don’t have the same amount of equipment and, as they themselves say, they are on a ‘diet’ of ammunition for assaults.”

Social media video showed both sides engaged in heavy fire in the Avdiivka area, which the Russians have surrounded on three sides.

Denis Pushilin, the leader of the self-declared Donetsk People’s Republic, claimed that Russian forces were still advancing in the Avdiivka direction.

“It is still premature to speak of encirclement, but the situation is being created, if not critical, then extremely difficult for the enemy… After clearing Kamianka, our units are moving further. There are difficulties both with the terrain, which must also be overcome, and there are also similarities with weather conditions. But these difficulties are mutual — both for the enemy and for us,” Pushilin said.

World.title: Suspected Chinese spy balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing
World.content:
Washington —

The Chinese spy balloon that transited the US earlier this year was able to capture imagery and collect some signals intelligence from US military sites, a source familiar with the matter tells CNN.

The balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing in real time, the source said, and the US government still does not know for sure whether the Chinese government could wipe the balloon’s data as it received it. That raises questions about whether there is intelligence the balloon was able to gather that the US still doesn’t know about.

Still, the intelligence community has not been overly concerned about the information the balloon was able to gather, the person said, because it is not much more sophisticated than what Chinese satellites are able to glean as they orbit over similar locations.

A US intelligence official told CNN on Monday that “although analysis of the wreckage of the High Altitude Balloon remains ongoing, thus far, its flight over the United States does not appear to have provided critical new insights to the People’s Republic of China.”

The US also knew what the balloon’s path would be and was able to protect sensitive sites and censor some signals before the balloon was able to pick them up, officials have said.

As CNN has reported, the US intelligence community last year developed a method of tracking what it says is a fleet of these Chinese balloons operating across the globe, controlled by the Chinese military.

The FBI is still examining the balloon, but so far officials have been able to glean additional information about how the device worked, including the algorithms used for the balloon’s software and how it is powered and designed.

CNN has reached out to the National Security Council at the White House and the Pentagon for comment. NBC was first to report on the new intelligence.

Video Ad Feedback Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33 • Source: CNN Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33

The balloon first crossed into US airspace over Alaska in late January before passing through Canada and down into Montana, where it hovered for a few days, leading the US to believe it was trying to surveil sensitive military sites, like Malmstrom Air Force Base in Montana. It was eventually shot down by the US off the East Coast on February 4, and the incident further escalated tensions between Washington and Beijing, including the postponement of a diplomatic visit by US Secretary of State Antony Blinken to China.

A senior State Department official said in February that, as the balloon floated across the US, it “was capable of conducting signals intelligence collection operations.”

Gen. Glen VanHerck, the commander of US Northern Command and NORAD, said at the time that the US “did not assess” that the balloon “presented a significant collection hazard beyond what already exists in actionable technical means from the Chinese.”

The surveillance program, which includes a number of similar balloons, is in part run out of the small Chinese province of Hainan, officials told CNN. The US does not know the precise size of the fleet of Chinese surveillance balloons, but sources tell CNN that the program has conducted at least two dozen missions over at least five continents in recent years.

Roughly half a dozen of those flights have been within US airspace, although not necessarily over US territory, according to one official familiar with the intelligence.

China has maintained that the balloon was actually just a weather balloon thrown off course, and the US has been assessing the possibility that it was not deliberately maneuvered into the continental US by the Chinese government, CNN has reported.

Still, China did maintain some ability to maneuver the balloon, officials believe. And once the balloon was over Montana, China appeared to take advantage of its position to loiter over sensitive sites and try to collect intelligence.

This story has been updated with additional reporting.

World.title: Beijing promised to 'fight back' over Taiwan leader's US visit. But this time it has more to lose
World.content:
Hong Kong —

An anticipated meeting between Taiwan’s President Tsai Ing-wen and US House Speaker Kevin McCarthy in California this week has sparked concerns of a repeat of the pressure campaign China launched last year when then-Speaker Nancy Pelosi visited Taipei.

At that time, Beijing encircled the island democracy with unprecedented military drills – firing multiple missiles into its surrounding waters and sending dozens of warplanes speeding across a sensitive median line dividing the Taiwan Strait.

It also cut off contact with the United States over a number of issues from military matters to combating climate change, in retaliation for what it viewed as a violation of its sovereignty.

This time, Beijing has already threatened to “resolutely fight back” if a Tsai-McCarthy meeting goes ahead.

Video Ad Feedback See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32 • Source: CNN See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32

It also slammed Washington for allowing Tsai to stopover in the US while en route to and from official visits in Central America, warning it could lead to “serious” confrontation between the two powers.

A defiant Tsai staked out her own ground, pledging as she took off on her 10-day trip not to let “external pressure” stop Taiwan from connecting with the world and like-minded democracies.

But the optics of the meeting, taking place in California and not Taiwan, and its timing – at a particularly thorny moment in China’s foreign relations and ahead of a presidential election in Taiwan that could reset the tone of its relationship with Beijing – may see Beijing tread more carefully this time, or at least not escalate further, analysts say.

“This puts the burden on China not to overreact, because any overreaction is only going to push China further away from the world,” said Yun Sun, director of the China Program at the Stimson Center think tank in Washington.

That doesn’t mean, however, that Beijing won’t be closely watching Tsai’s movements as it calibrates its response – and decides how much military might to flex over her meeting with an American lawmaker on American soil.

The opacity of China’s system – and the potential for competing interests within its vast bureaucracy – also make it difficult to accurately predict its response.

“Every time Taiwan does anything that China doesn’t like, the Chinese react with their own military coercion,” Sun said. But in the current situation, “they have to consider the consequences of overreaction,” she added.

House Speaker Kevin McCarthy talks to reporters at the Capitol in Washington on March 24, 2023. J. Scott Applewhite/AP

Rising pressure

The expected meeting, which McCarthy’s office announced earlier this week would take place on Wednesday, also comes at a precarious moment in US-China relations.

Washington and Beijing are struggling to stabilize their communication amid flaring tensions over issues from a downed suspected Chinese surveillance balloon to semiconductor supply chains – raising the stakes of potential damage to that relationship if Beijing lashes out as it did when Tsai met Pelosi.

Taiwan is still feeling the fallout of that response last August, with Chinese military forces now regularly making incursions over what had previously been an informal but largely respected border of control between Beijing and Taipei in the Taiwan Strait. Taiwan’s official Central News Agency also reported Monday that Tsai would meet with McCarthy, citing Tsai’s presidential office.

Video Ad Feedback See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05 • Source: CNN See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05

But a meeting between Tsai and the leader of the Republican majority in the US House of Representatives, who ranks second in line to the Presidency, would mark another symbolic moment for Taiwan and the US, which only maintain unofficial ties.

For Tsai, who is entering the final year of her two-term presidency, “it’s clearly a capstone event,” according to Wen-Ti Sung, a political scientist at the Australian National University’s Taiwan Studies Program. “She has this image as the Taiwanese president who has taken US-Taiwan relations to new heights, and who … has been able to give Taiwan almost unprecedented international visibility,” he said.

That increased visibility – and enhanced cooperation with the US – has followed China’s mounting pressure on the island, which sits fewer than 110 miles (177 kilometers) from the mainland coast.

China’s Communist Party claims the self-governing island democracy as its own despite never having controlled it, and has vowed to take the island, by force if necessary.

The party has undertaken a sweeping expansion of its military capabilities over the past decade under leader Xi Jinping – and ramped up its pervasive economic, diplomatic and military pressure on Taiwan.

That’s driven concerns, among some in Washington, that Beijing is preparing for an invasion, though China’s official language still suggests that scenario is not its preferred option for achieving the claimed goal of “reunification.”

It is those pressures – and how to support Taiwan against unilateral actions by Beijing – that are likely to be on the table when Tsai, McCarthy and a bipartisan group of US lawmakers sit down on Wednesday.

Congress has been a pillar of increasing American support for Taiwan in recent years. Lawmakers regularly visit the island and drive bipartisan legislation enhancing support and cooperation.

While the US switched its diplomatic relations to Beijing decades ago, it maintains unofficial ties with Taiwan and is bound by law to provide the democratic island with the means to defend itself.

Under Washington’s longstanding “One China” policy, the US acknowledges China’s position that Taiwan is part of China, but has never officially recognized Beijing’s claim to the island of 23 million.

Though McCarthy does not have Pelosi’s decades-long record of advocacy regarding China, the California Republican is now a leading voice pushing for closer scrutiny of Beijing, and meeting Tsai could help him to burnish that image.

Last month, McCarthy told reporters that meeting Tsai in the US would not impact whether he travels to Taiwan in the future – something he had earlier said he wanted to do.

Fighter jets of the Chinese People's Liberation Army Eastern Theater Command conduct joint combat training exercises around Taiwan on August 7, 2022 in this photo released by Xinhua News Agency. Gong Yulong/Xinhua/AP

Beijing watching

A meeting in California, on US soil, is widely seen as less likely to provoke Beijing than a McCarthy visit to Taiwan.

Pelosi’s trip – the first from a lawmaker of that rank to the island in 25 years – generated a fever pitch of nationalist and anti-US rhetoric in mainland China.

This time, so far, domestic conversation in China’s heavily controlled media sphere has been significantly muted.

But the stakes remain high – including for Beijing itself – over how it responds, analysts say.

As Taiwan prepares for a presidential election in January, a fierce response could push voters away from Taiwan’s main opposition party Kuomintang (KMT), widely seen as more friendly toward Beijing.

It could also jar with another high profile trip happening now: a tour of mainland China from former Taiwan president and senior KMT member Ma Ying-jeou, the first visit from a current or former Taiwan leader since the end of the Chinese Civil War in 1949.

Ma’s tour is a “once in a half a century opportunity to send a conciliatory message between the two sides, Beijing shouldn’t want to tank that,” said Sung, the political scientist.

China is also acutely aware that its actions toward Taiwan are under a significantly brighter global spotlight following the invasion of Ukraine by Russian President Vladimir Putin, a close diplomatic partner of Xi. Putin’s rhetoric over Ukraine has echoes of how Xi speaks of Taiwan.

Beijing has recently sought to position itself as an agent of peace in that conflict – especially as it aims to repair frayed ties with Europe.

This week, as Tsai is expected to meet with McCarthy, French President Emmanuel Macron and European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen will head to China – an important opportunity that Xi may not want to overshadow with military posturing.

An aggressive response also risks stoking confrontation with the US, not yet six months after Xi and US President Joe Biden called to enhance communication during a face-to-face meeting in Bali.

“(A less overtly aggressive response) would imply that Beijing does not wish to escalate tension with the US to a level that can risk getting out of hand,” said Steve Tsang, director of the SOAS China Institute in London.

“A reset in US-China ties is not on the agenda, but an easing of tension is not beyond the realm of possibility.”

World.title: Dodik declared Bosnia ‘dead’. Irrelevant rhetoric or serious threat?
World.content:
Speaking at the final rally of his right-wing alliance ahead of Bosnia’s October 4 election, Bosnian Serb leader Milorad Dodik delivered a predictably controversial statement.

“Bosnia-Herzegovina is dead. It is an impossible country, it makes no sense,” Dodik told supporters of the Alliance of Independent Social Democrats (SNSD) party in Banja Luka on Friday.

“It is now nothing more than an empty shell … for those who are trying to keep it alive, so they can prove themselves right about something,” said the former president of Republika Srpska, who is known for frequent separatist threats and for challenging the country’s constitution.

Dodik’s comments came as Bosnia remains deeply divided over its political future more than three decades since the 1995 Dayton peace agreement. It split the country into two semi-autonomous parts – the Serb-majority Republika Srpska entity and the Federation entity, where most Bosniaks and Croats live.

The agreement ended the 1992–95 Bosnian War and established a political framework for power-sharing among Muslim Bosniaks, Orthodox Serbs and Catholic Croats.

On Sunday, voters across the country cast ballots to elect the three members of Bosnia and Herzegovina’s multiethnic presidency, representatives to the national parliament and leaders of institutions in the country’s two entities.

Dodik himself is not on the ballot after being stripped of his post last year, following his conviction for refusing to carry out decisions issued by Christian Schmidt, the international peace envoy who oversees the implementation of the Dayton peace agreement.



‘No political relevance’

Elvis Fejzic, a professor at the Faculty of Political Science in Sarajevo, said attempts by figures such as Dodik to dismantle Bosnia and Herzegovina amount to “populist rhetoric”.

“Politicians and political parties that act unconstitutionally do not determine the fate of Bosnia and Herzegovina,” Fejzic told Al Jazeera, arguing that Bosnia and Herzegovina’s status as a UN member and internationally recognised state is secure.

“Bosnia and Herzegovina … will outlive all those who, through inflammatory statements, seek to obstruct its path towards integration and development,” he said. “Their statements have no political relevance whatsoever.”

Political analyst Tanja Topic said that while Dodik was not officially a candidate, he remained a central figure in the campaign and sought to present himself as a “senior official in international relations”.

Topic told Al Jazeera that the election result could produce several political scenarios in Bosnia and Herzegovina, from “cohabitation in Republika Srpska”, through the formation of a grand coalition, to a “blockage at the state level and the Council of Ministers continuing to operate in a caretaker capacity”.

Dodik’s rhetoric marks ‘long escalation’

Expert Adnan Cerimagic said Dodik’s rhetoric should be taken “seriously” and viewed as part of a “long escalation” rather than a reflection of the country’s current reality.

“For the past four years, his moves against the Dayton order and against Bosnia’s EU and NATO path have reached a new and dangerous level: in March 2025 the country came close to an armed standoff between Republika Srpska and state police,” Cerimagic, a senior analyst at the European Stability Initiative, told Al Jazeera.

“Casting Bosnia as a front-line in a supposed war between Christianity and Islam, and himself as a defender of Christian Europe, is aimed at the one people in Europe against whom a genocide has been committed since the Second World War and recognised as such by two international courts,” he added.

Cerimagic added that Dodik’s rhetoric may reflect uncertainty over the electoral prospects of his preferred candidate, as well as a belief that the European Union has less leverage over Bosnia than it once did.

Initial results are customarily released by the Central Election Commission late on election night and then refreshed every few hours.

In the days that follow, the commission progressively inputs votes from polling stations that remain outstanding, mobile voting teams, as well as ballots sent by mail and those cast at diplomatic and consular missions.



The final, official results must be published by November 20 at the latest.

World.title: How was Flydubai co-pilot cleared despite being deemed a security risk?
World.content:
Share How was Flydubai co-pilot cleared despite being deemed a security risk? on social media

A Flydubai co-pilot accused of attacking his captain with an emergency axe and attempting to seize control of the flight bound for Israel had previously been barred from flying over concerns about alleged “extremist” views, raising questions about how he was allowed to fly to Tel Aviv.

The co-pilot has been identified as Hamam al-Hammami, an Omani national, according to multiple media reports.

The United Arab Emirates (UAE) has described the September 30 incident aboard Flight FZ1073 as an attempted “terrorist” operation.

But investigators are still working to establish the motive and whether anyone else was connected to the attack, which has raised concerns about pilot vetting and aviation security.

So, what security checks do pilots have to go through and how al-Hammami may have evaded background checks?

How did al-Hammami apparently pass the checks?

That is now one of the central questions facing investigators.

Al-Hammami had previously been barred from flying in Oman because of concerns that he had adopted “extremist” views and was instead moved to an administrative role at Oman Air, according to sources who spoke to the AP news agency.

He was subsequently hired by Flydubai.

A Gulf diplomat told AP that al-Hammami had undergone standard security checks before being hired. It wasn’t immediately clear to what extent the co-pilot was vetted.

The US-based network CNN reported that a LinkedIn profile bearing al-Hammami’s name said he had spent seven years at Oman Air before leaving in February 2025. The profile said he joined Royal Air Maroc in June 2025 and left in January this year.



It is unclear what those alleged views were or whether Oman informed other countries or airlines about its concerns.

What background checks do commercial pilots go through?

Background checks for commercial pilots vary by airline and country, with no single global standard governing the process, an airline pilot and instructor told Al Jazeera.

The captain with an international airline who chose to remain anonymous said pilots are generally required to obtain aviation medical certification from the regulator in the country where they are licensed to fly.

In the UAE, that is overseen by the General Civil Aviation Authority (GCAA), he said.

Some airlines also require prospective pilots to provide police clearance certificates from their country of residence as part of pre-employment screening, the pilot added.

One type of check is a Class 1 medical assessment, which typically examines areas including vision, hearing, cardiovascular and neurological health, as well as conditions that could cause sudden incapacitation.

When it comes to security checks, aviation rules require background checks for personnel who have unescorted access to security-restricted areas.

Psychological assessments, drug and alcohol testing and other evaluations may be required depending on the jurisdiction.

How did Israel allow him to fly?

Israel has some of the world’s toughest aviation security measures.

As a result, questions have been raised over how the alleged attacker was allowed to operate a flight to Israel, despite reportedly being an Omani national and Oman having no diplomatic relations with Israel.

According to the Haaretz newspaper, Israeli authorities received the Flydubai flight’s crew and passenger lists before it departed. Under a law passed in 2023, airlines are required to provide information about passengers and crew members, including their names and nationalities, to Israel up to 48 hours before a flight.

The Israel Tax Authority confirmed to Haaretz that it had received the lists for the Flydubai flight. The media outlet reported that the information is also supposed to be available to Israeli security bodies, including the Mossad, police and Shin Bet, to identify people who may pose a security risk.

According to security sources who spoke to Haaretz, the Transportation Ministry’s Security Department and the Mossad are responsible for checking foreign flight crews and issuing alerts if concerns arise.

However, two security sources told Haaretz that while the Transportation Ministry holds responsibility “on paper”, it does not have its own intelligence capacity.



Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has said that Israel has longstanding arrangements with foreign airlines aimed at preventing pilots who are nationals of countries without diplomatic relations with Israel from flying there.

Netanyahu has described what happened as a “loophole” and Israel says it will now strengthen its checks.

The UAE has not yet publicly established a motive or announced whether investigators believe al-Hammami acted alone.

UAE presidential adviser Anwar Gargash said on Saturday that the latest ‘terrorist’ attack is a new warning that the region’s fight against “extremism” is not over.

“This underscores the importance of the UAE’s early and firm stance: no tolerance for extremism and no leniency towards its rhetoric. Security begins with confronting hatred and drying up the sources of extremism,” he posted on X.

World.title: Why is fighting intensifying in Yemen’s Taiz governorate?
World.content:
Government forces fend off waves of Houthi attacks as civilians in the populous province are imperiled.

Share Why is fighting intensifying in Yemen’s Taiz governorate? on social media

Yemen’s internationally recognised government and the Iran-backed Houthis are engaged in a fierce struggle for the Taiz governorate, a key strategic area in the southwest of the country.

Rashad al-Alimi, chief of the Saudi Arabia-backed Presidential Leadership Council (PLC), announced on Sunday the start of a major offensive against the Houthis to regain lost territory. It is expected that this will result in more battles around Taiz, already the site of some of the most recent fighting.

Observers and analysts say that the Houthis are trying to consolidate their gains after seizing much of Yemen’s Red Sea coast last month. For the government, the battle for Taiz represents a strategic and existential struggle for control of the country.

Here’s what we know.

Why is Taiz important?

Taiz governorate is Yemen’s most populous region, with nearly 4.5 million people. The flat western coastal region sits on the Red Sea and includes the port city of Mocha and the strategically important Bab al-Mandeb strait.

These coastal regions were captured by the Houthis in a surprise and lightning campaign in early September, raising fears the group could choke off international shipping through the strait. They were also key supply routes for Taiz.

Much of the governorate lies within Yemen’s highlands and remains contested between the two sides. The region’s capital, Taiz City, is nestled between a number of mountains and is under government control. It is one of Yemen’s most populous cities and a key source of legitimacy for the Yemeni government.



The governorate sits between Yemen’s Houthi-controlled north and the government-held south. The Houthi advance threatens to isolate government forces from Aden, the southern coastal town where key state institutions are based.

Ibrahim Jalal, a senior researcher and policy adviser, told Al Jazeera that Taiz is a city of huge social, political, economic and military importance for the whole of Yemen.

“The Houthi attempt to isolate and constrict the city seeks to secure their coastal Red Sea gains up to Bab al-Mandeb, as well as double down on pressure on Lahij, Aden and much of the south,” said Jalal.

“The Houthis seek to expand their territorial control at the moment along the former boundaries of northern Yemen, or to say, that they want to remove all little pockets of resistance to consolidate control.”

Taiz has been one of the most heavily contested cities in the war, beginning shortly after Houthi forces captured the capital Sanaa in September 2014.

Thousands of civilians have been killed in a devastating Houthi siege and assault on the city, with government forces driving back repeated assaults between 2015 and 2022.

Fighting has been focused on Jabal Han, a mountain overlooking Taiz from the west, as well as a key road into the city.

Control over this mountain would allow the Houthis to attack people and supplies entering Taiz City from the southwest, Saeed Thabet, head of Al Jazeera’s bureau in Yemen, said.

Who has the upper hand?

There has been no clear winner in the battle for Taiz so far, which observers have described as a stalemate.

Al Jazeera’s Mohammed al-Qadi, reporting from the city, said government forces have launched dozens of air strikes on Houthi bases and positions across Taiz in recent days.

Houthi fighters are trying to advance under cover of intense artillery, tank, mortar and Katyusha rocket fire into the city.

Artillery fire could be heard around Taiz as residents appealed to be evacuated, Al Jazeera’s Maha Ali, reporting from Taiz City, said on Sunday.

On that day, local authorities reported that a shell had hit a residential area in Dhubab, killing a 14-day-old infant. Other attacks have wounded civilians.

Government forces are also shelling Houthi forces positioned around the city.

Face-to-face fighting has now reached the countryside on the outskirts of Taiz City. Residents are fighting on their own initiative against Houthi attempts to infiltrate villages and mountain areas around Taiz, a local source said.

The heaviest fighting is taking place at the western axis of the city, where government forces have mounted a fierce defence at Jabal Han.



On Sunday, Yemen’s government forces announced gains against the Houthis, saying they had captured several areas, including a fort in Samaa.

The military command in Taiz also claimed its forces had repelled Houthi attacks on Jabal Han, Hazran and other points west of Taiz City.

Yemeni military spokesman Majed al-Nuzaili said government forces had carried out dozens of operations using aircraft, drones, artillery, missiles and snipers, resulting in hundreds of Houthi casualties. Al Jazeera could not verify these claims.

In early September, the Houthis managed to expand their control over Yemen’s Red Sea coast with unexpected speed and limited resistance.

However, they have faced much fiercer fighting from government forces in Taiz.

One key reason for this is the cohesion between government forces and the local tribes. Al Jazeera’s Yasser Hassan reports that tribesmen took part in Sunday’s capture of the Samaa Fort.

How are civilians in Taiz being impacted?

The humanitarian cost of the renewed fighting in Taiz has already manifested in a refugee crisis with limited access to humanitarian goods and services.

There has also been an increase in civilian casualties. Since fighting escalated in early September, nearly 200,000 people have been displaced in Yemen, most of them from Taiz governorate, according to Yemen’s Executive Unit for IDP Camps Management.

The closure of some major roads into Taiz City has raised fears of an impending humanitarian disaster.

The Office of the United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR) and the World Health Organization (WHO) have both warned that the fighting was putting Yemen’s fragile healthcare system in peril.

Al Jazeera’s Hassan described the humanitarian situation as “very difficult” after government forces decided to shut down all roads leading into the city out of fear of Houthi infiltration.

Before Mocha was taken over by Houthis, its port was a critical supply line from which food and aid were delivered to Taiz City.

The ongoing war has also devastated the country. Nearly half of Yemen’s 34 million population face acute food insecurity, according to the UN, with about half a million people suffering severe malnutrition.
