World.title: What are the five questions being asked regarding the Flydubai attack?
World.content:
As investigations are conducted, official versions of the incident have come under scrutiny.

Share What are the five questions being asked regarding the Flydubai attack? on social media

An attack by the copilot on the pilot during a Flydubai flight has raised many questions regarding aviation security, and some of the official versions of the incident have come under scrutiny from online commentators and aviation enthusiasts.

About two and a half hours after Flight FZ1073 departed from Dubai International Airport on Wednesday, it went into a sharp descent before eventually making an emergency landing in Saudi Arabia.

Media reports said the copilot attacked Captain Smit Machchhar. Passengers were able to overpower the copilot, identified by media as Hamam al-Hammami, after Machchhar managed to open the cockpit door during the attack, which the prosecutor general of the United Arab Emirates said was carried out with the cockpit’s crash axe.

While investigators continue working to establish a motive for the attack, several questions have arisen about the incident more generally across social media.

Here are five questions that are being asked:

Why was al-Hammami allowed to fly despite being flagged over security concerns?

Al-Hammami has been identified as an Omani national, according to media reports.

On Friday, The Wall Street Journal quoted unnamed sources as saying that Omani authorities previously blocked the suspect from flying in the country due to concerns over his ideological views.

On Saturday, CNN reported, quoting a regional diplomatic source, that the copilot had also been removed from flight training over similar concerns and was later reassigned to another position.



It added, quoting two sources familiar with the matter, that the pilot was removed from a job at Oman’s national airline last year over concerns about his views.

It remains unclear how al-Hammami managed to get the Flydubai route despite these security concerns.

The possibility of a plumber stabilising plane before reserve pilots stepped in

Reports have emerged that Machchhar managed to open the cockpit door while covered in blood, allowing passengers to subdue the copilot.

One of those who subdued al-Hammami was Yaniv Hayoun, whom Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu described as a plumber.

In a video with Netanyahu, who met him at the airport, Hayoun, 50, was asked how he knew what to do at the plane’s controls before another pilot took control. He said: “I watch Air Crash Investigation, Mr Prime Minister.”

“I jumped back, grabbed the controls and started pulling back the handles” the way he had seen in the Canadian investigation show, in which experts analyse plane crashes.

People on social media have questioned how a plumber could have handled an aircraft in the air.

No report of mass injuries despite fall of 5,180 metres

According to the flight-tracking website Flightradar24, the Flydubai flight rapidly descended about two and a half hours after takeoff, dropping more than 5,180 metres (17,000ft) in less than two minutes.

While the midair drop caused mass panic among passengers, no one was reportedly harmed, according to the publicly available information about the incident. An Air India flight that dropped 90 metres (300ft) during turbulence in August injured at least 17 passengers.

A flight instructor, who recreated the Flydubai jet’s near-vertical dive in a simulator, said the plane would have exceeded its maximum structural speed and anything unsecured would have flown all over the cabin during the recovery’s negative G-forces.

Why was the copilot allowed to fly despite being an Omani national?

Israel does not have official diplomatic relations with Oman, and Netanyahu has previously said such countries were not generally allowed to operate flights to Israel.

On Friday, Netanyahu said Israel was looking into whether the copilot had acted under anyone’s direction, warning that anyone involved would pay a “heavy price”.

On Saturday, the Israeli newspaper Haaretz reported that government officials had received in advance the list of crew members and passengers who were on the flight, including the Omani copilot.

Security sources told Haaretz that the government bodies responsible for monitoring and checking foreign flight crews landing in Israel are the Ministry of Transport and Road Safety’s Security Department and the security agency Mossad.



Copilot prayed before attack

According to The Times of Israel, Machchhar spoke to Netanyahu on Saturday. He told the prime minister that al-Hammami had asked to pray before the attack. Four or five minutes later, Machchhar was hit with “a big blow” to the back of his head, he said.

The flight departed from the UAE at 7:05am (03:05 GMT). The attack reportedly took place about two and a half hours later (05:35 GMT).

The predawn prayer time in the Emirates on Wednesday was 04:51am (12:51 GMT), which would mean al-Hammami’s prayer did not align with Islamic prayer times.

However, al-Hammami could also have been performing a different personal prayer before the attack.

World.title: Did the fall of al-Andalus reshape Europe forever?
World.content:
Deja Vu traces Europe’s Muslim history from Al-Andalus to today. Why are Muslims still treated as outsiders?

From Spain to Sicily, Muslims helped shape Europe for centuries. Why do they still seem to be cast as outsiders? In this episode of Deja Vu, author Tariq Ali traces the rise of al-Andalus to its fall amid the burning of books and the loss of a shared past. How does that history still shape Europe’s politics today?

In this episode:

Tariq Ali (@TariqAli_News), author and editor of the New Left Review

World.title: Amid teen triumph and organisational chaos, Asian Games close in Japan
World.content:
The continental competition hosted 17,000 athletes over two weeks in Aichi-Nagoya.

Share Amid teen triumph and organisational chaos, Asian Games close in Japan on social media

After two weeks of youthful brilliance on the field amid logistical dysfunction and subdued public interest off it, the curtain has come down on the 20th Asian Games in Japan.

Olympic Council of Asia (OCA) president Sheikh Joaan bin Hamad Al Thani declared the Games closed at Mizuho Park Athletic Stadium on Sunday, with the torch handed to organisers of the next event in Doha, Qatar, in 2030.

Some 17,000 athletes and officials came for the Aichi-Nagoya showpiece – more than the participants in the Paris Olympics – with athletes competing in 469 gold-medal events spanning Tokyo to Osaka.

The massive scale clashed with organisers’ planning for a “simple, streamlined and functional event” — and the results were often chaotic.

Athletes and teams complained of bungled accommodation and transport, prompting repeated apologies from the embarrassed organising committee.

Despite the challenges, the games were lifted by the performances of teenage titans, led by China’s 13-year-old swimmer Yu Zidi.

Awarded the female Most Valuable Player (MVP) of the games, Yu is on track for a huge Los Angeles Olympics after claiming three individual gold medals in the Tokyo pool.

She swam the second-fastest time in winning the 200 metres individual medley, setting up a battle royale with Canada’s world-record holder Summer McIntosh.

Her 19-year-old teammate Zhang Zhanshuo became the first swimmer to win seven golds at the games, while Japan’s 17-year-old wunderkind Shin Ohashi smashed the 200m breaststroke world record.



Track and field events were lit up by young athletes as well, with China’s 18-year-old Yan Ziyi producing a world-class throw to win the women’s javelin gold while 20-year-old Thai sprinter Puripol Boonson swept the 100m and 200m to become the men’s MVP.

No games village

The athletes performed despite regular logistical failures and occasional diplomatic gaffes.

“Accommodation, transport and other issues — it seems a lot of teams were affected,” Hong Kong team chef de mission Wong Po-kee told the Reuters news agency on Sunday.

Organisers opted to house athletes and officials in a mix of hotels, wooden container units and a cruise ship to cut costs rather than build a dedicated athletes’ village.

They budgeted for 15,000 athletes and officials — about 2,000 fewer than total registrations — and struggled to manage them.

Waves of athletes spent up to 12 hours waiting to be registered on arrival.

While checking in, some found their rooms double-booked or being shared by the wrong teammates.

Transport problems dogged the games throughout, with athletes’ shuttle buses failing to turn up or taking them to the wrong venues. Several competitions were delayed due to these errors.

South Korea’s delegation was particularly aggrieved, with their team chef de mission marking the games’ organisation with an “F”, the lowest grade.

South Korean men’s footballers were upset when their national flag could not be hoisted for the national anthem at the victory ceremony after they beat Japan for the gold medal on Saturday.

Earlier, the North Korean national anthem was played for South Korea’s men’s hockey team in another awkward mix-up.

Five years after the Tokyo Olympics were staged without fans due to COVID-19 restrictions, Japan’s first major multisport event was blighted by poor crowds.

Fewer than 1,000 spectators watched the hosts beat South Korea in a women’s football semifinal at a 50,000-capacity stadium.

Much smaller venues were often nearly empty, though many were based in far-flung locations, making access a challenge.

“If I had to say, well, I don’t think it was a success,” Nagoya resident Naoko Toda, who watched several competitions, told Reuters before the closing ceremony.

Despite the issues, the games’ governing body OCA declared Aichi-Nagoya a success and praised organisers for their frugal arrangements.



China topped the table with 341 medals, including 169 gold, with its best haul at an overseas Asian Games.

Japan also delivered for fans who tuned in, with 83 gold medals out of 269, smashing its previous record at Hiroshima 1994.

Padel, mixed martial arts, teqball and surfing made their games debuts in a record 43-sport programme that dwarfed the Paris Olympics.

Qatar is set to host the next continental games in 2030, though the OCA may elect to push it back a year to serve as the continent’s Olympic qualifiers before Brisbane 2032.

World.title: Yemen’s leader announces military operation to retake Houthi-held territory
World.content:
Rashad al-Alimi says the campaign aims to restore state authority throughout Yemen.

⁠The ⁠Saudi Arabia-backed head of ⁠Yemen’s Presidential Leadership Council, ⁠Rashad al-Alimi, has announced the start of military operations to retake the ⁠remaining territory held by ⁠the Iran-backed Houthi armed group ⁠and restore ⁠state ⁠authority across the country.

In a televised address, al-Alimi said on Sunday the internationally recognised government’s forces would extend “the authority of the state and its institutions over the entire national territory”.

“We have instructed the armed forces, security forces and all military formations to begin carrying out their assigned tasks under an approved plan until the country is liberated from the Houthis,” he said.

Al-Alimi added that all state institutions will be placed on full alert “until the mission is completed and victory is achieved”.

Hundreds of Houthis killed

The development comes after Yemeni forces “executed 257 precision targeting operations” against Houthi sites, movements, and military capabilities on Saturday, according to the spokesman for Yemen’s internationally recognised government forces, Colonel Majed Abdullah al-Nazili.

He added that initial estimates indicate that the operations killed at least 700 Houthi rebels.

The spokesman for the Saudi-led coalition supporting the government, Turki al-Malik, said on Saturday that the Houthis’ “ties to external agendas” have brought “chaos and devastation to Yemen”.

Early on Sunday, the Saudi-led coalition said its armed forces carried out 97 “precise targeting operations” against Houthi reinforcements on the Tor al-Baha front and the Taiz axis, using warplanes, drones, artillery, missiles and snipers.



Later in the day, Houthi spokesman Yahya Saree later claimed the group’s forces had fired ballistic missiles and drones at two Saudi Aramco sites in Saudi Arabia – one in Riyadh and the other in the area of Khurais, some 150km (93 miles) north-east of the capital.

There was no immediate comment by Saudi Arabia.

The fighting between the Houthis and Yemeni government forces has intensified since a fragile 2022 truce collapsed in July, displacing hundreds of thousands of people since.

In mid-September, the Houthis seized the port city of Mocha and strategic islands in the Bab al-Mandeb strait, a vital route for global oil shipments, before anti-Houthi forces stabilised front lines.

Yemen has been at war since the Houthis seized the capital, Sanaa, in 2014, forcing the Yemeni government to retreat to Aden.

World.title: Kyiv bridge hit in further Russian drone attack as German chancellor makes surprise visit
World.content:
Major bridges in Kyiv have been hit by Russian drone strikes for four consecutive days, as Moscow ramps up attacks on critical infrastructure in Ukraine's capital.

Two people were injured when the Pivnichnyi (Northern) Bridge was struck on Sunday morning for the second day in a row, while the Pivdennyi (Southern) Bridge was hit multiple times earlier in the week.

The latest attack came as German Chancellor Friedrich Merz made a surprise visit to Kyiv in a show of support against Russia's continuing full-scale invasion.

Russia's military said it would be intensifying strikes on Kyiv and other Ukrainian regions. It earlier said it had hit the two bridges used to transfer Ukrainian troops.

Video footage of Sunday's strike, verified by the BBC, shows cars moving on Pivnichnyi Bridge as a drone crashes into it before exploding, creating a ball of fire. A cloud of black smoke can be seen rising above the bridge.

Other videos and pictures have emerged on social media showing a gaping hole in the middle of a traffic lane on the bridge.

World.title: Watch: What we know about Russian strikes on Kyiv bridges
World.content:
Major bridges in Ukraine have been the target of Russian strikes over the past four days, as Moscow ramps up attacks in Ukraine's capital city.

The Pivnichnyi (Northern) Bridge, has been hit for the second day in a row, while the Pivdennyi (Southern) Bridge was hit multiple times earlier this week.

The latest attack came as German Chancellor Friedrich Merz made a visit to Kyiv on Sunday.

BBC Ukraine correspondent Dan Johnson is near one of the bridges that was targeted and explains what we know so far.

World.title: Yemen announces military campaign to reclaim land from Iran-backed Houthis
World.content:
Away from Yemen, the Houthis are also trying to hurt the Saudis with an attack aimed at the country's economic lifeblood - oil.

On Sunday, Yemen's Houthi military spokesman Yahya Saree said the group had launched a ballistic missile and drone attack on Aramco sites in the capital, Riyadh, and the oil-rich Khurais area in the kingdom's east.

"Both operations successfully achieved their objectives," the spokesman said in a statement. "The strikes were precise, causing large fires at the targeted sites."

It is not the first time the group has said it has hit Saudi oil sites. Saudi Arabia has yet to comment on Sunday's claimed attack, but has previously dismissed some claims as misleading, mocking the Houthis for "chasing imaginary victories".

But it has once again shown the price Saudi Arabia - and, as a consequence, the global economy - could pay if it launched a new all-out war against the Houthis.

In retaliation, Saudi Arabia has also been striking Houthi targets, according to the Houthi-run Al-Masirah TV channel. It said at least two people had been wounded in strikes on Sunday.

On Saturday, Yemen's government also said its forces had hit Houthi targets across the country, including in Sanaa, Saada and the group's positions near Taiz in the south-west.

Yemen is one of the poorest countries in the world and remains gripped by a vast humanitarian crisis.

A war erupted in 2014, when the Houthis seized the capital, Sanaa, from the Saudi-backed government, before going on to take control of swathes of the country's north.

Riyadh intervened in the war the following year, leading an international coalition.

After several years of relative calm, the war reignited in July amid the widening conflict in the Middle East.

The Houthis have launched a blockade of Saudi energy exports, which have already been squeezed by Iran's closure of the Strait of Hormuz.

World.title: Ethiopian rebel forces withdraw from Tigray regional capital
World.content:
Rebel forces in Ethiopia's northern Tigray region have said they have temporarily withdrawn from the regional capital, Mekelle, as fighting with the national army moves towards the city.

The Tigray People's Liberation Front (TPLF), which has been running the region, said its decision to relocate was made because of concerns about risks to civilians.

Two residents in Mekelle told the BBC that pro-government forces now control the city and TPLF forces have abandoned it. One resident also said mobile phone services appear to have resumed in parts of the city.

Fighting has erupted in recent weeks between the TPLF and federal government forces alongside allied fighters in parts of Ethiopia's northern regions of Tigray, Afar and Amhara.

The development marks a major shift in the conflict and raises concerns among observers that the fighting could further destabilise the Horn of Africa, potentially drawing in neighbouring countries.

The US Department of State called for "restraint" and "dialogue" on all sides ahead of a diplomatic meeting about the conflict in Egypt on Sunday with leaders from some of Ethiopia's neighbours.

World.title: Australia investigating Flydubai co-pilot's links to country
World.content:
Australian authorities are investigating the links between the country and a Flydubai co-pilot who attempted to take control of a plane travelling to Israel.

The co-pilot is alleged to have attacked the captain with a crash axe during a flight from Dubai to Tel Aviv before passengers managed to overpower him and successfully take control of the plane.

The Australian authorities have not identified the co-pilot, who has been named by multiple media outlets including Reuters, CNN and The New York Times as Hamam al-Hammami.

The prosecutor in the UAE has said it is investigating the incident and any possible motives.

In a statement to the BBC, the Australian Federal Police (AFP) confirmed its investigation into "the man's links to Australia".

The investigation involves state police and the country's security agency, it said, adding that an update would be "provided at the appropriate time".

Sources familiar with the case, who have spoken to Australian media, have said the co-pilot was issued a student visa in 2014, and studied in Australia between 2015 and 2017, until he left the country.

The Australian Broadcasting Corporation (ABC) said the co-pilot's student visa was cancelled in 2019 as he was no longer enrolled in a course, making him ineligible for it.

Counter-terrorism officials will look at whether the man was radicalised in Australia, the ABC reported.

Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has said he was an Omani national.

The flight from Dubai to Tel Aviv on 30 September was carrying more than 170 passengers to Israel.

Two and a half hours into its journey, the plane plunged 17,000ft (5,200m) when the Omani co-pilot attacked the pilot with a crash axe, the United Arab Emirates prosecutor general has said.

The pilot flying the plane, Capt Smit Machchhar, described how he was lying on the floor injured when he realised the plane was sinking and he had to act, explaining: "I told myself to go for one last push to open the door from inside", which allowed the passengers in.

Two reserve pilots then landed the plane safely in Saudi Arabia.

World.title: US Marine arrested over murder of woman in Okinawa, Japan
World.content:
A US Marine has been arrested on suspicion of murder after a woman's body was found in a hotel in Okinawa, Japan, local officials say.

Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi described the crime as a "brutal and heinous" robbery and murder. She said she had urged the US to "enforce stricter discipline" of its personnel.

Japan's public broadcaster NHK identified the victim as Yagi Anna, 39, and the suspect as Devin Jacob Ballard, 20, who is stationed at US Marine Corps Air Station Futenma.

"We are actively cooperating with Japanese authorities, in response to allegations of serious criminal actions by a Marine," the Marine Corps said on social media, extending condolences to the victim's family.

Japanese Defence Minister Shinjiro Koizumi said the woman's body was discovered early Saturday morning in a hotel in Naha City, the capital of the Okinawa prefecture.

"Such an incident is utterly inexcusable and fills me with strong indignation," Koizumi wrote on social media, adding that "incidents and accidents involving U.S. military personnel cause significant anxiety to the local community and must never occur".

The US Embassy in Tokyo said that it was fully cooperating with the Japanese government and local police. Japan's foreign ministry said it summoned US ambassador George Glass to discuss the incident on Sunday.

Okinawa is home to several US military bases and tens of thousands of American troops.

Okinawa Governor Genta Koja says the prefecture has repeatedly demanded that the US take action to prevent such incidents, and said he sees the alleged crime as a sign of a lack of discipline.

"The fact that this kind of event has happened again leaves us no choice but to conclude that the US military's efforts in maintaining discipline, educating personnel, and other such measures are completely ineffective," he said.

World.title: What to know about Brazil's election pitting Lula against Flávio Bolsonaro
World.content:
Lula, the 80-year-old candidate for the left-wing Workers' Party, has been president three times already.

He served two consecutive terms - from January 2003 to December 2010 - and was widely praised for lifting millions out of poverty during this time with the help of a cash-transfer programme called Bolsa FamÃ­lia.

The former metalworker left office with record approval ratings of over 80%, but his party was later rocked by huge corruption scandals.

Lula himself spent more than 18 months in prison between 2018 and 2019 after being convicted of corruption and money laundering, charges he has always denied.

Those convictions were annulled in 2021, leaving Lula free to run for the presidency in the 2022 election, in which he beat Jair Bolsonaro by 1.8 percentage points.

When he started his third term in office, he vowed it would be his last, and yet his party endorsed him as their candidate again this year, even though he will turn 81 later this month.

There is no doubt he remains a towering figure in the left. But while his supporters described him ahead of the 2022 election as the "saviour of the Amazon", praising his commitment to protecting the rainforest, some environmentalists have been critical of some of his recent actions.

His support for exploratory oil drilling in offshore waters near the mouth of the Amazon in particular has drawn criticism.

Lula insists that he remains committed to eventually phasing out fossil fuels and argues that oil revenues are key to financing Brazil's transition to clean energy.

His government has also pointed to the reduction in deforestation in the Amazon - satellite data suggests the area deforested in the first half of 2026 was reduced to its lowest in the past decade - as proof that its policies were working.

During Lula's latest term in office, relations with his US counterpart Donald Trump have been rocky.

Referring to what Trump has dubbed the "Donroe doctrine" - his administration's national security strategy which asserts that US dominance in the Western hemisphere should not be interfered with - Lula has insisted that "Brazil does not fit into anyone's backyard".

In another thinly veiled reference to both his rival FlÃ¡vio Bolsonaro and those in the Trump administration who would like to see the right-wing candidate win, the Brazilian leader has also warned that he would not tolerate "foreign and local enemies of democracy" interfering with the polls.

World.title: Cornell president says university 'must do better' after frat house rape allegations
World.content:
Cornell University's president says the school "must do better" after a woman alleged she was drugged and raped by a group of men at a fraternity house.

In an eight-minute video statement released on Saturday night, Michael Kotlikoff described the allegations raised by the woman, identified as Jane Doe, as "deeply disturbing".

The alleged incident has raised questions around the culture on campus of drug and alcohol use, and the way investigations were conducted in the case, Kotlikoff said.

Jane Doe was a 20-year-old student at the university when she says seven men from its Chi Phi fraternity assaulted her for hours in an incident involving alcohol and the drug ketamine on 19 October 2024.

She said she had reported the incident two weeks after it happened to Cornell University police, which investigated, but no charges were laid.

Last month, Jane Doe filed a civil lawsuit against the Ivy League university, in which she alleged Cornell had failed to protect her or adequately punish the men involved.

Kotlikoff said Cornell was "committed to investigating" the way the case was handled, and said the school administration and community "must do better".

"We must foster a culture in which sexual assault is inexcusable and ensure our community is empowered and understands informed consent," he said.

He added that university leaders need to create an environment where victims of sexual assault "feel safe coming forward and are treated with compassion and dignity".

Kotlikoff said it is a "defining moment" in the university's history.

"We must lead the way, we owe it to Jane Doe and to survivors of assault to get this right. And we must keep each other safe," he said.

On the university's campus this week, the BBC saw growing frustration about the situation.

World.title: NLO Cup adopts home-and-away format to guarantee clubs more matches
World.content:
The Nationwide League One (NLO) has announced that its revamped NLO Cup will adopt a regional home-and-away league format designed to guarantee participating clubs more matches and improve players’ competitive exposure.

Under the new structure, the number of fixtures each team plays will depend on the total number of clubs in its zone. A team in a 10-club group, for instance, could play up to 18 matches, with the possibility of more fixtures in zones featuring additional teams.

The format represents a departure from a single-match knockout arrangement, offering clubs a more extensive schedule of competitive engagements.

The NLO Chief Operating Officer, Olushola Ogunnowo, said the new structure was designed to address the need for more playing opportunities while creating a more sustainable competitive environment for clubs.

“A key benefit of the new NLO Cup format is the guaranteed increase in match opportunities. Instead of a single knockout fixture, the league format provides a broader schedule of competitive games,” Mr Ogunnowo told the NLO media channel.

He said the expanded schedule would enable clubs to host more matches before their supporters, gain valuable experience from away fixtures, expose players to competitive football and strengthen their sporting and commercial prospects.

The league also expects the format to promote youth development, deepen fan engagement and strengthen the relationship between clubs and their host communities.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

Shared venues to ease logistics

To reduce travel demands and logistical pressures, the NLO said multiple clubs would be permitted to host their home matches at the same venues, with fixtures scheduled on weekdays or weekends.

The arrangement is expected to make the competition more manageable for participating teams while ensuring a smoother fixture schedule.

Mr Ogunnowo said the revamped format would provide a more structured environment for clubs to develop their teams and establish stronger competitive identities.

“The revitalised NLO Cup advances a more structured and competitive environment for NLO clubs. With more fixtures, players can showcase their skills, coaches can improve teams, and clubs can enhance their competitive identity,” he said.

He added that the home-and-away arrangement would give players the experience of competing before home supporters while preparing them for the demands of away matches.

“The home-and-away format will motivate clubs to enjoy the excitement of playing in front of supporters and to tackle the challenges of away games,” he said.

READ ALSO: Lagos Sports Commission DG meets mother of young athlete over viral video

Registration requirements

The NLO Cup is scheduled to kick off on 10 October 2026, with eligible clubs from NLO Division One and the NLO Youth League Under-19 required to pay a non-refundable registration fee of ₦1 million.

The league said the fee would cover tournament logistics, with payments to be made directly into its designated account with FCMB.

Participating clubs are required to submit proof of payment to the NLO Secretariat for verification and registration clearance.

The competition forms part of the NLO’s efforts to expand playing opportunities, improve talent development and create greater visibility for clubs and players within Nigeria’s lower-tier football structure.

World.title: NDLEA intercepts N5bn cannabis, codeine consignments at Lagos, Onne ports
World.content:
The National Drug Law Enforcement Agency (NDLEA) says it has intercepted cannabis and codeine-based cough syrup consignments worth more than N5 billion at the Apapa, Tincan Island in Lagos and Onne ports in Rivers State.

The agency also stated that it destroyed 20,234kg of cannabis on a farm in Osun State and arrested suspects in separate operations in Lagos, Kogi, Edo and Plateau states.

The NDLEA Director of Media and Advocacy, Femi Babafemi, disclosed this in a statement on Sunday.

At Apapa Port in Lagos, NDLEA operatives, working with the Nigeria Customs Service and other agencies, searched two containers from Bangkok, Thailand, following intelligence.

One of the containers contained 161 parcels of Thai Loud weighing 124kg. The agency valued the consignment at N372 million.

The cannabis was concealed inside two refrigerators and two cartons.

At Onne Port in Rivers State, operatives searched two containers placed on the NDLEA watchlist.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

They recovered 40 packs of Loud weighing 22kg from a travelling bag and found three vehicles — a Toyota Matrix, Toyota Corolla and Hyundai Elantra — in one of the containers.

The second container contained 109,600 bottles of codeine-based cough syrup weighing 16,440kg.

The NDLEA explained that the container originated from India and was shipped to Saudi Arabia, but details of its original route were allegedly altered to avoid detection.

The agency valued the two consignments at Onne at N833.2 million.

The seizure follows an earlier major interception at the port.

In April, the NDLEA said a Federal High Court in Port Harcourt granted an interim forfeiture order over 17 containers containing illicit opioids worth N33.69 billion intercepted at the Port Harcourt Ports Complex, Onne.

The agency stated that the containers contained millions of opioid pills and nearly 2.5 million bottles of codeine-based syrup.

Tincan port

At Tincan Island Port in Lagos, operatives on 29 September searched a container from Montreal, Canada, following intelligence.

They recovered 2,595 parcels of Canadian Loud weighing 1,297.5kg.

The cannabis was concealed inside a Toyota Sienna and a Hyundai Elantra, alongside 24 blue drums and six jumbo bags.

The NDLEA valued the consignment at more than N3.8 billion.

Weeks earlier, the agency had announced the seizure of 1,200 parcels of Canadian Loud weighing 603.75kg at the same port. It valued that consignment at N1.81 billion.

4.8kg cocaine seized at Lagos airport

At the Murtala Muhammed International Airport, Lagos, NDLEA operatives arrested a 38-year-old businessman, Philip Tunde, who allegedly attempted to smuggle 4.8kg of cocaine to Milan, Italy.

Mr Babafemi said the suspect was arrested on 27 September at the joint screening point of Terminal 2 before boarding a Royal Air Maroc flight.

Sixteen parcels of cocaine were allegedly concealed in the soles of eight pairs of trainers and canvas shoes, while another 195 wraps were hidden in the railings of four travelling bags.

The substance tested positive for cocaine and weighed 4.8kg.

According to the NDLEA, Mr Tunde told investigators that he paid N16 million in cash for the cocaine hidden in the shoes and that the consignment in the bags was meant for his partner in Italy.

He also reportedly said he raised the money from compensation he received after sustaining an injury while working at a plastic manufacturing company in Italy, where he lost the tips of two fingers.

20,234kg cannabis destroyed in Osun

In Osun State, operatives destroyed 20,234kg of skunk found on an 8.0936-hectare cannabis farm in Area 4, Ife South Local Government Area.

The operation was carried out on 30 September.

In Plateau State, operatives arrested 41-year-old Agbo Dennis in the West of Mines area of Jos North on 29 September after recovering 33 bags of skunk weighing 385kg.

The agency also arrested Idris Mohammed Kurra, 47, who had allegedly been on the run since December 2020 after jumping bail in a drug trafficking case.

Mr Kurra was standing trial before the Federal High Court in Jos over the alleged possession and dealing in 198kg of skunk.

Other arrests and seizures

In Lagos, operatives on 28 September raided an unoccupied compound at Divine Estate, Ago Palace, and recovered 209,000 tablets of tramadol.

A follow-up operation led to the arrest of 23-year-old Ekundayo Taiwo at Ladipo Spare Parts Market on 30 September.

The NDLEA said 61 grammes of Colorado and 24 grammes of methamphetamine were recovered from him. The drugs were allegedly concealed in an energy drink bottle and sent as a waybill package through a commercial bus along the Lagos-Ibadan Expressway.

On the Okene-Lokoja highway in Kogi State, operatives intercepted a Lagos-Abuja-bound bus on 30 September and found two sachets containing 1kg of methamphetamine in a waybill package.

A follow-up operation led to the arrest of the alleged owner of the consignment, 29-year-old Michael Chukwuememka Uzoma, in Utako, Abuja.

In Edo State, operatives raided the residence of 35-year-old Saturday Omimi at Uyere community in Ovia North-East Local Government Area on 2 October and recovered 32.2kg of cannabis sativa.

The same day, they arrested 23-year-old Osazuwa Iyabor Michael at Auchi Bypass, Benin City, with 59 grammes of Loud, 12 grammes of Colorado, 19 grammes of tramadol, 16 grammes of methamphetamine, four grammes of Swinol and four grammes of Molly.

N301bn drugs destroyed in Lagos

The NDLEA said last month that it destroyed 329,865.585kg of assorted illicit drugs worth N301.06 billion following court orders.

According to the agency, 246,864.535kg of the drugs had been seized by its Lagos Strategic Command between April 2025 and May 2026.

The destroyed drugs included cocaine, heroin, methamphetamine, Canadian Loud, skunk, tramadol, codeine syrup and other opioids.

In his remarks, the NDLEA Chairman and Chief Executive Officer, Buba Marwa, commended the officers involved in the operations.

He urged them to sustain efforts against drug trafficking while maintaining what he described as a balanced approach to drug control.

World.title: Government, security officials aiding illegal mining – Taraba governor
World.content:
Taraba State Governor Agbu Kefas has alleged that some government and security officials are facilitating illegal mining in the state.

Mr Kefas made the allegation on Saturday at a meeting with artisanal and small-scale miners in Jalingo, vowing to dismantle the network behind the activities.

He said his administration would strengthen regulation of the mining sector and ensure that the state’s mineral resources are not exploited outside the law.

The governor said the problem went beyond miners operating without licences, alleging that some people within government and security structures had become part of the network sustaining illegal mining.

“We have more illegal mining inside than those outside,” Mr Kefas said.

He said his administration was determined to understand the structure behind the illegal operations and disrupt it through stronger coordination among security agencies, mining regulators and mining communities.

Mr Kefas said the government would establish a system that would enable genuine miners to operate legally while making it easier for authorities to identify and deal with those exploiting the state’s mineral resources illegally.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

He said registered miners would operate in designated areas, while mineral off-takers would be encouraged to buy from regulated locations to improve traceability and government oversight.

According to him, the arrangement would also give security agencies better information about mining activities and help authorities distinguish legitimate artisanal miners from criminal operators.

The governor directed the miners’ association to submit a comprehensive list of equipment required by its members, including estimated costs, saying the government would explore financing support to acquire and deploy the equipment to designated mining sites.

He also directed the compilation of accurate data on miners, their communities, villages, locations and operations, saying reliable information was necessary for effective regulation and protection of legitimate miners.

Mr Kefas said the state government was also working to replace unsafe mining and processing methods with safer technologies, particularly the use of mercury in gold processing.

He said the economic value of the state’s mineral resources could not justify practices capable of exposing miners and host communities to hazardous substances.

“Government will work with mining stakeholders across the state to establish practical environmental and health standards for our people,” he said.

The governor said the proposed reforms would require cooperation among the state government, federal mining authorities, security agencies, financial institutions, miners’ associations and host communities.

He directed stakeholders to immediately commence work on the modalities for the new framework, insisting that the reforms must protect legitimate livelihoods while ensuring that Taraba’s mineral resources are properly regulated and contribute to the state’s development.

Miners seek review of monazite restrictions

At the meeting, the state chairman of the Artisanal and Small-Scale Miners Association, Emmanuel George, asked Mr Kefas to reconsider restrictions on monazite mining, saying the policy had pushed many miners into illegal operations.

Mr George claimed that more than 500,000 young men and women were engaged in artisanal mining across the state.

He also claimed that the restrictions on monazite mining had pushed more than 300,000 members of the association into illegal mining.

Despite the restrictions, he alleged that large quantities of monazite were still leaving the state through informal channels.

Mr George argued that allowing regulated mining would enable the government to monitor production, generate revenue and create employment.

He said miners were not opposed to regulation but wanted to be properly organised, recognised, trained and empowered to operate within the law.

The association chairman also appealed for operational vehicles and motorcycles to enable its officials and representatives to reach mining communities across the state.

He pledged the association’s cooperation with government and regulatory agencies to educate miners, enforce safety standards and ensure compliance with mining laws.

The state chairperson of Women in Mining, Elizabeth Elijah, also called for the inclusion of women in the proposed mining reforms and government interventions.

World.title: CAF confirms date for 2026 Awards in Lagos
World.content:
The Confederation of African Football (CAF) has confirmed that the 2026 edition of its annual awards ceremony will take place in Lagos, Nigeria, on 7 December.

The decision was reached at a virtual meeting of the CAF Executive Committee (EXCO), chaired by the organisation’s president, Patrice Motsepe, on Friday, 2 October.

The meeting also approved the CAF Competitions Calendar for 2026–2030, alongside amendments to the regulations governing the continent’s interclub competitions.

Nigeria will host another major CAF event, the organisation’s Ordinary General Assembly, on 21 November.

The EXCO also received an update on preparations for the CAF Strategy Conference, scheduled to hold in Sal, Cabo Verde, from 7 to 9 October.

The 2026 CAF Awards will bring together leading footballers, coaches, clubs and administrators to celebrate outstanding performances in African football.

The ceremony recognises achievements across men’s and women’s football, including the Player of the Year, Coach of the Year, Goalkeeper of the Year, Young Player of the Year and Club of the Year categories.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

Nigeria has enjoyed considerable success at the awards, particularly in the men’s and women’s Player of the Year categories.

Ademola Lookman won the men’s award in 2024, following Victor Osimhen’s triumph in 2023, making them the first Nigerian pair to secure consecutive victories in the category since Nwankwo Kanu and Victor Ikpeba achieved the feat in 1996 and 1997, respectively.

The 2024 ceremony, held in Marrakech, Morocco, also saw Nigeria’s Super Falcons named Women’s National Team of the Year, while goalkeeper Chiamaka Nnadozie received the Women’s Goalkeeper of the Year award.

At the 2025 edition held in Rabat, Morocco dominated the ceremony during a historic night in Rabat, with Achraf Hakimi (Morocco/Paris Saint-Germain) and Ghizlane Chebbak (Morocco/Al Hilal) winning the Men’s and Women’s Player of the Year awards, respectively.

Yassine Bounou (Morocco/Al Hilal) and Nigeria’s Chiamaka Nnadozie (Brighton & Hove Albion) claimed the Men’s and Women’s Goalkeeper of the Year honours, and Othmane Maamma (Morocco/Watford) and Doha El Madani (Morocco/AS FAR) were named Men’s and Women’s Young Players of the Year, respectively.

CAF approves new interclub regulations

Beyond the awards announcement, the EXCO approved significant changes to the regulations governing the CAF Champions League and CAF Confederation Cup.

Under the revised rules, players will be permitted to represent more than one club during a single CAF interclub season, a change that could provide clubs with greater flexibility in managing their squads.

The committee also approved an increase in the number of players clubs can register, setting the maximum at 40 players at any point during the season.

Clubs will additionally be allowed to replace four players during the final registration window, provided those players have not featured in any CAF interclub match during the season.

Another significant amendment concerns disciplinary proceedings. All disciplinary matters will now be referred to the CAF Disciplinary Board, removing that responsibility from the Interclub Committee.

The changes are expected to influence how clubs approach player recruitment, registration and squad management in continental competitions.

Women’s Champions League gets November dates

The EXCO also approved the dates for the 2026 CAF Women’s Champions League, with the final tournament scheduled to run from 1 to 15 November.

The competition, which brings together the leading women’s club sides from across Africa, has become a major platform for the development and visibility of women’s football on the continent.

Nigeria’s Edo Queen’s participation in this year’s competition is presently being challenged following the annulment of their victory at the WAFU B tournament after a protest by Ampem Dakoa.

Senegal to host Beach Soccer AFCON

In another decision, CAF confirmed that Senegal will host the 2026 Beach Soccer Africa Cup of Nations from 28 November to 6 December.

The West African country, which won the previous edition, will host the tournament as it seeks to defend its continental title.

World.title: Nigerian drugmaker Fidson selected to manufacture generic influenza antiviral under global licence
World.content:
A Nigerian pharmaceutical company, Fidson Healthcare Plc, has been selected to develop and manufacture a generic version of baloxavir marboxil, an antiviral medicine used to treat influenza.

The selection makes Fidson one of 11 manufacturers across nine countries chosen under a voluntary licensing agreement between the Medicines Patent Pool (MPP) and Swiss pharmaceutical company Roche.

The company disclosed this in a press release signed by its media contact, Tope Akindele. The MPP, a United Nations-backed public health organisation, also announced the sublicence agreements on 25 September.

The selected manufacturers are from Brazil, China, India, Indonesia, Malaysia, Nigeria, Uganda, Ukraine and Vietnam. The MPP said the arrangement is intended to “diversify supply pathways for influenza treatment, support regional production, and strengthen preparedness for future outbreaks and pandemics.”

What it means for Fidson, Nigeria

The selection makes Fidson one of the manufacturers that would develop, manufacture and supply generic versions of baloxavir in 129 countries covered by the licence, subject to regulatory authorisation.

The agreement also gives selected manufacturers access to technical data, reference products for bioequivalence studies and other support to facilitate product development and regulatory approval.

The MPP said it selected the manufacturers following an open Expression of Interest process and an assessment of their technical and regulatory capacities and commitment to producing quality-assured baloxavir products.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

The organisation said having manufacturers in different regions would help build production capacity closer to the populations the medicines are intended to serve and strengthen the resilience of global supply.

For Nigeria, the selection places a local pharmaceutical manufacturer in a global effort to expand production of an influenza antiviral while strengthening domestic and regional pharmaceutical manufacturing capacity.

Selection strengthens Africa’s role

Fidson’s Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer, Biola Adebayo, described the selection as a validation of the company’s commitment to quality-assured pharmaceutical manufacturing and innovation.

“Being selected by the Medicines Patent Pool as a sublicensee under the Roche-MPP voluntary licensing programme for baloxavir marboxil is both an honour and a validation of Fidson’s longstanding commitment to quality-assured pharmaceutical manufacturing, innovation, and improving healthcare outcomes,” Mr Adebayo said.

He said the partnership would allow the company to contribute to efforts to strengthen regional health security and preparedness for future health emergencies.

“As an African healthcare company, we are proud to contribute to global efforts aimed at strengthening regional health security, enhancing preparedness for future health emergencies, and ensuring that life-saving medicines reach the patients who need them most,” he said.

Mr Adebayo said the partnership also demonstrated the growing role of African manufacturers in the global health ecosystem.

He said Fidson would work with Roche, the MPP and other stakeholders to support broader access to baloxavir across eligible markets.

Part of pandemic preparedness

The announcement came as global leaders gathered in New York for the United Nations General Assembly to discuss pandemic prevention, preparedness and response.

The MPP said the licensing arrangement is designed to build manufacturing capacity before, rather than during, a health emergency.

Charles Gore, Executive Director of the MPP, said the organisation would work with the selected manufacturers on product development and regulatory approval, aiming to make quality-assured generic baloxavir available as quickly as possible.

“By combining global manufacturing capacity with regionally focused production, we are helping build a more geographically diverse and resilient supply base for the future,” Mr Gore said.

World.title: Court places restriction on Osun bank accounts
World.content:
The bank accounts of the Osun State Government have again been placed under restriction, some weeks after the Economic and Financial Crimes Commission (EFCC) lifted a freeze on some of the state’s accounts following President Bola Tinubu’s intervention.

Punch reported that the latest restriction followed an application by Gamji Nigeria Company Limited seeking to preserve funds belonging to the state over a $13.9 million arbitration award arising from water infrastructure projects in Ilesa West Local Government Area.

Judge Daniel Osiagor of the Federal High Court in Lagos in a suit marked FHC/L/CS/1233/2026, ordered commercial banks to place a “Post No Debit” restriction on the state government’s accounts.

The order covers funds up to $13.9 million and N157.5 million, pending the hearing and determination of Gamji’s motion on notice.

Affected banks include Guaranty Trust, Access Bank, First HoldCo, Zenith Bank, United Bank for Africa, Ecobank, Fidelity Bank, Stanbic IBTC, Sterling Bank, Union Bank and Wema Bank, among others.

The development comes about months after the EFCC restricted Osun government accounts during the build-up to the 15 August governorship election.

In that earlier case, the anti-graft agency restricted the state’s Federal Allocation Account domiciled with First Bank and two joint allocation accounts with Zenith Bank over an investigation into the alleged handling of about N11 billion in Ecology Funds, Intervention Funds and Federation Account Allocation Committee allocations.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

The EFCC said it acted after detecting what it described as suspicious movements of funds from the accounts, while the Osun government rejected the allegation and described the restriction as politically motivated.

The timing of that restriction became particularly controversial because it occurred 10 days before the governorship election, which Governor Ademola Adeleke contested on the platform of the Accord Party against the All Progressives Congress candidate, Bola Oyebamiji.

President Tinubu subsequently directed the EFCC to vacate the restriction, saying the timing of the action was capable of creating an impression that a federal agency was being used to interfere with the election. The accounts were eventually unfrozen on 22 August.

The latest restriction, however, is unrelated to the EFCC investigation.

Why the latest accounts were restricted

The latest case arose from two contracts awarded by the Osun State Government then led by former Governor Adegboyega Oyetola (the incumbent minster of marine and blue economy) to Gamji in June 2017 for water infrastructure works in Ilesa West.

One contract involved the construction of transmission mains and booster pump stations, while the second covered the construction of water reservoirs under a water supply and sanitation project.

According to court documents filed by Gamji, the projects were funded through an Islamic Development Bank loan facility facilitated by the Federal Ministry of Finance.

The original value of the first contract was $15.98 million, while the second was valued at $9.70 million.

Gamji said subsequent changes to engineering designs and variations in the scope of the works resulted in delays and increased project costs.

The company said the contract values were subsequently revised to $20.24 million for the first project and $10.95 million for the second.

Gamji further claimed that about 93 per cent of the work had been completed by October 2023 and that the Osun government issued a Substantial Completion Certificate on 14 November 2024.

Disagreements later emerged between the company and the state government over extensions of time, price adjustments and increased costs of materials and labour.

Gamji said its claims were rejected by the state government and that attempts to resolve the dispute through mediation failed.

The company subsequently issued an arbitration notice on 3 April 2025.

The state government accepted the arbitration process and nominated its arbitrator, leading to preliminary proceedings in Lagos on 15 May 2025.

According to Punch’s report, the arbitral panel eventually issued its final award on 24 July 2026, directing the Osun government to pay Gamji $13 million and N157.5 million in reimbursable arbitration fees.

READ ALSO: EFCC unfreezes Osun govt accounts after Tinubus directive

“A preservation order of interim injunction is granted directing the cited financial institutions in Nigeria to immediately place a Post No Debit restriction on the Respondent’s account domiciled with them for the preservation of the funds with them in the sum of $13,924,343.32 and N157,500,000.00 towards the liquidation of the Arbitral Award dated 24th July, 2026 which has become due and enforceable, pending the hearing and determination of the motion on notice,” the order read in part.

The award also provided for 20 per cent annual interest on any outstanding balance after the deadline for compliance.

Gamji told the court that the deadline expired on 24 August without payment of the awarded sums.

It subsequently approached the Federal High Court in Lagos seeking an order to preserve funds in the state government’s accounts pending enforcement of the award.

However, Judge Osiagor granted the interim application and directed the listed banks to place the accounts under “Post No Debit” restriction to preserve funds towards the liquidation of the arbitral award.

The order is interim and does not finally determine the substantive application before the court. The court adjourned the case until 22 October 2026 for hearing of the motion on notice.

The Osun State Government has yet to respond publicly to the court order.

World.title: NPFL Matchday 7: Rangers face derby test as Rivers United close in
World.content:
The Nigeria Premier Football League title race takes another intriguing turn this weekend, as Matchday 7 brings together title contenders, ambitious challengers, and clubs eager to improve their fortunes.

Rangers International have the biggest target on their backs after reclaiming top spot, but the defending champions face a potentially explosive South-East derby against Abia Warriors.

Just one point separates Rangers from unbeaten Rivers United, while Barau FC are also lurking with the same 12-point haul as Rivers.

And behind the leading pack, Enyimba’s emphatic 4-2 victory over Shooting Stars has finally given the Aba giants something to build on, while several clubs at the other end of the table are already feeling the pressure to turn promising performances into points.

With Kano Pillars and Sporting Lagos opening the weekend on Saturday, the rest of Matchday 7 serves up a nine-game Sunday programme that could significantly reshape the standings.

Rangers put top spot and South-East bragging Rights on the Line

Rangers return to action as league leaders, but there will be little room for complacency when they face Abia Warriors in Awka.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

The Flying Antelopes climbed back to the summit after a crucial 1-0 victory over Warri Wolves in their rescheduled midweek fixture.

It was exactly the response they needed after their previous defeat to Ikorodu City at the Mobolaji Johnson Arena.

Now comes another test, and this one carries the extra spice of a South-East derby, as Abia Warriors arrive with confidence after recording their first home victory of the campaign, a commanding 3-0 triumph over Bendel Insurance.

Imama Amapakabo’s side will believe they can trouble Rangers, particularly after ending their wait for a convincing result.

Recent meetings between the rivals underline how competitive this fixture has become. Rangers have won three of their last six encounters, Abia Warriors have won two, while one ended in a draw.

So while Rangers will be defending first place, Abia Warriors will be chasing much more than three points. This is a derby for momentum, pride and bragging rights.

Meanwhile, another subplot to Rangers’ challenge is that the club continues to play away from its traditional Nnamdi Azikiwe Stadium home because of renovation work.

Their home fixtures have already taken them to the MKO Abiola Stadium in Abeokuta and the Dan Anyiam Stadium in Owerri.

This time, the Awka Township Stadium provides the setting. That lack of a permanent home could potentially favour Abia Warriors, who will not have to contend with the intimidating atmosphere Rangers traditionally enjoy at the Cathedral in Enugu.

But Rangers have shown enough resilience to suggest they can overcome the inconvenience; more importantly, they now have the confidence of sitting at the top of the table.

Rivers United: Unbeaten, Second and running out of breathing space

If Rangers are under pressure to stay top, Rivers United are applying it from immediately behind.

The Pride of Rivers remain unbeaten after six matches, with three wins and three draws giving them 12 points, just one behind the leaders. But Sunday’s clash against Ikorodu City presents a different kind of challenge.

Rivers United have been forced into a demanding schedule, with the encounter against Ikorodu City coming after a quick succession of matches against Ranchers Bees and Katsina United.

Their latest outing produced a 1-1 draw against Katsina United at the Muhammadu Dikko Stadium, as Samson Olasupo put Rivers ahead after the break before former Rivers United midfielder Sani Mubarak’s deflected free-kick restored parity.

Now the Port Harcourt side must find enough energy to maintain their unbeaten start. At this stage of the season, dropping points is not necessarily disastrous.

But when Rangers are only one point ahead, every dropped point gives the leaders a little more breathing space.

With eight points from six matches, the Oga Boys have two wins, two draws and two defeats. A victory against Rivers United would be another major statement and could pull them closer to the leading group.

For Rivers, however, the objective is simple: protect their unbeaten record and keep Rangers within striking distance.

Enyimba finally find their spark

One of the biggest storylines away from the top two comes from Aba, where Enyimba finally got their campaign moving with a thrilling 4-2 victory over Shooting Stars.

For a club of Enyimba’s stature, the opening weeks of the season had been unusually frustrating as the nine-time NPFL champions have struggled badly for goals, points, and consistency. But the emphatic victory in Aba reminded everyone of what they can do when in full flow.

Now they face Plateau United at the Enyimba Stadium. The away side will not arrive merely to admire the surroundings. They come into the contest after beating Inter Lagos 2-0 and will be looking to build on that result.

For Enyimba, however, the challenge is bigger than simply winning another home game. They must prove the Shooting Stars victory was the beginning of a revival rather than an isolated flash of brilliance.

Barau FC looking to keep their unbeaten run alive

Another club demanding attention is Barau FC, as the newcomers have made an impressive start to life in the NPFL and sit among the leading pack after six matches without defeat.

Their next assignment is a trip to Bendel Insurance, who will be desperate for a response after the heavy 3-0 defeat to Abia Warriors.

It sets up an intriguing contest between a Barau side eager to preserve its momentum and an Insurance team determined to restore pride before its supporters.

For Barau, another positive result would further strengthen their credentials as early-season surprise packages.

Kano Pillars held by Sporting Lagos

Matchday 7 began on Saturday with Kano Pillars hosting Sporting Lagos at the Sani Abacha Stadium.

The encounter ended 1-1, with Valentine Ugwu putting Sporting Lagos ahead in first-half stoppage time before Abdullahi Musa equalised three minutes after the restart.

Both sides had chances to claim the points, but neither found a winner. The result extended Sporting Lagos’ unbeaten start and moved them onto eight points.

For Kano Pillars, however, the draw ended an impressive home run, with the Sai Masu Gida having won 10 of their previous 11 home matches before Sporting Lagos arrived.

Sporting Lagos will now turn their attention to Bendel Insurance, while Kano Pillars face another difficult assignment away to Shooting Stars.

The other Sunday battles

The weekend’s remaining fixtures provide their own storylines.

At Pantami Stadium, Doma United will host Warri Wolves, with both sides looking for a result that could change the direction of their campaigns.

In Ibadan, Shooting Stars face Nasarawa United, with the Oluyole Warriors seeking to bounce back from their heavy defeat to Enyimba.

Kwara United will host Ranchers Bees in Ilorin, while Niger Tornadoes welcome Kun Khalifat to Minna. Kun Khalifat arrive with confidence after their 1-0 victory over Kwara United and will look to build on it with another positive result.

In Lagos, Inter Lagos face Katsina United at the Mobolaji Johnson Arena, with the hosts seeking to convert home performances into points. And in Aba, Enyimba host Plateau United in a fixture that could tell us whether the People’s Elephant have genuinely turned the corner.

Matchday Seven could change the Picture

The beauty of the NPFL at this stage of the season is that the table remains open enough for one weekend to create major movement.

Rangers have the advantage at the top, but Rivers United are unbeaten and only one point behind. Barau FC are refusing to disappear from the conversation, while Enyimba are suddenly showing signs of life.

Below them, Ikorodu City, Sporting Lagos and several other clubs remain close enough to make a serious push with a run of positive results, making Sunday’s fixtures more than just another round of matches.

For Rangers, it is about protecting the top spot; for Rivers United, maintaining the pressure. While for the people’s Elephant in Aba, it is about proving their revival is real, and for Barau FC, it is about showing their unbeaten start is no fluke.

And for the teams struggling near the wrong end of the table, Matchday 7 is another opportunity to ensure the season does not begin slipping away.

The race is still wide open, and another dramatic chapter is waiting to be written.

World.title: Rev Dachomo in Israel, seeks audience with Netanyahu over killings
World.content:
Ezekiel Dachomo, a Reverend and regional leader of the Church of Christ in Nations (COCIN) in Barkin Ladi Local Government Area of Plateau State, has travelled to Israel as part of efforts to draw international attention to killings and insecurity in Plateau and other parts of Nigeria.

Mr Dachomo announced his arrival in Israel on Friday, October 2, on his Facebook account, describing the trip as his first international Christian advocacy tour.

Recent reports also show that he has been using the visit to pray for Nigeria, its leaders and communities affected by violence.

The cleric said he intends to use the visit to highlight attacks affecting communities in Plateau and the wider Middle Belt and seek an audience with Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu.

His stated programme also includes engagements with Christian leaders and prayer groups from different countries, whom he said he hopes to mobilise attention and prayers for Nigeria.

Mr Dachomo has repeatedly spoken publicly about attacks on communities in Plateau and described some of the violence as persecution and “genocide” against Christians.

Those descriptions are his characterisation of the violence and are not presented here as an established finding.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

In a message announcing his visit, the cleric said he was in Israel to pray for Nigeria, its leaders and its people.

“Today, I am in Israel praying for Nigeria, our leaders, and our people. I believe in miracles, and I believe God can change what looks impossible,” he said.

In a video accompanying his message, Mr Dachomo also said he had prayed for Israel, its people and its leadership, including Mr Netanyahu, his cabinet and the Israel Defence Forces.

He also prayed for President Bola Tinubu, Plateau State Governor Caleb Mutfwang and other African leaders.

The cleric said his advocacy would extend beyond Christian victims of violence, noting that Muslims and other Nigerians affected by insecurity also needed prayers and attention.

“I am coming to stand for Nigeria and to pray for our nation: for Muslims being killed in Zamfara, Kebbi, Sokoto and Katsina; for Christians; for my Biafran brothers,” he said.

Mr Dachomo also referred to attacks in his community and alleged that armed men had invaded his village and killed three people in his jurisdiction.

He said he hoped that, if granted a one-on-one meeting with Mr Netanyahu, he would present what he described as the suffering of Christian communities in Nigeria.

“By God’s grace, if we meet one-on-one in Israel, I will share with him the agony of Christians in Nigeria,” he said.

The Israel trip comes against the backdrop of Mr Dachomo’s sustained advocacy over insecurity in Plateau State.

He has been particularly vocal following attacks on communities in the state, including an attack in July in which he alleged that nine members of his extended family were killed in Riyom Local Government Area.

READ ALSO: Nicki Minaj shares prayer over killings in Plateau

PUNCH reported the allegation and Mr Dachomo’s subsequent public advocacy over the killings.

His latest initiative moves that advocacy beyond Nigeria, with the cleric seeking to engage international Christian groups and draw greater attention to the security challenges confronting communities in Plateau and other parts of the country.

Nigeria’s insecurity has affected communities across religious and ethnic lines, with terrorism, banditry, communal violence, farmer-herder conflicts and criminality among the factors cited in different parts of the country.

Claims concerning the identity of perpetrators, motives and the religious character of individual attacks therefore require independent verification.

For Mr Dachomo, the Israel visit represents an attempt to take his campaign for greater international attention to Plateau’s security crisis beyond Nigeria.

The outcome of his proposed engagements with Israeli officials and international Christian groups will determine the advocacy campaign’s international reach.

World.title: Amaechi incapable of earning a living outside public office, APC declares
World.content:
By Omeiza Ajayi

ABUJA: The ruling All Progressives Congress APC has declared that a former Governor of oil-rich Rivers State and vice-presidential candidate of the African Democratic Congress ADC, Rotimi Amaechi, is incapable of earning a living outside public office.

The declaration came two days after he told a television audience that President Bola Tinubu’s unfriendly economic policies killed his mother.

In a statement by its National Publicity Secretary, Felix Morka, the party on Sunday said Amaechi “must be a loafer, aimless and irresponsible for his inability to be productive and earn a living outside the patronage of public office.”

Amaechi had made the claim on Channels Television’s Politics Today last Friday. Asked whether he was directly attributing his mother’s death to Tinubu’s policies, he answered, “Of course.” He said his mother was healthy before Tinubu became President and that the rising cost of medicines later made it increasingly difficult for him to provide the drugs she needed. His mother, Mary Amaechi, died on July 16, 2026, at 89.

The APC statement did not however address his claim that government policy was to blame, but focused on his personal circumstances. “Rotimi Amaechi’s uncanny confessions must not be missed,” the party said. “First, he howled that he had become so broke and hungry that his wife was now feeding him. Now, he has stated that his inability to afford medications killed his mother at 89.

“For four decades, Rotimi Amaechi freeloaded at the highest levels of public office. He was never hungry and could afford medications for himself and his family. Just three years out of office, he has become destitute, unable to fend for himself and his loved ones,” the statement said.

It listed his record as a two-term Speaker of the Rivers State House of Assembly, two-term Governor, two-term Minister of Transportation and former presidential aspirant.

The APC added: “If Amaechi is not struggling with some kind of Peter Pan syndrome, then he must be a loafer, aimless and irresponsible for his inability to be productive and earn a living outside the patronage of public office.”

The party also accused him of using his vice presidential bid as a route back to public funds. “The same Rotimi Amaechi now asks Nigerians to make him vice president come 2027 so he can continue leeching on public treasury and keep the predatory lifestyle he has grown accustomed to,” it stated.

The statement had earlier opened with condolences to Amaechi over the death of his mother, Dame Ezinne Mary Oduah Amaechi and then offered a wish for Amaechi’a future. “The All Progressives Congress APC prays that the soul of Dame Ezinne Mary Oduah Amaechi continues to rest in perfect peace. Amen.

“It is our sincere wish that employers of labour in his hometown of Ubima in Ikwerre Local Government Area of Rivers State may find him suitable for a job that pays wages sufficient for him to feed and buy medications for himself and his beloved family the rest of his retirement. Amen.

“The presidency is not a soup kitchen, and will not be a soup kitchen for Rotimi Amaechi. There can be no better speaker of Rotimi Amaechi’s unfitness for the office of vice president than Rotimi Amaechi himself”, APC added, in rejection of Amaechi’s candidacy.

World.title: ‘APC’s cruel mockery of Amaechi can’t hide Tinubu’s misery’ — ADC PCC
World.content:
The African Democratic Congress (ADC) Presidential Campaign Council has criticised the All Progressives Congress (APC) over its response to former Rivers State governor Rotimi Amaechi’s reported difficulty in affording medication for his late mother.

Phrank Shaibu, Director of Strategic Communications of the ADC Presidential Campaign Council, described the APC statement signed by its National Publicity Secretary, Felix Morka, as “a display of political cruelty” and accused the ruling party of turning a family’s bereavement into partisan ridicule.

Shaibu stated this in a post on his X platform on Sunday.

He said Morka’s criticism of Amaechi missed the broader issue of Nigerians struggling to afford healthcare, food and other basic necessities.

“If Rotimi Amaechi says he struggled to afford his mother’s medication, the humane response is compassion. The political response is to ask why millions of Nigerians are also being priced out of medicines, food and basic necessities,” he said.

The ADC campaign spokesman also faulted Morka for describing Amaechi as a “loafer” over his alleged financial difficulties after leaving public office.

Shaibu said the comment was indicative of what he described as the APC’s attitude towards Nigerians facing economic hardship.

“Nigerians who cannot afford treatment, keep the lights on or travel safely on their roads are not loafers. They are citizens living through the consequences of a government that has failed them,” he said.

He criticised the Tinubu administration over the state of the economy, roads, electricity, security and public welfare, alleging that Nigerians were experiencing worsening hardship.

“The reality is plain: the roads are bad, the economy is bad, electricity is bad, security is bad and the welfare of the people is bad,” Shaibu said.

He challenged the APC to explain what he described as the poor condition of roads across the country, particularly in the South-East.

“Instead of sneering at Amaechi, Morka should explain why Nigerians face dangerous journeys on roads meant to connect communities and support trade,” he said.

Shaibu alleged that the condition of roads in parts of the South-East had made transportation increasingly difficult, and questioned how long Nigerians would continue to endure unsafe journeys.

He also criticised the Federal Government over public spending, arguing that increased expenditure had not translated into affordable healthcare, reliable electricity and safe roads for many Nigerians.

“The APC cannot boast about trillions in public spending while Nigerians lack safe roads, reliable electricity and affordable healthcare,” he said.

Shaibu said the performance of any government should be measured by whether citizens could live safely, access healthcare and earn decent livelihoods.

“The test of government is not how viciously its spokesmen can insult their opponents. It is whether people can live safely, afford treatment and earn a decent living,” he said.

He urged Morka to explain the Federal Government’s record to Nigerians, while calling for respect for Amaechi’s family during its period of bereavement.

Shaibu also linked the controversy to the 2027 general elections, urging Nigerians to use the election to determine the direction of the country.

“Nigerians owe themselves the resolve to make 2027 a turning point, so that the poverty and insecurity associated with Tinubu’s rule do not become the country’s future,” he said.

World.title: Sokoto spends N3.5bn on WAEC, NECO, NABTEB fees
World.content:
By Musa Ubandawaki, Sokoto

SOKOTO — The Sokoto State Government has disclosed that it spent about N3.5 billion in 2026 to pay registration and examination fees for students who sat for the West African Examinations Council (WAEC), National Examinations Council (NECO) and National Business and Technical Examinations Board (NABTEB) examinations across the state.

The Commissioner for Basic and Secondary Education, Prof. Ahmad Ala, represented by the Permanent Secretary of the ministry, Dr Sanusi Aliyu Binji, disclosed this at an education support programme in Sokoto.

Ala said the expenditure was part of the state government’s efforts to remove financial barriers preventing indigent students from participating in critical public examinations.

He said, “The government’s decision to shoulder the registration and examination fees is aimed at ensuring that no child is denied the opportunity to sit for these examinations because of financial constraints.”

The commissioner also disclosed that the state recorded an 80 per cent pass rate in the 2026 examinations, describing the performance as an indication of the potential for improved educational outcomes when students and schools receive adequate institutional and financial support.

According to him, the result underscored the importance of sustained investment in education, noting that government alone could not bear the responsibility of improving learning outcomes and infrastructure across the state.

Ala therefore appealed to corporate organisations, philanthropists, development partners and other stakeholders to complement government efforts by investing in schools, learning materials, infrastructure and other initiatives aimed at improving the quality of education.

Also speaking, the Executive Chairman of the Sokoto State Universal Basic Education Board (SUBEB), Alhaji Umar Nagwari Tambuwal, represented by the Director of Mobilisation, Hajiya Rabi Muhammad Gwadabawa, commended the initiative, particularly its focus on providing direct support to schools and learners.

Similarly, the District Head of Gagi, Alhaji Sani Umar Jabbi, described education as the foundation for sustainable socio-economic development and urged individuals, organisations and institutions to support initiatives aimed at strengthening the education system.

Jabbi said, “Funding education must be a collective responsibility. Our youths are the future leaders of this country, and they deserve access to quality education that will equip them to confront the challenges of tomorrow.”

He described education as an important tool for addressing poverty, unemployment, insecurity and other social challenges, and called for sustained investment in the sector by the federal, state and local governments.

The programme also highlighted the role of public-private partnerships in strengthening Nigeria’s education system, particularly amid rising costs of education and learning materials.

In a vote of thanks, the Secretary of Sokoto South Local Government, Comrade Kabiru Aliyu Minanata, appreciated Pinnacle Hotel and other stakeholders for supporting the initiative.

He described their intervention as an example of how private organisations could complement government efforts to build a stronger and more inclusive education system.

World.title: APC knocks Amaechi over claim he couldn’t afford mother’s drugs
World.content:
The All Progressives Congress (APC) has criticised former Rivers State governor and African Democratic Congress (ADC) vice-presidential candidate, Rotimi Amaechi, over his reported claim that he could not afford medication for his late mother before her death at the age of 89.

In a statement issued in Abuja on Sunday by its National Publicity Secretary, Felix Morka, the APC questioned Amaechi’s financial circumstances after leaving public office and criticised his decision to seek the vice-presidential ticket of the ADC ahead of the 2027 general elections.

The party began the statement by commiserating with Amaechi over the death of his mother, Dame Ezinne Mary Oduah Amaechi, and praying for the former minister’s wellbeing.

It, however, swiftly turned to a criticism of Amaechi’s reported comments about his financial difficulties.

The APC said it was its “sincere wish” that employers in Amaechi’s hometown of Ubima, Ikwerre Local Government Area of Rivers State, would find him suitable employment that could provide sufficient income for his needs.

The party recalled an earlier statement attributed to Amaechi in which he reportedly said he had become financially constrained to the extent that his wife was now supporting him.
