The APC said his latest claim about being unable to afford his mother’s medication raised questions about his financial position after leaving public office.

“Rotimi Amaechi’s uncanny confessions must not be missed. First, he howled that he had become so broke and hungry that his wife was now feeding him. Now, he has stated that his inability to afford medications killed his mother at 89,” Morka said.

The party also questioned Amaechi’s ability to sustain himself outside public office, citing his long career in government.

Amaechi served as Speaker of the Rivers State House of Assembly, governor of the state and Minister of Transportation, and was also a presidential aspirant before emerging as the ADC’s vice-presidential candidate.

The APC alleged that his comments suggested he had become financially dependent after leaving government, describing the situation in strongly worded terms.

It further criticised Amaechi for seeking the vice-presidential position in 2027, alleging that his objective was to return to access to public resources.

“The same Rotimi Amaechi now asks Nigerians to make him vice president come 2027 so he can continue leeching on public treasury and keep the predatory lifestyle he has grown accustomed to,” the party said.

The APC declared that the presidency should not be treated as a means of providing financial support to political office holders.

“The presidency is not a soup kitchen, and will not be a soup kitchen for Rotimi Amaechi,” Morka said.

The party concluded by questioning Amaechi’s suitability for the vice-presidential position, saying his own reported statements had raised questions about his readiness for the office.

“There can be no better speaker of Rotimi Amaechi’s unfitness for the office of vice president than Rotimi Amaechi himself,” the APC said.

World.title: ‘Killing farmers attacks Nigeria’s food security’ — Kyari
World.content:
Senator Abubakar Kyari, Minister of Agriculture and Food security

By Gabriel Ewepu

ABUJA — Minister of Agriculture and Food Security, Senator Abubakar Kyari, has condemned the killing of 15 farmers in Marte Local Government Area of Borno State by suspected terrorists, describing the attack as a threat to Nigeria’s food security.

Kyari, in a statement on Sunday, said the victims were killed while working on their farms to earn a living and contribute to the nation’s food supply.

He said, “I am deeply saddened and outraged by the tragic killing of 15 farmers in Marte Local Government Area of Borno State by suspected terrorists.

“These innocent Nigerians lost their lives while working on their farms to earn a living and contribute to the food security of our nation.

“I extend my heartfelt condolences to the families of the victims, the people of Marte, His Excellency the Executive Governor Prof. Babagana Umara Zulum CON, FNSE, FNIAE mni, the Government and people of Borno State.

“I pray that Almighty Allah grant the deceased eternal rest and comfort their families.

“The killing of farmers is not only an attack on innocent lives and livelihoods, but also on our collective efforts to achieve food security.”

The minister assured farmers of the Federal Government’s commitment to creating a safe environment for agricultural activities under President Bola Tinubu’s Renewed Hope Agenda.

According to him, protecting farmers and farming communities remains critical to achieving national food security.

He commended security agencies for their efforts to protect farming communities and urged them to intensify operations to apprehend those responsible for the killings.

Kyari also called for efforts to locate the three persons reportedly still missing following the attack.

“Protecting our farmers is protecting Nigeria’s food security,” he said.

He prayed for continued protection for farmers, rural communities and the country.

“May Almighty Allah continue to protect our farmers, rural communities and our nation,” the minister added.

World.title: Nigeria cannot progress on ‘voodoo governance’ — Bakare
World.content:
Public affairs analyst and All Progressives Congress (APC) chieftain, Otunba Lukman Taiwo Bakare, has urged Nigerians to look beyond short-term consumer relief and support economic reforms and infrastructure development, saying the country cannot achieve sustainable growth through what he described as “voodoo style of governance.”

Bakare, while assessing Nigeria’s socio-economic development ahead of the 2027 general elections, argued that the country’s economic challenges could not be resolved through the return of fuel and foreign exchange subsidies.

He said Nigeria’s relatively strong currency and lower cost of living in the 1970s and early 1980s were largely products of higher domestic production and exports rather than government subsidies.

“When Nigerians were buying things cheap in the 70s and early 80s, that comfort was not because we were subsidising forex. It was as a result of hard work,” Bakare said.

He recalled that Nigeria was then a major producer of cocoa, palm oil and groundnuts, adding that the country produced much of the food it consumed and had local manufacturing and vehicle assembly capacity.

He argued that sustained currency strength required increased domestic production and export capacity, rather than continued government intervention through subsidies.

Infrastructure over consumption

Bakare criticised successive administrations over their handling of the country’s resources, particularly the use of public funds to subsidise consumption rather than invest in infrastructure and productive sectors.

Comparing the administrations of former President Goodluck Jonathan and former President Muhammadu Buhari, he cited changes in Nigeria’s foreign reserves as part of his argument.

According to him, Nigeria’s foreign reserves stood at about $43 billion in 2010 but fell to about $29 billion by May 2015.

He contrasted this with what he described as an increase in reserves to about $36 billion by May 2023 under Buhari, despite the economic recessions and COVID-19 pandemic experienced during the period.

Bakare criticised the Jonathan administration, alleging that it failed to invest sufficiently in roads, agriculture and power infrastructure.

“Jonathan didn’t build roads that would make transportation cheaper. He didn’t invest in agriculture that would make food cheaper and our export larger. He didn’t invest in power that would improve our manufacturing sector,” he said.

He accused the administration of using foreign reserves to support fuel and foreign exchange subsidies, as well as imports.

Bakare also highlighted infrastructure projects associated with the Buhari administration, including the Lagos-Ibadan Standard Gauge Railway, Lagos-Ibadan Expressway reconstruction and the Second Niger Bridge.

The Buhari administration itself listed the Lagos-Ibadan rail project and the Second Niger Bridge among its major infrastructure projects.

Bakare also cited the Bodo-Bonny Road and Bridges Project in Rivers State and support for the development of the Dangote Petroleum Refinery as examples of investments he believes could contribute to long-term economic development.

“You praised Jonathan’s government for selling cheap imported rice that you consumed, but you insulted Buhari who built the best railway in Africa,” he said.

Tinubu reforms

On the 2027 elections, Bakare defended President Bola Tinubu’s economic policies, describing the reforms as necessary steps to address what he considered longstanding structural weaknesses in the economy.

He particularly cited major road projects, including the Lagos-Calabar Coastal Highway and the proposed Badagry-Sokoto Superhighway, as initiatives that could improve transportation and facilitate the movement of agricultural produce.

Bakare rejected calls by opposition politicians for a return to fuel subsidies, arguing that the cost would place additional pressure on the country’s finances.

“How can any sensible person be talking about subsidy returns in a country with a $37 billion budget and still having a $10 billion budget deficit and you want to add over $10 billion fuel subsidy?” he asked.

He acknowledged concerns over rising food prices and the hardship being experienced by Nigerians but argued that improving roads and other transportation infrastructure was necessary to strengthen agricultural distribution.

“Without road you can’t even have food to eat, because how can food get to your destination without good roads? Our farmers lost most of their harvest because of lack of good roads,” he said.

‘Hold government accountable’

Bakare urged Nigerians to demand accountability from government officials over the delivery of infrastructure projects, rather than focusing exclusively on immediate consumer benefits.

He specifically called for regular updates on highway projects from the Minister of Works, David Umahi, including visual evidence of progress.

The APC chieftain warned against abandoning ongoing structural reforms after the 2027 elections, arguing that sustainable development required continuity and effective implementation.

“No country develops with magic; you must pass through due process to build a nation. Stop looking for miraculous achievements from any government because it will never happen,” Bakare said.

“Nigeria must get it right through reforms and perfect implementation.”

World.title: 2027: Fani-Kayode, Atiku’s aide clash over ‘Bola’
World.content:
Former Minister of Aviation, Femi Fani-Kayode, and the media adviser to former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar, Paul Ibe, have traded words over Atiku’s decision to repeatedly refer to President Bola Tinubu as “Bola” in his October 1 Independence Day address.

Fani-Kayode, in a post on his Facebook page on Sunday, accused Atiku of disrespecting the office of the President, describing the former vice-president’s speech as “intellectually-flawed, highly disrespectful” and lacking “decency, logic and rationality.”

He said Atiku deliberately refused to address Tinubu as “President”, choosing instead to repeatedly call him by his first name.

“Surely this level of pettiness is below even you. Yet despite this provocation I will not refer to you as ‘Kachalla’ and I will accord you the respect that I still think you deserve,” Fani-Kayode wrote.

He cited comments by Akin Osuntokun, a former Special Adviser on Politics to former President Olusegun Obasanjo and former Director-General of the Peter Obi Presidential Campaign Organisation, who had also criticised Atiku’s use of Tinubu’s first name.

Fani-Kayode said Osuntokun was right to demand “decorum and decency” in addressing the President, arguing that Atiku’s conduct was inconsistent with the respect expected of a former vice-president.

The former minister subsequently raised several past political controversies involving Atiku, including his relationship with Obasanjo during their tenure as president and vice-president between 1999 and 2007.

Fani-Kayode also criticised Atiku’s comments about former President Goodluck Jonathan, his exchange with Vice-President Kashim Shettima and his handling of the 2022 killing of Deborah Samuel in Sokoto.

He alleged that Atiku’s political conduct demonstrated a lack of respect, restraint and loyalty, and accused him of being driven primarily by his ambition to become president.

Fani-Kayode further referred to comments attributed to former Rivers State governor Rotimi Amaechi, who he said had recently questioned Atiku’s electability and ability to offer anything new.

He concluded by warning that Atiku’s refusal to show respect for the presidential office could hurt his ambition to occupy it.

Responding, Ibe dismissed Fani-Kayode’s criticism as a distraction from the substantive issues raised by Atiku in his Independence Day address.

In a statement posted on his social media platforms, Ibe said Atiku had committed no offence by referring to Tinubu as “Bola”.

“His name is Bola. And that is not Nigeria’s problem,” Ibe said.

According to him, Nigerians were more concerned about the cost of living, insecurity and rising food, transport and energy costs than the form of address used for the President.

“Nigeria is a republic, not a monarchy. The President is an elected public servant, not an emperor before whom opponents must genuflect,” he said.

Ibe argued that “President” was the title of an office and not a requirement that should shield its occupant from criticism.

He also accused Fani-Kayode of contradicting his own call for decorum by using harsh descriptions against political opponents in his response.

“You lecture Atiku about ‘decency’, ‘decorum’ and ‘restraint’, yet your essay calls people ‘pit bull terriers’, ‘hungry wolves’, ‘fallen angels’ and sufferers of ‘pathological obsession’,” Ibe said.

He also referred to previous controversies involving Fani-Kayode, including his confrontation with a Daily Trust journalist and allegations made against him by his estranged wife, stressing that some of the matters remained contested.

On Atiku’s relationship with Obasanjo, Ibe said political disagreement should not be equated with treason, arguing that Atiku was the vice-president and not a subordinate without political rights.

He also described the alleged account of Obasanjo kneeling before Atiku during their political dispute as contested history, saying Atiku had denied it.

“On the claim that Obasanjo knelt before Atiku, Atiku has denied it, while others have offered a different account. It remains disputed history. You may choose your version, but you cannot manufacture certainty,” Ibe said.

On Atiku’s comments about Jonathan, Ibe said the former vice-president was entitled to assess the former president’s preparedness for office, adding that criticism should not automatically be interpreted as disrespect.

He also defended Atiku over the controversy surrounding the killing of Deborah Samuel, saying the deleted social media post had been published without Atiku’s approval.

Ibe said Atiku subsequently condemned the killing and made it clear that Islam provided no justification for taking another person’s life outside due process.

Turning to the 2027 election, Ibe said Nigerians would ultimately judge the Tinubu administration on the impact of its policies on their lives rather than on the manner in which Atiku addressed the President.

He asked whether food, petrol and electricity had become more affordable, whether Nigerians were safer, and whether incomes and businesses had improved under Tinubu.

“Those are the questions that matter,” Ibe said.

“It is easier to debate ‘Bola’ versus ‘Mr President’ than to defend what Bola’s policies have done to Nigerians.

“In 2027, Nigerians will vote on food, petrol, electricity, jobs, insecurity, the naira and their quality of life — not forms of address.”

World.title: How bus driver nearly landed in jail after accepting ‘energy drink’ parcel
World.content:
NDLEA

A commercial bus driver nearly landed in jail after accepting a bottle of energy drink as a waybill package in Lagos for delivery to Ondo State, only for the National Drug Law Enforcement Agency, NDLEA, to discover that it contained illicit drugs.

NDLEA Director of Media and Advocacy, Femi Babafemi, said the bottle was used to conceal Colos and methamphetamine.

The driver, who was unaware of the contents, spent some time in custody before operatives traced and arrested the person who gave him the package.

Babafemi said the driver was fortunate that the person behind the package was identified, warning that others may not be as lucky.

“He may be lucky to have escaped gaol because officers who made the discovery were able to track and arrest the person who gave him the package, your own case may be devoid of such luck and you go in for it,” he said.

The NDLEA spokesman urged commercial drivers and other transport workers to avoid accepting parcels whose contents they cannot verify, stressing that possession of illicit drugs can make the person carrying them legally liable.

“As drivers or whoever, please avoid taking parcels you don’t know its content because possession makes you culpable, that’s the law and you go explain tire!” Babafemi added.

Vanguard News

World.title: Corporal Punishment Ban: Stakeholders Seek Clearer Discipline Framework, More Counsellors
World.content:
Funmi Ogundare

Stakeholders in the education sector weekend called for a comprehensive review of school discipline frameworks, stronger parental involvement and increased deployment of guidance counsellors to help schools manage student misconduct following the ban on corporal punishment.

They made the call at the Lagos State school discipline policy roundtable organised by the Ajoke Ayisat Afolabi Foundation (AAAF), with support from SIFAX Group, in Lagos.

The roundtable, themed, ‘Assessing the Impact of Banning Corporal Punishment on Discipline in Schools: Exploring Alternative Strategies for Managing Student Misconduct’, brought together policymakers, educators, students, civil society organisations and other stakeholders.

The event also formed part of activities marking International Teachers’ Day and featured the recognition of outstanding teachers in Lagos State following AAAF’s statewide nomination exercise.

They include Mrs. Modupe Odumade of Ijaye Ojokoro Senior High School, who emerged as the highest-ranked teacher, followed by Mrs. ThankGod Priscilla, Mrs Ramota Balogun, Mr. Akinola Oluwatobi and James Mary Omolade.

The stakeholders called for increased recruitment of guidance counsellors, specialised teacher training and stronger collaboration among parents, schools and government agencies.

They agreed that sustainable reform of school discipline in Lagos required shared responsibility among government, schools, parents, civil society organisations and students.

According to them, “There is a need for clearer disciplinary procedures, stronger safeguarding mechanisms and sustained stakeholder engagement to ensure that school discipline promotes accountability while protecting the dignity and rights of learners.”

Participants agreed that although the ban on corporal punishment was consistent with child protection principles, schools needed clearer operational guidelines, stronger institutional support and effective alternatives for addressing behavioural challenges.

A statewide policy review conducted by AAAF across the five divisions of Lagos State provided a major focus of the discussions.

The study involved 451 students, 42 school leaders and teachers, while 150 students participated in focus group discussions across 15 schools.

Presenting the findings, the researchers said that while most students surveyed considered discipline in their schools to be relatively good, many educators expressed concerns about inadequate guidance on disciplinary alternatives following the ban on corporal punishment.

The report identified gaps in policy implementation, teacher capacity, institutional support and stakeholder engagement.

It recommended greater clarity in disciplinary policies, continuous teacher training, the development of school-level disciplinary frameworks, stronger parental participation and periodic reviews of discipline policies to reflect emerging realities.

The study also proposed structured escalation procedures for dealing with offences, with disciplinary measures made proportionate to the nature and severity of misconduct.

In his remarks, Chairman of SIFAX Group and Chairman, Board of Trustees of AAAF, Dr. Taiwo Afolabi, who was represented by the Deputy Director, Strategy and Operations of the organisation, Oliver Omajuwa, said discipline remained fundamental to educational success and national development.

Declaring the roundtable opened, he stated that the discussion was not merely about policy but about safeguarding children’s future, strengthening teachers’ confidence and building a society anchored on responsibility and character.

He said schools should be environments where children could learn in safety and teachers could teach with dignity, adding that discipline should promote character, responsibility and growth rather than fear and resentment.

He urged stakeholders to approach the issue with open minds and develop practical solutions that would place the best interests of children at the centre of educational reforms.

Lagos State Commissioner for Basic and Secondary Education, Jamiu Tolani Ali-Balogun, said discipline begins at home, arguing that many behavioural challenges confronting schools reflected wider societal problems.

He stated that while government policies were important, their effective implementation depended largely on cooperation among parents, schools and communities.

He expressed concern over what he described as a growing disconnect between parents and schools, noting that some parents failed to respond when invited to discuss behavioural concerns involving their children.

“We must create society first. It is not just about policy. Parents are critical to discipline,” he said, urging families to take greater responsibility for the moral upbringing of their children.

Also speaking, Executive Secretary of the Lagos State Domestic and Sexual Violence Agency, Lola Vivour-Adeniyi, explained that corporal punishment often failed to produce lasting behavioural change.

She advocated disciplinary approaches based on communication, guidance and accountability, describing physical punishment as a lazy approach that could create fear without necessarily developing character.

Participants also identified emerging challenges requiring new approaches to school discipline, including social media influence, changing family structures, peer pressure, mental health concerns and neurodiversity.

They stressed the need to equip teachers with the knowledge and skills required to understand and respond appropriately to these realities.

Students who participated in AAAF’s essay competition on school discipline also contributed to the debate, challenging stakeholders to move away from traditional punitive approaches towards strategies that develop character, responsibility and self-control.

The winner of the competition, Olachiwa Sharon Iwala, said true discipline should enable children to make responsible choices even when no authority figure was present.

She advocated guidance and counselling, restorative justice measures and clear disciplinary codes as alternatives to physical punishment.

Another student speaker, Anuoluwa Mudahiru, urged policymakers to move beyond the debate over whether teachers should flog students, arguing that greater attention should be given to building a school system capable of producing disciplined, responsible and self-motivated young people.

World.title: Sacrifices of Our Fallen Heroes ‘ll Not Be in Vain, Says Naval Spokesperson
World.content:
*As widows of fallen personnel appeal to corporate organisations for support for families

Linus Aleke in Abuja

The Director of Naval Information, Navy Captain Abiodun Folorunsho, has said that the Armed Forces of Nigeria (AFN) is working hard to ensure that those left behind by troops who died in active service are not neglected, assuring them that: “We will not allow the sacrifices of our fallen heroes to be in vain.”

This comes as the widows of fallen heroes appealed to corporate organisations and foundations to support the families of fallen military personnel, particularly widows and children who continue to face financial and social challenges following the loss of their breadwinners.

The widows made the appeal during the Military Widows Outreach Programme, organised by the Military Widow Support Initiative (MWSI) at the Naval Base Abuja Parade Ground on Saturday.

Speaking at the outreach programme, the Naval spokesperson, Captain Folorunsho, said the initiative was established to complement the support already provided by the Armed Forces of Nigeria.

He said there was no way the Armed Forces, as an institution, could bridge the huge gap alone.

According to him, “We thought it wise to pull funds from our sponsors to see how we can also add to what the military is already doing for them. A number of these people are the true warriors; they are the true heroes because it is they who are really paying the sacrifice.

“It is because of them that we can do what we are doing. Their spouses and children have had to pay the ultimate price so that Nigeria can be won.

“So, yes, we started this three years ago, just pulling funds, personal funds from us and from some of our friends, to assist these widows to adequately cater for their families.

“We will not allow the sacrifices of our fallen heroes to be in vain.”

Speaking during the empowerment programme, Mrs Olubunmi Oni, whose husband, the late Major S. Oni, who died in active service in Niger State in 2023, said widows of fallen heroes continued to face significant challenges.

She said: “We would really appreciate it if a lot of organisations, NGOs and foundations could continue to reach out to fallen heroes’ wives and children, help them with their academics through scholarships, and help the wives get jobs and empowerment for their businesses.

“So, this would also make us happy and help us know that we are not alone in this and that our husbands did not die for nothing.”

Lamenting the difficulties some widows face in accessing the benefits of their deceased husbands from the relevant authorities, Mrs Oni said such issues should also be addressed.

“These are things that should also be looked into so that course mates and friends of the late officer or soldier can also assist these women in accessing their benefits,” she said.

Another widow, Mrs Ibrahim Adeze, appealed to the government and corporate organisations to create employment opportunities for young widows of fallen heroes to enable them to provide for their families.

“I would appreciate it if they could give them jobs to do, enlighten them about available schemes or train them so that they can become economically independent.

“Another thing they can do to help the widows is to ensure that they are not misled by bad elements by making sure that, after the training, they are properly mentored. This will help ensure that the skills and training they receive enable them to stabilise their homes,” she said.

The programme brought together 500 widows of military personnel who paid the supreme price in service to the nation, with interventions focused on welfare support, empowerment and strengthening the economic resilience of beneficiaries.

The widows called for sustained support in areas such as education, healthcare, skills acquisition, housing and other forms of assistance that could improve the welfare and livelihoods of affected families.

They also urged well-meaning individuals, corporate organisations, foundations and other stakeholders to partner with relevant government agencies and associations to provide sustainable interventions for the families of fallen heroes.

World.title: NAFDAC DG Seeks Foreign Partners’ Support For Local Vaccine Production
World.content:
Onyebuchi Ezigbo in Abuja

The Director General of the National Agency for Food and Drug Administration and Control (NAFDAC), Prof. Mojisola Adeyeye, has solicited the support of international partners to establish vaccine manufacturing facilities in Nigeriia.

She said that opening vaccine manufacturing companies will hasten the push by the agency to attain World Health Organisation (WHO) Maturity Level 4 for vaccine lot release.

Adeyeye made the call at the 8th Nigeria Pharma Manufacturers’ Expo in Lagos, jointly organised by the Pharmaceutical Manufacturing Group of Manufacturers Association of Nigeria (PMG-MAN) and PGE Expo Pvt Ltd.

A statement signed by NAFDAC’s Resident Media Consultant Sanyo Akintola said that the DG acknowledged the continued support of international partners in NAFDAC’s attainment of Maturity Level 3, and challenged them to contribute to fill-and-finish modular vaccine manufacturing.

According to Adeyeye, NAFDAC has nine functions to meet for full benchmarking for medicines and vaccines, but has only been benchmarked in eight, with lot release for vaccines outstanding.

“We want to call on our international partners that have been of tremendous help. Without them we wouldn’t have been here. I want to challenge them to contribute to fill and finish modular vaccine manufacturing so that we can get our vaccine lot release,” she said.

Adeyeye said Nigeria has what it takes to attain the level except local vaccine manufacturing, adding that the cost has been estimated and will not be too high. “We cannot afford to go back to where we used to be,” she said.

Recalling that Nigeria used to manufacture vaccines, Adeyeye said it is time to return to local production.

She commended President Bola Tinubu for the Executive Order 2024, describing it as game-changing and bringing life to NAFDAC’s clamour for incentives for local manufacturers operating under harsh conditions.

“I was championing incentives for the manufacturers until President Tinubu came on board with the Executive Order of 2024,” she said, noting that both the Coordinating Minister of Health and Minister of State bought into the rationale leading to unlocking the healthcare value chain.

She said NAFDAC’s Good Manufacturing Practice (GMP) Roadmap audit of over 165 companies, funded by USAID and executed by United States Pharmacopeia, led to improved quality and 70 per cent decrease in import of products under the ‘5 plus 5’ and Ceiling Initiatives between 2021 and 2025.

She also said that NAFDAC became a member of International Medical Device Forum in 2023 while, its Yaba laboratory became WHO pre-qualified in September 2023, and it became the first agency in sub-Saharan Africa to be successfully re-benchmarked for Maturity Level 3.

In his remarks, Chairman of PMG-MAN, Mr. Oluwatosin Jolayemi, described the expo as only complete pharma manufacturing platform in Central and West Africa and commended Adeyeye for driving international best practices.

He called for the extension of the presidential executive order by two years at expiration in March 2027, saying medicine security requires policy consistency.

No fewer than 132 companies from US, China, Argentina, Egypt, India, Rwanda, Austria, UAE, France, Germany, Indonesia and Nigeria participated in the two-day expo.

World.title: Shettima Arrives Katsina to Inaugurate 11.2km Roads, Launch 230 Mass Transit Vehicles
World.content:
Francis Sardauna in Katsina

Vice-President Kashim Shettima has arrived in Katsina State for a one-day official visit during which he is expected to inaugurate 11.2 kilometres of road projects and launch 230 mass transit vehicles.

The vice-president, who was received by Governor Dikko Umaru Radda on arrival at the Umaru Musa Yar’Adua Airport, Katsina, also inspected a quarter guard mounted by the personnel of the Nigerian Air Force.

During the visit, Shettima is scheduled to inaugurate three major road projects executed by Governor Radda’s administration.

The projects include the dualised 4.80-kilometre Kofar Sauri–Central Mosque Roundabout Road; the dualised 2.40-kilometre Central Police Station Junction–Kofar Kaura Underpass Road; and the newly constructed 4.00-kilometre Filin Polo–Ring Road.

The vice-president will also launch 30 CNG hybrid buses and 200 Phase I electric tricycles at the Old Ministry of Works as part of efforts to strengthen mass transportation in the state.

Shettima is further expected to receive new defectors into the All Progressives Congress (APC) at a political gathering at the Peoples Square, Government House, Katsina.

At the time of filing this report, the vice-president was at the Muhammadu Dikko Stadium, Katsina, where he was flagging off the Community Investment Fund under the Nigeria for Women Programme Scale-Up (NFWP-SU).

The World Bank-supported initiative focused on supporting women’s economic empowerment and financial inclusion in the state.

Among those who joined Governor Radda to receive the vice-president were the Emir of Katsina, Alhaji Abdulmumini Kabir Usman, members of the State Executive Council and other top government officials

World.title: Ndume Lauds Tinubu For Increase In Military Personnel Salary
World.content:
Folalumi Alaran in Abuja

A member of the National Assembly, Senator Ali Ndume, has hailed President Bola Tinubu for making good his pledge to increase the salary of Armed Forces personnel.

The former Senate Leader thumbed up the president in a release issued at the weekend.

Reacting to the increase in the salary of both officers and men of the three services which took effect from September 2026, the ranking senator praised Tinubu for walking his talks and urged him to continue to do everything necessary to boost the morale of personnel of the Nigerian military.

He however tasked military personnel to redouble their efforts in combating insurgency, kidnapping and banditry.

The former Chairman of the Senate Committee on Army maintained that in the last three years, the present government has shown commitment to curbing insecurity by taking proactive initiatives in terms of financing to procure adequate arms and ammunition and doing everything necessary to boost the morale of the Armed Forces personnel.

His words: “Making a pronouncement is one thing, redeeming your pledge is a different ball game entirely.

“President Tinubu has shown times without number that he keeps to his words. It is heartwarming to note that the salary increment he promised the Nigerian Army has been redeemed.

“I want to urge our officers to redouble their efforts to curtail insecurity since the present administration is doing everything to boost their morale. They should do more now that they also have more troops on the ground with the recent recruitment.

“The activation of the Army Aviation would also go a long way in complementing the efforts of the Air Force now that we also have attack helicopters in the six geo-political zones.”

Ndume reiterated his appeal for better, coordinated synergy between the infantry and the Air Force in the war against insurgency and banditry.

The Presidency had last month issued an official statement with a commitment to commence implementation of new salary package for certain categories of Armed Forces personnel.

According to a statement attributed to presidential spokesperson, Bayo Onanuga,

officers above the rank of colonel, including brigadier generals, major generals, lieutenant generals and generals, would receive a 30 percent salary increase.

He also added that personnel from lieutenant colonel down to warrant officer would get a 50 per cent increase, while those from private to staff sergeant would receive an 80 per cent increase.

The presidential aide, who said the new package would raise the annual salary bill for armed forces personnel from N660 billion to N924 billion, declared that over 250,000 personnel of the Nigerian Armed Forces would be beneficiaries..

World.title: 2027: ADP’ ill Offer Alternative Platform for Kwarans, Says Chieftain
World.content:
Hammed Shittu in Ilorin

Kwara South senatorial candidate on the platform of the African Democratic Party (ADP), Alhaji Abdullahi Mohammed, has said the party is well positioned to serve as an alternative platform capable of addressing various challenges facing the people of the state and bring government closer to the people come 2027.

Speaking with journalists in Ilorin weekend, Mohammed said the state is blessed with both human and natural resources that can be tapped for the overall socio economic well being of the residents if it is well managed for the benefit of the residents.

He said the ADP has a blueprint to address issues such as high cost of living, low agricultural development, persistent insecurity and poor micro, small and medium entrepreneurship growth.

Mohammed, who hails from Balogun Ward in Offa, Kwara South district, urged the electorate to shift focus from the two main political parties in the state, saying that ADP has a lot to offer to better lives of the people.

He stated: “One problem we’re having here is this focus on the two major political parties. The people have refused to see alternative in many other platforms that can be used for political emancipation. Interestingly, the two don’t have clear cut agenda or manifesto for the masses.”

The senatorial candidate, who condemned lack of continuity in projects and policies among successive governments in the state, said that people had suffered consequences of such actions.

“If the ADP is given the opportunity to serve Kwara, people will see a lot of difference in governance and even spread of projects to the three senatorial districts in the state, because our main objective is to assist the poor people, empower them by creating opportunity for them to grow.

“For instance, if you are good in engineering, it’s the responsibility of the government to assist those who are in engineering sector. If you are a farmer, the government should assist the farmers and provide enabling environment for them to plant many food and cash crops. At least to assist the people in the state,” he said.

Mohammed, who lamented low school enrolment in the Kwara South district, said that successive administration had neglected educational development among the people.

“There is a large population of our people in entrepreneurship. Some are artisans, traders and the like. Most of them lack financial capacity to even have their own shops and capital for business.

“They need support from government. And that’s the reason most of the people organize themselves in cooperative. But at the end of the day, where does it take them to? No where.

“If we get the opportunity to be in power, that’s the kind of people we will face. When you empower people, the progress will be felt in the society. It’s not for government to be constructing this, constructing that, more so when we lack maintenance culture. We will provide assistance,” he said.

World.title: Chidera Okonji on Why Women Need to Be Intentional About Rest
World.content:
Is there an art to rest? Can someone be inactive and still not truly rest? These are questions Chidera Okonji, better known as Odera Collins, hopes to explore at her upcoming Bloom & Brunch event, themed ‘The Art of Rest.’

A media professional, event host and creative producer with experience spanning radio, television and large-scale productions, Okonji understands how demanding work environments can affect one’s wellbeing. Having experienced firsthand the physical and mental toll of constantly being in motion, she has also observed how often women put themselves last. These experiences inspired her to create Bloom & Brunch as a space where women can pause, connect, reflect, have a good time and simply be.

In this interview with Vanessa Obioha, she explains the idea behind ‘The Art of Rest.’

Ordinarily, one sees rest as just taking a break from work, but the theme of your event suggests otherwise. Does rest really require an art?

Yes, there is. Sadly, due to the current state of the economy, coupled with living in a capitalist world, we have been tasked with a life where we have to keep working/running different streams of income in a bid to measure up to the demands of our society. So what you see is people, in this case women, burying themselves in their business/work. Now, behind this are high-stress conditions, bad eating habits, toxic relationships, etc., which greatly affect the overall balance of women’s lives and health.

I have also seen this personally. I spent over 10 years working in a very demanding environment, and I barely took days off or even a leave. I eventually realised the effect that lifestyle was having on my mental and physical health. That experience, alongside seeing women constantly self-sacrifice and later carry resentment from years of putting themselves last, made me start thinking about how I could contribute differently.

That is part of what inspired Bloom & Brunch. An avenue and a space where women can actually pause, reconnect, talk about the things they are experiencing and learn better ways to prioritise themselves, while having a good time.

Would you say that our culture of constant work and “hustle” has changed our understanding of rest, particularly in a place like Lagos where many people cannot easily step away from their responsibilities?

Oh, definitely. In a way, we have demonised rest. I mean, you hear people say things like, “If you sleep beyond 4/5 a.m., then you are unserious with your life,” and unfortunately, people have become slaves to these types of ideologies.

Speaking about Lagos, we can also see the weight that basic living expenses have put on people, so for some, it’s almost impossible to consider themselves deserving of rest when there is always another bill, responsibility or goal to meet. We have normalised being constantly busy to the point where slowing down can almost feel like failure.

I think that is why we need to start having more honest conversations around rest, and also intentionally curating spaces that allow us to do so. This is more about learning how to create healthier rhythms within the realities of the lives we are living.

What makes rest different from doing nothing? Can someone be physically inactive and still not be truly resting?

You have to be intentional about rest. It’s more mental, in my experience, than it is physical. I mean, you could be physically inactive but have a thousand tabs open in your head. That is not rest. It is in the intentional acts of boundaries, prioritisation, hobbies, etc.

It was something I realised in my last job, which was a high-stress one with tight deadlines, heavy work and intense emotional demands. I mentioned I had spent over 10 years working in demanding environments, so I know what it feels like to be physically present but mentally exhausted.

That is also why, with Bloom & Brunch, we want to create an environment where women can actually pause. We want them to talk, laugh, engage in sensory activities, dress up nice, enjoy good food, connect with other women and simply be present without feeling the need to be productive.

Why do you think rest has to be something people feel they need to justify, earn or even be productive about?

Because of how we have been socialised to think that slowing down is a bad thing, so we go about our lives thinking that taking a break is an abominable thing; meanwhile, an optimised life is one where balance exists.

I think women especially have been conditioned to constantly pour into other people, their work, their families and their responsibilities, while putting themselves last. So even when they finally have an opportunity to rest, there can be this feeling that they should be doing something more productive with that time.

For me, part of the conversation around the Art of Rest is helping women understand that they do not have to wait until they are completely exhausted before they give themselves permission to pause. Rest can be intentional, and it can exist alongside ambition, responsibility and everything else that matters to us.

What makes rest genuinely restorative?

Proper rest helps us recalibrate and moves our nervous system out of that fight-or-flight mode, allowing for better emotional regulation. Doctors have spoken about how it helps with cellular repair and immune system function. In my experience, my health became better when I started resting intentionally. From skin, physical health, to work output, I saw immense improvement.

Bloom & Brunch practically exists to reach more women and show them that intentional living is possible. For this edition, we are creating a curated experience themed ‘Arabian Luxe’ where women can come together, relate to each other’s experiences and hear from experts about the importance of self-prioritisation, rest and the best ways to practise it in the world we currently live in.

Beyond the conversation, we are also curating activities that allow women to engage their senses through wellness activities, laugh, play and reconnect with themselves.

If rest is an art, what are the skills involved in learning it, recognising when we need it, creating the space for it, and resisting the guilt that can come with it?

I think the first skill is self-awareness, being able to recognise when your body and mind are asking you to slow down. Then comes intentionality, setting boundaries, prioritising what truly matters and creating the space to rest without waiting until you are completely burnt out.

You also have to learn to detach your sense of worth from how much you are able to accomplish. Rest is not something you have to earn. It is part of living a balanced life, and learning to rest without guilt involves unlearning the idea that being constantly busy is the same as being productive.

Sometimes, it also means giving yourself permission to simply be. To laugh, enjoy yourself, reconnect with yourself and do things that have no other purpose than making you feel present and alive. I think that is an important part of the art of rest too.

World.title: Benue APC Leaders Petition NWC, Demand Suspension of Ex-Chairman Over Alleged Anti-party Activities
World.content:
Adedayo Akinwale in Abuja

Prominent leaders of the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC) have formally petitioned the National Working Committee (NWC) of the party demanding the immediate suspension of the former Benue State party Chairman, Austin Agada, over his fraternisation with ‘Rainbow Coalition’ and alleged anti-party activities.

The ‘Rainbow Coalition’ is the support group of the Minister of Federal Capital Territory (FCT), Nyesom Wike, aimed at galvanising support across party lines for the re-election of President Bola Tinubu in the 2027 elections.

However, the coalition has put some governors of the ruling party in an uneasy situation because of the decision to support candidates against the APC in some states.

Nevertheless, the petition signed by the group’s National Organising Secretary, Sa’idu Muhammad, accused Agada of cross party endorsement of Senator Abba Moro of the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) and others.

The petition dated 28th September, 2026, was titled ‘Petition against anti-party activities, public opposition to the APC governorship, Senatorial, House of Representatives and House of Assembly candidates in Benue South Senatorial district, Zone C of Benue state: A conduct prejudicial to the interest of the APC at large.’

The party leaders under the auspices of APC Solidarity Group said Agada — acting as leader of a prominent faction of the APC loyal to the Secretary to the government of the Federation, SGF, Senator George Akume in Benue State — made a highly publicised move by cross-party endorsing Moro for the 2027 senatorial seat, where he boldly printed banners of Tinubu and Moro of the PDP.

The group recalled that on September 28, 2026, Agada granted an interview on TVC PoliticsTonight, where he stated very clearly that he has no reason to campaign for the APC gubernatorial candidate in Benue State, Fr. Hyacinth Alia, in the 2027 governorship election.

To this end, the group called on the NWC to constitute an investigative committee, invite Agada to appear before it, constitute a disciplinary committee to discipline him if found guilty and publicise his disciplinary measures to serve as deterrent to others.

It noted: “Agada’s position is contrary to the position of the governors elected in the platform of the APC which was communicated through the Progressives Governor’ Forum and also endorsed by the 36 state chapters of the party and the FCT through the state chairmen of the party.

“The interview as confirmed from the recordings of the programme, we believe his position raises serious questions of party loyalty and compliance with the obligations expected of a senior member of the APC as stated in the party’s constitution.”

It also accused Agada of involvement in Rainbow Coalition, contrary to the interest of the party, saying the ruling party has over 12 million members and is ahead of all other political parties, fully prepared to win the 2027 general election.

It added: “We are further concerned about Agada’s reported activities within a group known as the Strategic Alliance for Tinubu 2027, (the Rainbow Coalition in Benue) which is in bed with the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP), the Social Democratic Party (SDP), the Labour Party (LP), the Nigerian Democratic Congress (NDC), particularly where such activities are being conducted in a manner that opposes or undermines the APC’s officially recognised political structure and its governorship, senatorial, House of Representatives and House of Assembly candidates in Benue State.

“We firmly acknowledged that supporting President Bola Ahmed Tinubu’s 2027 presidential re-election is consistent with APC’s national interest. However, support for the president should not be used as a basis for campaigning against other candidates of the APC where the party has established candidates and recognized campaign structure.

“The central issue before the party is therefore not whether Austin Agada supports President Tinubu, but whether his activities amount to conduct that undermines the APC, its candidates, its structures or its electoral interests in Benue State or it violates the relevant section of the APC Constitution.”

The group stressed that the party’s NWC should interrogate the relevant provisions of Article 21 of the APC Constitution and determine whether the activities of Agada as stated above amount to anti- party activities and are punishable under the relevant section of the party’s constitution.

The group declared that the petition was borne out of loyalty and commitment to party supremacy, discipline, unity and the collective interest of the APC ahead of the 2027 general election.

It pointed out that as a former Chairman of the APC in Benue State, Agada understands the importance of party supremacy, discipline, loyalty and respect for constituted party organs.

It maintained that Benue APC cannot afford a situation in which senior members openly campaign for other political parties against the APC.

It urged the NWC to act within the framework of the party’s constitution to prevent indiscipline from becoming a norm as the power to discipline members is vested on it.

“We therefore respectfully request the National Working Committee to cause this petition to be investigated and, where the allegations are proven, ensure that the appropriate disciplinary measures are applied in accordance with the constitution,” it insisted.

World.title: Which is the cheapest Kruger gate to use when travelling from Jhb?
World.content:
If you’re looking for the cheapest Kruger gate, there is a catch: no gate is cheaper to enter than another. Every visitor pays the same daily conservation fee wherever they come in.

South African citizens and residents with an ID pay R134 per adult and R67 per child per day until 31 October 2026. From 1 November 2026 the SANParks schedule lists R140 and R70. Wild Card members don’t pay the daily fee when they show their card and ID.

So the real saving lies in how you get there, not which gate you use.



THE SHORTEST DISTANCE GATE

SANParks lists Numbi as the shortest drive from Johannesburg at 411km. You take the N4 to Nelspruit, then the R40 to White River and the R538/R539 to the gate.

Malelane follows closely at 428km, entirely on the N4 via Witbank and Nelspruit. Phabeni is 430km and Paul Kruger is 460km, both via Hazyview. Less distance means less fuel, but the gap between the top three is only about 20km. So, the savings are not massive.

The better money-saver is choosing the gate closest to your camp. Berg-en-Dal is about 20 minutes from Malelane, and Pretoriuskop is about 20 minutes from Numbi. A gate that looks cheaper on the map can cost you more in fuel once you’ve driven a long internal route to your camp. Malelane is also handy if you’re staying at Berg-en-Dal or Malelane camp, as it keeps you on the N4 the whole way. The N4 is a toll road. So, check current tariffs when you budget.

PRACTICAL TIPS TO CONSIDER

Some travel guides advise using Phabeni instead of Numbi for safety and security reasons. I’d check SANParks’ latest travel advisories before settling on Numbi, even though it is the shortest route.

Practical tips

Carry your ID or driver’s licence for every adult in the car. Without it, you’ll be charged the international rate (R602 for adults at the time of writing).

Gates are cashless, so bring a card.

Gate times are strictly enforced. Late arrivals are only allowed in emergencies.

During the festive season, gate quotas apply. Once the daily quota is reached, only pre-booked visitors get in.

For the lowest cost, pick the gate nearest your camp. If you have no preference, Numbi is shortest on paper, while Malelane is the simplest N4 run. The cheapest option is whichever route puts you in the park soonest.

World.title: Orlando Pirates news: Mbatha, Makgopa, Sibisi, R10 million
World.content:
Orlando Pirates return to action next weekend when they face Mamelodi Sundowns in the MTN8 final.

The highly anticipated clash will take place at the Moses Mabhida Stadium on 10 October 2026 and will be the first meeting between the two sides this season.

In the Betway Premiership, Masandawana currently sit at the top of the table, leading the Buccaneers by just one point. Pirates, however, have a game in hand over their rivals.



Saturday’s final will have plenty at stake, with the winner likely to gain a significant psychological advantage in the title race.

Pirates could also welcome some familiar faces back into the squad.

Orlando Pirates eyeing win over Sundowns

Thalente Mbatha and Evidence Makgopa have been sidelined with injuries for the past two months and have not featured in recent weeks. Both players are in contention to return for Saturday’s clash, although their lack of match fitness makes a starting berth unlikely in a game of such magnitude.



Mbatha, in particular, has been an important figure in the Pirates midfield. The midfielder enjoyed an impressive run last season, with the Buccaneers unbeaten in matches he started.

He was also absent when Orlando Pirates suffered a 2-1 defeat to Sundowns earlier this year.

In defence, meanwhile, the Buccaneers are sweating over the fitness of captain Nkosinathi Sibisi. The 31-year-old is currently with Bafana Bafana but has been unable to feature due to a knock.



Orlando Pirates coach Abdeslam Ouaddou will be hoping his captain recovers in time to return to club duty fully fit.

With R10 million on the line, the Buccaneers will be determined to make history by lifting a record fifth consecutive MTN8 title.

Who’s winning the MTN8?

World.title: Springbok Women beat Spain in WXV as Ireland home Tests loom
World.content:
The Springbok Women thump Spain ahead of a WXV Global Series double against Ireland. Image: South Africa Rugby website.

The Springbok Women are building momentum heading into their final WXV Global Series tour fixtures.

They sealed a convincing 20-0 win over Spain in Seville on 4 October, running in 3 tries.

The women’s team are looking strong ahead of a two-match visit by Ireland later this month.



Springbok Women too strong for Spain

It took the South Africans 14 minutes to get on the scoreboard, with Catha Jacobs dotting down.

Jakkie Cilliers added the conversion, and then added a penalty at the half-hour mark.

Early in the second half, Aseza Hele scored the Springbok Women’s second try.

Cilliers then added to her points tally by crossing the try line in the 67th minute.

This sealed a flawless 20-0 result for the visitors in Seville, according to the South Africa Rugby website.

South Africa hammered in Wales

Their start to the WXV Global Series was less than ideal following a loss in Cardiff on 18 September.



Wales outscored South Africa by 8 tries to 3, with Sisilia Tuipulotu doing much of the damage, according to Rugby365.

Things went from bad to worse after Danelle Lochner was red-carded for a high tackle.

Despite going into halftime 31-5 behind, the Springbok Women managed to claw back some ground, but were never in the game.

The match ended 50-19 to the hosts, with Wales recording their first win in more than a year.

Springbok Women bounce back in Italy

The team switched things up against Italy in Pordenone on 26 September with a hard-fought 41-29 win.

The Springbok Women relied on more polished set pieces, but were still guilty of multiple errors.

South Africa used their wits and physicality better against the Italians, heading into the break 12 points ahead.

However, the hosts were not counted out, capitalising on a Yonela Ngxingolo yellow card to score twice in the second half.

Italy then took the lead in the final quarter of the game, before Micke Gunter scored a crucial try to seal the result.

Upcoming fixtures

The Springbok Women have two Tests against Ireland on 24 and 31 October.

Both games kick off at 15:00 at the Athlone Stadium in Cape Town.

Ireland are currently 5th in the World Rugby rankings, and this will be a huge test for South Africa, who are 10th.

The women’s teams have only met once before, during the 2006 World Cup hosted in Canada.

South Africa exited after three losses in the pool stages, including a 0-37 thumping by the Irish.
