World.title: Croatia Suffer Heaviest Defeat in History in 7-0 Loss to England
World.content:
Croatia hosted England at Rujevica in Rijeka in the third round of Nations League A, Group 3. Both sides went into the match with three points, each having beaten the Czech Republic and lost to Spain. After a win against the Czechs in Prague and a defeat to Spain in Seville, Croatia welcomed England for a 6 pm kickoff, but the evening turned into the darkest in the national team’s history.

Due to a UEFA sanction, no tickets were sold for the match, but the stands were far from empty, as around 6,000 children from primary schools and football academies across Croatia, accompanied by their coaches, turned out to support the Vatreni.

Lineups:

CROATIA: Livaković, Stanišić (Šutalo 76′), Vušković, Gvardiol, Perišić, Modrić (Jakić 56′), Kovačić (yellow card), Baturina (Vlašić 46′), P. Sučić (Mario Pašalić 46′), Ivanović, Musa (Matanović 46′)

ENGLAND: Pickford, Quansah, Konsa, Guehi, Hall (Gibbs-White 80′), Anderson (Lewis-Skelly 80′), Scott (Garner 69′), Saka, Gordon (Eze 69′), Bellingham, Kane (Rogers 69′)



Match report

German referee Sven Jablonski got the match underway, and England threatened from the start, with Livaković ready for Gordon’s third-minute effort. The visitors took the lead in the eighth minute after Joško Gvardiol played a loose pass into the middle. England pounced, and Jude Bellingham slipped in an unmarked Kane. The England captain had time to compose himself and lifted the ball over Livaković from around ten meters to make it 1-0.

By the 20th minute, England were in total control, with Croatia unable to get out of their own half. A minute later, England struck again, this time through Bellingham. Livaković denied Gordon a sitter in the 25th minute, and at the half-hour mark Croatia were still searching for their first attempt on the England goal. In the 35th minute, Perišić delivered a good cross into the box, but Pickford punched clear.

England crowned their dominance with a third goal in the 39th minute, as Gordon finally beat his club teammate Livaković at the third attempt. Croatia registered their first shot on target in the 41st minute from a Stanišić cross, though it posed no danger to England. Moments later came Croatia’s first real chance, but after weaving through the English defence, Kovačić’s finish lacked accuracy.

England added a fourth right on the stroke of half-time. In the 45th minute, Bellingham crossed from the left to find Bukayo Saka completely alone five meters out, and the Arsenal forward had no trouble making it 4-0. Just one minute of stoppage time was added, and Croatia went into the break completely powerless after England’s show of strength at Rujevica.

Croatia made three changes at half-time, with Musa, Baturina and Petar Sučić staying in the dressing room and Matanović, Vlašić and Mario Pašalić coming on. Matanović nearly made an immediate impact in the 48th minute with a powerful strike from distance that flew just wide of the post. But the nightmare continued in the 53rd minute, when Kane grabbed his second of the night to make it 5-0.

Bellingham was off target with another England chance in the 56th minute, and Croatia captain Luka Modrić then made way for Kristijan Jakić. Croatia won their first corner of the match in the 62nd minute, but Pickford claimed Perišić’s delivery. In the 68th minute, Saka netted his second to put England 6-0 up, and Kovačić was shown a yellow card shortly after.

England manager Thomas Tuchel made a triple change in the 69th minute, bringing off Kane, Scott and Gordon for Rogers, Garner and Eze. Croatia brought on Šutalo for Stanišić in the 76th minute, while England replaced Hall and Anderson with Gibbs-White and Lewis-Skelly in the 80th.

Croatia’s heaviest ever defeat had been the 6-0 loss to Spain in the 2018 Nations League, and that record came under threat in the 72nd minute when Saka nearly added a seventh. Croatia brought on Šutalo for Stanišić in the 76th minute, while England replaced Hall and Anderson with Gibbs-White and Lewis-Skelly in the 80th.

Croatia’s players were left fuming in the 83rd minute when Franjo Ivanović went down in the box after a challenge from Konsa, but referee Jablonski waved away their penalty appeals. Four minutes later, the record was gone. In the 87th minute, Morgan Rogers collected a long ball from Bellingham in the Croatian half, raced clear on the counter, sent Livaković the wrong way and slotted home to make it 7-0, the heaviest defeat in Croatia’s history.

Croatia meets Spain next on Tuesday at Poljud.

World.title: Zadar Connected Year-Round: Winter Flights to Munich Confirmed, Expansion to Paris, London or Venice
World.content:
October the 3rd, 2026 – Zadar is set to become connected year-round, with winter flights to Munich now confirmed, and expansion to Paris, London or Venice being actively eyed.

The new year-round air route between Zadar and Munich should be only the beginning of the further expansion of Zadar’s air connectivity with Europe, County Prefect Josip Bilaver said in response to journalists’ questions after a working meeting at the Zadar County House with Croatian Roads Management Board President Ivica Budimir and associates. O23 reports how Bilaver recalled that the possibility of introducing a year-round connection was announced about a year ago, and that operations during the winter months have now also been confirmed. He emphasised that the first reactions from citizens have been extremely positive.

“Munich is a major international air hub from which you can continue travelling practically to the entire world. Our wish is to have more such routes and we believe this should only be the beginning,” Bilaver said. He added that talks have already been held with other airlines, as well as with Croatia Airlines, and that further expansion of the year-round route offer is expected next year.

“As a county, together with the tourist boards, cities and municipalities and the tourism sector, we are ready to support such projects. Representatives of the tourism sector already several months ago expressed their readiness to participate in co-financing the routes. When we have concrete routes and proposals, we will also discuss concrete amounts,” the Prefect announced. He stressed that year-round air connectivity is important not only for tourism, but also for better connecting the residents of Zadar County with the rest of Europe and indeed the world.

“A good indicator will be precisely the Munich route, for which we expect good occupancy. After that we will see whether there is a possibility of connecting Zadar with some other major European centre. Split, for example, has a connection with Rome, but I believe there is no need for us to compete with them on the same route in the winter period. I would like Zadar to get a connection with some other major European centre such as Venice, Paris or London and thus further expand its year-round connectivity,” County Prefect Bilaver concluded.

World.title: Railway Mega-Project Would Position Croatia as Important Transit Hub
World.content:
October the 3rd, 2026 – The recently announced and sighed railway mega-project has a high chance of positioning Croatia as an important transit hub.

The future Adriatic-Ionian railway corridor would bring many benefits, and its importance is also recognised by the European Commission. Europe must be better connected, that’s the premise that guided the signatories of the initiative “Adriatic-Ionian Railway Corridor. Transport Connectivity is deemed to be the Foundation of Development and Resilience”, and finalising the documents, the first step has been taken towards a future railway corridor that will connect Italy, Slovenia and Croatia with Bosnia and Herzegovina, Montenegro, Albania and Greece. Katarina Kusec reports for Poslovni that Croatia could benefit greatly in this story, as the new corridor would specifically link Trieste, Koper, Rijeka, Zadar, Šibenik, Split, Ploče, Bar, Durrës and Greek centres along the Adriatic-Ionian route.

better connectivity for all

The initiative was signed on Friday by Member of the European Parliament and member of the Committee on Transport and Tourism Nikolina Brnjac, Zadar County Prefect Josip Bilaver, representatives of the coastal counties, and State Secretary in the Ministry of Maritime Affairs, Transport and Infrastructure Žarko Tušek. The aim of the initiative, it was said at the conference, is to better connect Croatia by rail with neighbouring countries and the rest of the Adriatic-Ionian region and to encourage joint investments in transport infrastructure, Hina reports.

“I don’t even need to say how important this is for the railway connection of Ploče, the Port of Ploče, with the ports of Split, Zadar, Šibenik and Rijeka. At the same time, for the first time it would enable the railway connection and financing of Istria County, Kvarner and Dalmatia with the rest of Croatia and with the European network,” said Brnjac, emphasising that the next step is a meeting with stakeholders from the governments of the countries through which the route would pass. The initiative will, she said, also influence the reconstruction of existing railway corridors as well as the construction of new lines. Tušek noted that without a modern railway there can be no strengthening of logistics capacities and position in the TEN-T network. He also highlighted the need to integrate the Istrian railways into the complete Croatian network, adding that study documentation for the Učka railway tunnel is currently being prepared. In this regard, he also announced that next year a tender will be issued for the Učka project, that is, the lowland railway project and the connection of Rijeka to that lowland railway.

financing the future adriatic-ionion corridor

Returning to the Adriatic-Ionian corridor, the question of its financing also needs to be raised. Brnjac said that 81 billion euros of EU money is currently available until the next financial framework, of which 35 billion for transport, 30 for energy and 17.5 for military mobility, and that is why this initiative was launched, working on opening the regulation of the Trans-European Transport Network.

“When the regulation tender is opened, then the Adriatic-Ionian corridor would become an integral corridor and then we can have funds for further financing,” she stressed, noting that the only known deadline is that a large conference on this topic will be organised in the European Parliament at the beginning of next year. More specifically speaking, the final conference is planned in Brussels, when the initiative will be handed over to European Commission Commissioner for Sustainable Transport and Tourism Apostolos Tzitzikostas, who, she said, has recognised the importance of this initiative.

All the signatories are aware of the importance of the said corridor for Croatia both in terms of connectivity and tourism, so HŽ Infrastruktura Management Board President Damir Lončarić emphasised that the Adriatic-Ionian railway corridor is a strategic issue for the state. “HŽ Infrastruktura is ready to make a full contribution in terms of expert and operational support for this project,” Lončarić added. The sheer importance of this massive project is further heightened by the security and geopolitical circumstances in Europe, as the war in Ukraine has shown how important alternative and reliable transport routes are for the economy, energy and military mobility. In addition, a more modern railway would enable faster freight transport, relieve road traffic and stronger inclusion of Croatian ports in the international chain.

World.title: Croatian Subjects Found to Have Forever Chemicals in Them Speak Out
World.content:
October the 3rd, 2026 – Croatian subjects found to have so-called forever chemicals in them have spoken out, with one man from Lika having been found with the highest levels of all.

Gospić lawyer Vjekoslav Bušić, better known to the public as one of the founders and prominent representatives of the Citizens’ Initiative “Gospić is Our Home”, revealed in a report by Slobodan Mufic for Index that he has the worst findings among the ten Croatian participants in the study on the presence of PFAS compounds in the blood, also known as “forever chemicals”.

“I spoke with the other participants in the study and it turned out that the highest values of the four long-chain PFAS were found in me, even though I’ve only been living in Gospić for the last three and a half years. Interestingly, my wife is clean as a whistle. Her findings are phenomenally low, and we have practically the same lifestyle habits and eat the same food,” said Bušić.

7 from gospić, one from pula and two from knin

The study was commissioned by the Greens/EFA group in the European Parliament. The biological analyses were carried out by the Institute for Occupational Medicine of the University Medical Center Hamburg-Eppendorf, and the toxicological interpretation of the results was done by Vrije Universiteit Amsterdam. In addition to the seven people from Gospić, two more from Knin and one person from Pula were tested.

A total of 110 people from Croatia, Italy, Belgium, France, Germany, Luxembourg, Spain, Denmark and Finland took part. Among the participants were also women of reproductive age, residents of areas near the chemical industry and trade union representatives, which shows that this is not a randomly selected representative sample of the European population.

All four analysed long-chain PFAS compounds (PFOA, PFNA, PFHxS and PFOS) were found in all 110 participants. However, in 27 of them, or 25 percent, the sum was above the health-based reference value set by the European Food Safety Authority (EFSA). Of the ten Croatian participants included in the study, six had a sum above the reference value – that is, 60 percent. The sum of the four long-chain PFAS compounds in the study was compared with the reference concentration of 6.9 nanograms per millilitre of blood. Exceeding that value does not mean that a person will develop a disease, nor does it constitute a diagnosis. It is a health-based reference value linked to EFSA’s assessment of long-term exposure to PFAS compounds and possible effects on the immune system.

Bušić emphasises that he has no reliable explanation for his findings: “It’s difficult for me to assess what the cause could be; I can only speculate. I thought it might be because in the last year and a half I have really often walked around the silos in the former PPK Velebit. Maybe the problem is inhaling those particles – I don’t know myself.”

how dangerous are these forever chemicals?

“On the other hand, toxicologists warn that heavy metals, which were also found in the illegally disposed hazardous waste in Gospić, are in the long term much more toxic and dangerous to human health than those ‘forever chemicals’. In any case, the findings are what they are, but one should not draw some final and alarming conclusions about carcinogenicity from them. It seems to me that all of this is still quite unresearched,” says Bušić, and adds:

“I still believe that I live in one of the cleanest and best-preserved areas in all of Europe. It’s important that it remains so and that the remediation of the waste in Gospić is carried out in the best possible way. And who knows, maybe I ‘picked up’ the PFAS while I was living in Zagreb.” The testing was carried out in the first days of July this year in Brussels. Bušić says that the people from Gospić received a link where they could apply online: “We didn’t even know how many people were participating in the study; in the end we realised that there were ten of us from Croatia. Apart from the seven of us from Gospić, the application of one person from Pula and two people from Knin, also members of an association, was accepted.”

The office of Croatian MEP from the Greens/EFA, Gordan Bosanac, organised the participation of ten Croatian volunteers and their trip to Belgium for blood sampling. In June, Bosanac described the project as a study of people deliberately selected from areas with possible increased exposure to PFAS, for example near landfills or industrial plants.

“Given our situation, this was a good signal that we should perhaps carry out some biomonitoring on a wider circle of people. Especially on those who live relatively close to the silos in Gospić or those who worked at the Rakitovac municipal landfill, where that hazardous waste was also brought. And it would be interesting to see the findings of the people who worked for Josip Šincek, who transported and unloaded that waste,” said Bušić.

Josip Šincek is a Varaždin entrepreneur and the main suspect in the USKOK investigation into illegal waste management; investigators suspect that through related companies he organised the import and transport of plastic, mixed and medical waste from Croatia and abroad. In Gospić, his company operated from 2021 in the former PPK Velebit complex in Bilajska Street, where tens of thousands of tonnes of illegally disposed and partly hazardous waste were later discovered.

World.title: Plenković: Without Government Measures, Inflation Would be 7%
World.content:
October the 3rd, 2026 – PM Andrej Plenković has stated that without government measures, inflation would currently be 7% in Croatia.

The Croatian Bureau of Statistics (DZS) recently published that the year-on-year inflation rate measured by the consumer price index in September amounted to 4.7 percent, and 0.9 percent compared to August. Poslovni reports that it accelerated by 0.5 percentage points compared to August on an annual basis, and by 0.8 percent compared to July.

Prime Minister Andrej Plenković warned on Friday after a meeting with Bavarian Prime Minister Markus Söder that without government measures inflation would have been 35 percent higher and would have stood at around seven percent, instead of the 4.7 percent that is the first estimate by the Croatian Bureau of Statistics (DZS) for September, Hina reports.

The DZS earlier today published that the year-on-year inflation rate measured by the consumer price index in September amounted to 4.7 percent, and 0.9 percent compared to August. It accelerated by 0.5 percentage points compared to August on an annual basis, and by 0.8 percent compared to July. Energy prices had the greatest impact on the rise in inflation, rising by 20.5 percent year-on-year in September, while food, beverages and tobacco rose by only 0.2 percent, and non-food industrial products fell by 1.4 percent.

“What is good is that other segments are going downwards; there we have succeeded with measures in mitigating the growth. Without government measures, the overall inflation rate would have been 35 percent higher – it would have been around seven percent,” Plenković said in response to journalists’ questions.

He also recalled that prices of motor fuels are lower due to the government’s weekly interventions and stated that at the moment blue diesel is 10 cents cheaper, eurosuper 20 cents cheaper, and eurodiesel as much as 32 cents cheaper than the prices that would have been formed without government measures.

He added that there is still room to mitigate the rise in fuel prices through interventions, because Croatia is in good time asking the European Commission for permission to exceptionally lower excise duties even below the minimum threshold set by European regulations. A new government intervention is expected next Monday.

World.title: Iraq’s financial revenues hit $30 billion in seven months
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The Iraqi Ministry of Finance revealed on Sunday that the country’s total revenues reached approximately 39.09 trillion Iraqi dinars (nearly $30 billion) until the end of July 2026, with oil revenues accounting for about 78 percent of total state resources.

The revenues from oil exports totaled over 30.35 trillion Iraqi dinars (approximately $23.24 billion). In comparison, non-oil revenues amounted to 8.74 trillion Iraqi dinars (nearly $6.7 billion), which represented about 22 percent of the total income.

The figures indicated that total revenues of 39.09 trillion Iraqi dinars (approximately $30 billion) were offset by total expenditures of approximately 65.42 trillion Iraqi dinars (about $50.09 billion), resulting in a deficit of 26.32 trillion Iraqi dinars ($20.15 billion).

Iraq’s financial revenues between January and April surpassed 31.16 trillion Iraqi dinars ($23.6 billion).

Oil sales during the first four months of 2026 produced 26.12 trillion Iraqi dinars (approximately $19.9 billion), accounting for 84 percent of overall state income, while non-oil revenues were around 5.04 trillion Iraqi dinars (around $3.84 billion).

Iraq’s significant reliance on oil as the primary source of its national budget exposes the country to vulnerabilities stemming from global crises that impact the oil sector.

The government’s reliance on oil to address the deficit forces it to seek external or internal loans, underscoring its struggle to manage public finances efficiently and revealing a deficiency in developing alternative revenue streams.

World.title: Iraq, OPEC+ members agree to keep oil production unchanged
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The OPEC+ alliance decided in principle to maintain oil output objectives unchanged during a meeting on Sunday, according to Reuters.

The meeting included seven key OPEC+ members—Saudi Arabia, Russia, Iraq, Kuwait, Algeria, Kazakhstan, and Oman—and took place as Gulf states work to boost exports following months of turmoil caused by the US war against Iran; however, most producers are still pumping much below their goal quotas.

The OPEC+ alliance had raised its production targets for most of the year before deciding to keep them unchanged in October, after completing the phasing out of voluntary cuts, which totaled approximately 1.65 million barrels per day that began in 2023.

OPEC+ comprises the Organization of the Petroleum Exporting Countries (OPEC) and its allies, including Russia.

Sources indicated that a review by OPEC+, intended to establish oil production quotas for member states for 2027, has been postponed.

This delay is attributed to the disruption of capacity-expansion initiatives across the Middle East caused by the US-Israeli war on Iran, which complicates the evaluation of future production capabilities for member states.

World.title: Iraq’s Real Estate Bank challenges legality of Zayouna Gate project
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The state-owned Real Estate Bank of Iraq issued an official statement on Saturday, October 3, 2026, challenging claims regarding the newly launched Zayouna Gate residential development in eastern Baghdad.

Addressing promotional campaigns and unit pre-sales announced by private developer Amwaj International, the bank warned that the underlying land remains protected sovereign property, stating that unauthorized residential conversions on the site constitute an infringement on public assets and a squandering of public funds.

According to a formal statement received by the Iraqi News Agency (INA), the Real Estate Bank detailed five structural and legal clarifications:

Sovereign Land Ownership: As a public state-owned banking enterprise, all real estate holdings and property assets form an indivisible part of the bank’s sovereign capital reserves. The institution stressed that no civil servant or public official, regardless of executive rank, holds legal authority to waive, transfer, or reassign ownership of the land to private parties.

Permit Scope & Build-Operate-Transfer Terms: The investment permit associated with the property was issued in 2022 to a private firm, Wahat Al-Rawan, solely for the construction of a modest three-story commercial complex—not a high-density, multi-tower residential project for freehold unit sales. Under the statutory terms of the concession, all structures were mandated to revert fully to the Real Estate Bank upon expiration of the investment lease.

Physical Status of the Site: The bank affirmed that the land plot remains vacant and free of authorized construction as of October 3, 2026. Authorities cautioned that any unauthorized excavation, perimeter fencing, or groundwork on the parcel will be treated as an illegal encroachment on state property.

No Contract Executed or Land Transferred: The Real Estate Bank stated that it has neither signed an execution contract nor handed over the physical plot. The parcel remains subject to ongoing judicial proceedings and active inquiries by the Federal Commission of Integrity regarding alleged administrative infractions and improper attempts to modify the project’s zoned use from commercial leasing to residential sale.

Active Legal Injunctions: The bank confirmed it has filed a formal appeal in the interest of the law, lodged lawsuits before competent judicial courts, and submitted dossiers to the Federal Commission of Integrity to block any illicit transfer of public assets while investigative reviews remain underway.

The bank’s public disclosure introduces significant regulatory friction into the project just 24 hours after Amwaj International hosted its launch event for the proposed twin 36-story development, highlighting heightened government scrutiny over urban land allocations and sovereign property rights in central Baghdad.

World.title: Iraq transits 2M barrels past Hormuz on VLCC in decades-first shipping shift
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The Iraqi Oil Tankers Company (IOTC), an affiliate of the Ministry of Oil, announced on Saturday, October 3, 2026, the successful transit of two million barrels of domestic crude oil aboard a chartered Very Large Crude Carrier (VLCC) past the Strait of Hormuz.

The operation marks the first time in decades that the state-owned maritime shipping enterprise has conducted independent crude transportation beyond the strategic maritime chokepoint, shifting a portion of Iraq’s petroleum commercialization away from traditional delivery at Basra offshore terminals to delivery points beyond the Gulf.

Speaking to the official Iraqi News Agency (INA) in remarks reported by the 964 Network, IOTC Director General Ali Qais explained that the landmark transit was executed under the direct directives of the Prime Minister and the supervision of the Minister of Oil.

Following extensive technical negotiations with international maritime carriers, IOTC chartered a VLCC supertanker, loaded two million barrels of crude, and navigated the vessel into open international waters outside the Strait of Hormuz.

The strategic maneuver is designed to grant the State Organization for Marketing of Oil (SOMO) elevated commercial flexibility, capturing premium pricing benchmarks, mitigating regional maritime transit risk premiums for buyers, and optimizing sovereign export revenues.

Qais emphasized that executive directives are actively steering the company toward the expedited procurement and outright ownership of its own fleet of dedicated crude oil supertankers.

Moving beyond spot charters, the acquisition drive seeks to restore Iraq’s sovereign blue-water tanker capabilities, modernizing IOTC’s logistics infrastructure to compete directly with national maritime shipping lines across the Gulf and broader Middle East.

World.title: Iraq studies raising oil export capacity through Turkey’s Ceyhan
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi Oil Minister Basim Khudair and Turkish Energy Minister Alparslan Bayraktar met in Turkey to finalize a deal for oil flows between Iraq and Turkey through the Mediterranean port of Ceyhan.

Khudair stated on Saturday that the meeting was highly constructive, with discussions centered on increasing export capacity through Ceyhan and Turkish firms’ participation in Iraqi oil and gas projects.

The involvement of Turkish companies in Iraq’s energy sector is critical to the governments of both countries, particularly the Iraqi government, according to Khudair. He noted that the step helps attract competent global corporations to develop Iraq’s oil and gas resources.

The Iraqi oil minister indicated that two joint technical committees have been formed to develop oilfields and construct oil facility infrastructure.

Khudair arrived in the Turkish capital, Ankara, on Friday to discuss cooperation in the fields of oil, gas, and energy.

Khudair signed an agreement with Turkey in early August to transport Iraqi crude oil through the Iraq-Turkey pipeline to the port of Ceyhan. The deal stipulates a minimum volume of 750,000 barrels per day for a one-year period, pending the completion of a broader framework agreement.

At the time, Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi declared that Iraqi and Turkish enterprises will begin executing the deal to transport crude oil to Ceyhan via the Iraq-Turkey pipeline.

Al-Zaidi said that Baghdad and Ankara were working to finalize a framework deal for the oil, electricity, and water resources sectors.

World.title: Amwaj International launches 36-story Zayouna Gate towers in Baghdad
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Amwaj International officially launched its latest premium residential development, Zayouna Gate, during a launch ceremony hosted on Thursday, October 1, 2026, at the Mövenpick Hotel Baghdad.

The event convened business leaders, prominent real estate figures, and investment stakeholders to review the master plan of the large-scale urban project, which aims to expand modern vertical living within eastern Baghdad.

Located in the central Zayouna district, the development features two 36-story residential towers accommodating 524 apartments. Units range from two-bedroom and three-bedroom layouts starting at 163 square meters to high-end penthouses on the upper levels.

Positioned as a self-sustaining gated community, Zayouna Gate combines luxury housing with civic infrastructure, dedicated green space, and family-oriented amenities.

Key components of the development include:

An integrated private school serving community residents.

Central landscaped gardens and landscaped green spaces.

Dedicated children’s play zones and pedestrian walking and jogging circuits.

A sports club, fitness gym, and exclusive residents’ social club.

Retail promenades, commercial outlets, and day-to-day community services.

Structured underground and surface parking for residents and visitors.

Smart-home building automation, 24/7 concierge, and integrated surveillance security systems.

Amwaj International confirmed that its primary sales center began receiving prospective buyers and prospective residents on Friday, October 2, 2026, to review architectural models, unit configurations, and available inventory.

The project marks another expansion in Amwaj’s metropolitan pipeline, advancing master-planned residential communities across Baghdad’s high-density urban corridors.

World.title: Graham Arnold sets sights on Asian Cup following Iraq’s Khaleeji 27 exit
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi national football team head coach Graham Arnold addressed media representatives on Saturday, October 3, 2026, affirming that the squad’s primary strategic objective is to deliver a commanding performance at the upcoming AFC Asian Cup.

Reflecting on the Lions of Mesopotamia’s campaign at the 27th Arabian Gulf Cup (“Khaleeji 27”) in Jeddah, Arnold stated that despite falling short of the knockout stages, the tournament yielded crucial tactical gains, most notably expanding squad depth and integrating a new generation of domestic talent.

Speaking to journalists, Arnold voiced strong optimism regarding Iraqi football’s long-term trajectory. He highlighted that working alongside a refreshed technical staff while blooding younger prospects produced impressive individual showings.

Arnold revealed that the technical team has identified four to five newly tested players who demonstrated starting-caliber potential, adding essential tactical variety—particularly across the frontline—ahead of the continental championship.

Addressing the public scrutiny surrounding Iraq’s early elimination, Arnold defended his squad’s on-pitch record, which concluded with one victory, one draw, and a narrow defeat to tournament hosts Saudi Arabia.

The Australian tactician voiced deep frustration with the tournament’s regulations, arguing that relying on a drawing of lots rather than official FIFA world rankings to break group-stage ties was deeply disappointing.

Nevertheless, Arnold affirmed he returned to Baghdad with his head held high, satisfied that the pre-tournament objective of evaluating emerging talent succeeded.

Looking ahead, Arnold outlined the national team’s roadmap toward the AFC Asian Cup, confirming that Iraq will contest two international friendlies during the November 2026 FIFA international window.

The upcoming training camp will serve as an operational proving ground to merge the newly discovered prospects with established key starters returning from injury, cementing an expanded, competitive roster for continental competition.

World.title: Construction begins on first phase of Iraq’s Madinat Al Ward
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – ORA Iraq awarded CRC Dorra the building contract for the first phase of Madinat Al Ward, paving the way for large-scale development in Iraq.

The deal was signed in the presence of Naguib Sawiris, Chairman of ORA, and Mohamed Dorra, Vice Chairman of Dorra Group, as the project progressed from ground preparation to primary construction.

CRC Dorra will begin construction after POWERCHINA has completed the earthworks and ground preparation for Phase One, according to ORA Iraq.

The deal adds another important regional contractor to the development.

CRC Dorra is the contracting arm of Dorra Group, an engineering and construction business founded in 1943 that operates in Egypt, Saudi Arabia, the United Arab Emirates, Qatar, and Iraq.

Its work includes residential, commercial, office, and hotel developments, as well as design-build projects.

ORA said that the selection was based on CRC Dorra’s construction expertise and capacity to perform large-scale projects.

The commencement of construction marks a key milestone for Madinat Al Ward as ORA expands its investment and development efforts in the Iraqi market.

The company said that it continues to be dedicated to building the project as an integrated community, with the new contract advancing Phase One from site preparation to physical construction.

World.title: Farm groups protest low Rabi MSP hike, call it an insult
World.content:
Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: A number of farmer organisations, joining hands under umbrella outfit, Samyukta Kisan Morcha (SKM), have rejected the new minimum support prices (MSPs) for Rabi crops for 2027-28, announced by the govt on Sept 30, saying that the Rs 25-per-quintal hike in the MSP for wheatâequivalent to just 25 paise per kilogramâis an insult.The farm group also called for an immediate revision of the MSPs for all Rabi crops, including wheat, and demanded that states be given full freedom to provide bonuses.Referring to the hike, the farm group said, â25 paise a kilo is not a price it is an insultâ¦Yet the government calls it a 106% profit (return over the cost of production).âAlleging that the statesâ price recommendations were bulldozed by the Centre and the Commission for Agricultural Costs & Prices (CACP), the SKM flagged that the increase in the diesel prices and other input costs were ignored while arriving at the cost of production.Noting that the price of diesel, which powers every tractor and pump set, was hiked four times in ten days in May, by about Rs 7.50 a litre, the SKM also demanded a rollback of the increase in diesel prices.Factoring in the deficient monsoon rainfall this year, the Centre last Wednesday announced new MSPs with focus on better hike to low water-consuming oilseeds, pulses and coarse grain so that farmers may opt for these crops over the most popular winter crop, wheat, whose new MSP at Rs 2,610 per quintal for 2027-28 got an increase of less than 1% over the existing support price of Rs 2,585 per quintal in 2026-27.The absolute highest increase in MSP was announced for Safflower (oilseeds) at Rs 675 per quintal followed by Rapeseed & Mustard (oilseeds) at Rs 413 per quintal. For Lentil (Masur), barley (coarse grain), and gram, there is an increase of Rs 390 per quintal, Rs 136 per quintal and Rs 83 per quintal, respectively.The Union agriculture ministry noted that the expected margin over cost of production, as calculated by the CACP, is the highest (106%) for wheat, followed by 96% for rapeseed & mustard; 92% for lentil; 59% for gram; 58% for barley; and 50% for safflower.Agriculture expert and former member of the Uttar Pradesh Planning Commission, Sudhir Panwar, however, questioned the hike, saying it is lower than inflation in input costs. âThis suggests that the govt rejected the norm of providing a 50% profit on input costs under the guise of diversification,â he said.The new MSP for the Rabi marketing season, beginning April 1 next year, will give a signal to farmers for their choice of crops during the upcoming sowing season, which is expected to face challenges of low moisture content in the soil and less water availability for irrigation due to deficient monsoon rainfall.The govt claimed that the increase in MSPs of all six Rabi crops is in sync with the Union Budget 2018-19 announcement of fixing the support price at a level of at least 1.5 times of the All-India weighted average Cost of Production, ensuring minimum 50% return over the cost of production.The cost, as calculated by the CACP, includes all paid out costs such as those incurred on account of hired human labour, bullock labour/machine labour, rent paid for leased in land, expenses incurred on use of material inputs like seeds, fertilizers, manures, irrigation charges, depreciation on implements and farm buildings, interest on working capital, diesel/electricity for operation of pump sets etc., miscellaneous expenses and imputed value of family labour. It is called A2+FL methodology, which means paid-out cost of cultivation plus the imputed value of family labour.SKM, however, has been demanding the comprehensive cost (C2 methodology) that should also include the rental value of the family's own land and the interest on its own capital, and a legally guaranteed MSP at C2+50%.Giving a call for protests against the new MSP, the SKM on Saturday urged farmers and youth of rural India to burn copies of the recent order on the hike in every village, saying it will go on until a legal MSP at C2+50% is won.

World.title: Social, rights activist Harbans Bharowal remembered upon his demise in Brampton
World.content:
BATHINDA: A number of social activists, rights activists mainly people of Punjab origin presently settled in Canada, remembered a noted social and rights activist Harbans Singh Bharowal in a memorial service at Brampton in Canada late Saturday evening.

68 years old Bharowal, chief editor of a monthly magazine Sarokaran Di Awaaz had passed away after a brief illness at Brampton on September 28. Another memorial has been planned by various farmers, left leaning organizations in Punjab on October 13. The activists recalled Bharowal spent his entire life for the social causes, agitations and struggles fought in Punjab and even while residing in Canada. He also contributed to the historic farmer struggle fought at the borders of Delhi in 2020-21.

The memorial service was held immediately after his funeral at Brampton crematorium and visitation centre.

Bharowal had worked in Punjab Students Union, Naujawan Bharat Sabha and worked as science teacher briefly before migrating to Canada in late 1980s.

Hailing from Dhurkot Ransih village in Moga, Harbans Singh had shifted to Bharowal Kalan village in Ludhiana to live with his aunt. He played a role in PSU after the infamous Moga Cinema agitation in 1972.





He got involved in agitation against the hefty increase in bus fares in 1980.

âAfter the formation of Congress government under Darbara Singh in 1980, the government increased bus fares by 43%. PSU and Naujawa Bharat Sabha started agitation against it wherein Harbans Singh was involved in deflating bus tyres on December 29, 1980 and held ralliesâ, recalls Inquilabi Kendra Punjab convener Kanwaljit Khanna.

Khanna and Punjab lok sabhyacharak manch president Amolak Singh said the farmer, worker and left organizations including BKU Ekta Ugrahan, BKU Ekta Dakaunda have decided to hold a memorial service at Bharowal Kalan village on October 13 to recall his immense contribution in various agitations and struggles right from late 10970s to the present.

NEW DELHI: Protests demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar intensified in Delhi on Sunday, with AAP workers, AISA and NSUI activists among those detained as demonstrators attempted to march towards Jantar Mantar for the third consecutive day.AAP workers, members of its student wing ASAP, NSUI workers, AISA activists and members of other organisations took part in the demonstrations, prompting heavy deployment of Delhi Police and paramilitary personnel across central Delhi.The protests are part of a wider agitation over alleged irregularities in the Election Commissionâs functioning, the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls and alleged mass deletion of voters.AISA members and activists from several organisations marched from the Ashoka Road area towards Jantar Mantar but were stopped by police barricades.The protesters briefly clashed with security personnel as they tried to cross the barricades. AISA national president Neha Bora was among those seen attempting to breach the police cordon. Senior advocates Prashant Bhushan and Kapil Sibal also participated in the protest.The mobilisation began from Andhra Bhawan Circle on Ashoka Road, with protesters raising slogans against Kumar and demanding his resignation.AISA members later alleged that Bora was taken away in a private vehicle and that her whereabouts were initially unknown.The organisation said the detention took place as its activists attempted to return to Jantar Mantar for the third consecutive day despite heavy barricading and security arrangements.Visuals showed Bora attempting to climb over a barricade as police officials tried to stop her.Cockroach Janta Party founder Abhijeet Dipke slammed Delhi Police for detaining Bora, saying it has âonce again shown cowardiceâ.In a post on X, Dipke said, âDelhi Police has once again shown its cowardice by detaining Neha and Rosy for simply raising their voices. Rosy yesterday was molested by ACP Vivek Bhagat and instead of acting against the pervert, the cops detained her.âSo much for women empowerment Narendra Modi,â he added.More than a dozen AAP workers were detained during the protest at India Gate, including Delhi unit chief Saurabh Bharadwaj and MLA Sanjeev Jha.Visuals from the protest showed AAP workers blocking buses carrying detained protesters as security personnel tried to clear the area. The situation escalated when protesters broke through barricades and moved towards Jantar Mantar, where Delhi Police and the Rapid Action Force were deployed to stop them.Bharadwaj alleged that police manhandled him during the detention and said protesters were being treated harshly.âThey are picking me up and throwing me around like I am a football... There is such a large police force here, yet they are not even registering an FIR against their own ACP, nor are they arresting the ACP,â he said.Bharadwaj also shared a photograph on X, saying he had been turned upside down by Delhi Police at India Gate to hide his face from cameras.âThese are my shoes in the air,â he said.AAP chief Arvind Kejriwal criticised the police action on X, saying, âThis is absolutely shocking. Modi ji has left even Hitler behind.âThe protests have also triggered a controversy over allegations of sexual harassment and misconduct by police personnel during Saturdayâs demonstrations.Three women identifying themselves as journalists complained that they were manhandled and sexually harassed by police officers while covering the protests near Jantar Mantar on October 3.Delhi Police said the complaints had been received, medical examinations conducted and the matter transferred to the Crime Branch for a âfair and impartial enquiryâ.CPM leader Brinda Karat criticised the police over the handling of the complaints and questioned the reported demand for video evidence before registering an FIR.âNow, when sexual harassment is happening with a journalist and Delhi Police is trying to save him and it is being asked to show the video,â Karat said, calling the response âextremely wrongâ.Opposition leaders, including Rahul Gandhi, have also criticised the alleged police conduct and demanded accountability.More than 500 protesters, including student activists and political leaders, were detained during demonstrations in central Delhi on Friday. AAP leaders, Bora and activist Yogendra Yadav were among those detained.Police had denied permission for Fridayâs gathering and deployed additional personnel across central Delhi. Several roads leading towards Jantar Mantar were barricaded, while access to some metro stations in the area was temporarily restricted during the earlier protests.This comes after a report in The Indian Express said Election Commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi had formally raised objections on at least 14 occasions over 10 months regarding decisions concerning electoral rolls, voter registration and the Commissionâs technology sy

World.title: 'Russia stood by us when our territorial integrity was under threat': Jaishankar
World.content:
Jaishankar said India and Russia had maintained strong relations since the 1950s.

Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: External affairs minister S Jaishankar on Sunday highlighted India's longstanding ties with Russia, saying the country had stood by us when New Delhi's security and territorial integrity faced threats and much of the world preferred backing a military regime.Speaking at the Munich Leaders Meeting, Jaishankar said India and Russia had maintained strong relations since the 1950s and that the legacy of those ties continued to shape the relationship.âIndia and Russia have historically very good relations, particularly since the 1950s. That history is not forgotten,â Jaishankar said.He added that Russia which was Soviet Union before âstood by us in many ways when our security, when our territorial integrity was under threatâ.âAt a time when much of the world preferred backing a military regime (Pakistan) next to us, Russia was a country with which our relations were very good, and we are shaped in many ways by that legacy,â he said.âToday, the relationship has widened beyond that... It is very much more today an economic relationship as well. So there is a military component, there are nuclear component, there is space issues, but there is a significant amount of trade and investment between the two countries and energy and resources as well...India's experience has been quite positive and consistently positiveâ he added.Jaishankar also said India had moved beyond simply advocating dialogue and diplomacy to taking a more active role in efforts to resolve the Ukraine conflict.He said India had held conversations with both Kyiv and Moscow in recent months and was trying to address some immediate concerns arising from the conflict.âOur position on that conflict has been very clear, which is that we would like to see an end to this conflict. This will require dialogue and diplomacy. There has to be negotiations in this regard,â he said.âWe have been advocating it for many years, and in recent months we have got a little bit more involved beyond advocacy. We have conversations with both Russia and Ukraine in this regard. We are trying to be helpful, starting with the Black Sea safety of shipping issue,â he added.Jaishankar said India's efforts were focused initially on ensuring the safety of shipping in the Black Sea, while also addressing issues related to grain and energy exports.âIndia is going beyond that to cover some immediate concerns which both of them (Russia and Ukraine) have on grain exports, energy exports, non-attack possibilities. Those are ongoing conversations right now,â he said.His remarks came days after Russian President Vladimir Putin said Prime Minister Narendra Modi had âgood ideasâ for finding a mutually acceptable solution to the conflict.Ukraine foreign minister Andrii Sybiha had also said on Friday that Kyiv received separate proposals from India and three other countries on a possible ceasefire. India has for more than four years maintained that the Ukraine conflict should be resolved through dialogue and diplomacy, PTI reported.PM Modi held wide-ranging talks with Putin in Bishkek on August 31. During the meeting, the Prime Minister stated that âendless war must now give way to end of warâ.

World.title: 300 students take on AI, deepfake fraud challenges at BIT Mesra hackathon
World.content:
RANCHI: More than 300 students from Birla Institute of Technology (BIT) Mesra took part in in a 24-hour hackathon focused on some of the most pressing challenges emerging from the rapid adoption of artificial intelligence, including high-precision generative AI systems, deepfake-driven insurance fraud and agentic AI applications.

The event, Adrosonic Build, organised by technology company Adrosonic, has attracted 106 teams comprising around three students each. Twenty-one teams have been shortlisted for the final round, which began on October 3 and will conclude with the announcement of results on October 4.

Unlike conventional coding competitions, the hackathon is centred on real-world industry problems. Participants are developing solutions for high-precision Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) systems, AI-powered detection of synthetic identities and deepfake-based insurance claims, and agentic Statement of Values (SOV) intelligence systems for the insurance sector.

Highlighting the broader objective of the initiative, Mayank, founder, CEO and MD of Adrosonic, said the idea was to bring practical industry knowledge, real-world use cases and access to technology leaders into the academic ecosystem so that students can work on problems that mirror actual business and societal challenges.

Faculty members say such platforms are becoming increasingly important as employers seek graduates who can apply technical knowledge to complex situations rather than merely demonstrate theoretical understanding.





âThe gap is not in knowledge. It is in applying that knowledge to real-life scenarios, which are more uncertain and complex,â said Dr Manish Kumar Pandey, head of the Digital Innovation Lab and Department of Quantitative Economics and Data Science at BIT Mesra.

The hackathon is part of a wider industry-academia partnership between Adrosonic and BIT Mesra that has been underway since 2022. The collaboration led to the establishment of the Digital Innovation Lab (DIL) in 2024, with an investment of around Rs 5 crore.

The facility provides students access to infrastructure and technologies spanning artificial intelligence, machine learning, large language models and data science.

Over the past two years, the partnership has expanded through fellowship programmes, industry-led initiatives and mentorship opportunities, allowing students to engage with professionals and gain exposure to practical technology applications beyond the classroom.

The event was inaugurated on October 2 in the presence of senior faculty members, including Prof Vishal H Shah, associate dean, alumni and international relations, and Dr Kishore Kumar Sinapati, along with representatives from Adrosonic. As teams race against time to build and present working solutions, the hackathon offers a glimpse into how institutes are preparing students for an AI-driven future.

External affairs minister S Jaishankar said India has the potential to move rapidly up the global power hierarchy over the next five to 10 years, citing decades of high growth ahead, a supportive demographic profile and the emergence of new economic opportunities.Speaking at the Munich Leaders Meeting in New Delhi on Sunday, Jaishankar was asked where India would be positioned in the global order five to 10 years from now. He said countries currently classified as middle powers would not necessarily follow the same trajectory.âSome powers are more middle, and some are upper middle,â Jaishankar said. âSome of the powers have considerable and realistic potential even in the near short medium term to grow very rapidly.âTurning to India, Jaishankar said the country has âdecades of high growthâ ahead and argued that its demographic profile could help sustain that growth.âIn the case of India, because we have decades of high growth ahead of us, and we have all said and done, a demography that will sustain that growth,â he said.Jaishankar also argued that India may not need to follow the traditional industrialisation path taken by earlier economies, pointing to the emergence of new possibilities in a rapidly changing global economy.âI would even argue, a world that is much more creative, where many new possibilities are there, so that we don't necessarily have to tread the earlier path of industrialization,â he said.âThe orthodox path will have to devise something much more contemporary for what awaits us,â he added.Jaishankar said the global power hierarchy is likely to evolve unevenly, with countries currently grouped together as middle powers potentially moving in different directions.âAmong the middle powers, some will peel off, some will stay put, some may drop down a bit,â he said.âThat is the reality. That will be part of the evolution of the global order,â Jaishankar added.His remarks came during a wider discussion on the changing international power structure at the Munich Leaders Meeting in New Delhi. The meeting is being held on October 4 and 5 and brings together senior decision-makers and experts to discuss foreign and security policy issues.Earlier during the discussion, Jaishankar said the United States and China should not be viewed as middle powers, highlighting their vastly different levels of global influence.âWhen we say what the prospects are, we are also looking at an international landscape. As I said, what is important to define is what is not a middle power,â he said.On the US, Jaishankar said Washington has been the âunderwriter of the global system for many decadesâ and has âa significant lead over any other powerâ.He then pointed to Chinaâs economic strength, saying it accounts for âone third of the global manufacturingâ and that its economic capabilities are translating into political influence.âThis is really, in a sense, the subject matter of our discussion,â Jaishankar said.The Munich Leaders Meeting is a platform organised by the Munich Security Conference, a leading international forum on security and foreign policy. The New Delhi meeting on October 4 and 5 brings together senior decision-makers and experts from the Indo-Pacific, Europe and the US for discussions on major geopolitical, foreign and security policy issues.

World.title: Yemen presidency announces military drive to retake all Houthi territory
World.content:
Yemen's leader announced on Sunday (October 4, 2026) the start of a new military operation to retake all territory held by the Houthis, even as the group made fresh gains on the ground, effectively encircling a government-held city.

The announcement sets an ambitious goal for the embattled government, which recently lost large swathes of the country's Red Sea coastline and areas around the Bab al-Mandab Strait — a chokepoint for international shipping — after a lightning offensive by the Iran-backed Houthis.

Yemen's government has struggled to roll back the surge, even with the military support of Saudi Arabia, where the Houthis said they had attacked oil infrastructure in the capital yet again on Sunday (October 4).

"I announce today the start of military operations to retake the remaining territories of the republic and extend the authority of the state and its institutions across the entire national territory," Rashad al-Alimi, the head of Yemen's presidential council, said in a statement.

Mr. Alimi called on all the armed forces "to begin carrying out their assigned missions, in accordance with the approved plans, until the country is liberated from the grip of the Houthi terrorist militia".

The statement came just hours after the Houthis cut a vital supply route linking the besieged city of Taiz with the government's interim capital Aden, according to four security sources.

The Houthi advance followed days of heavy fighting in and around the city.

"We were informed that the Houthis had taken control of the al-Safiya area, where they cut the main road and took control of the police station," a police source in the area told AFP.

Three sources with the Yemeni military also confirmed Houthi control over the area and the supply route, with traffic along the road halted and the group now surrounding Taiz city.

The military sources added that fighting in the area was ongoing.

Taiz itself remains under the control of government forces but has long been besieged from the north, east and west by Houthi fighters and remains one of the main fronts in Yemen's long-running civil war.

"They've achieved the military objective of isolating Taiz from Aden, even if they haven't fully taken control of it," Farea Al-Muslimi, research fellow at the Chatham House think-tank, told AFP.

Muslimi also downplayed expectations over what the coming government offensive might accomplish.

"In my opinion, it's meaningless, he added.

Saudi attacks

Following several years of relative calm, Yemen's civil war reignited in July against the backdrop of the wider conflict in the West Asia.

It has also drawn in Saudi Arabia — leader of an anti-Houthi military coalition since 2015 — with the group regularly claiming attacks on the kingdom's territory in recent weeks and declaring a blockade of its ships in the Red Sea.

Houthi military spokesman Yahya Saree on Sunday said the group launched ballistic missiles and drones at Saudi energy giant Aramco's sites in Riyadh and in the oil-rich Khurais area in the east.

"The strikes were precise, causing large fires at the targeted sites," Mr. Saree said on X.

Saudi oil exports were already under pressure thanks to Iran's blockade of the Strait of Hormuz in the Gulf.

The Houthis' Al-Masirah TV channel reported Saudi strikes Sunday in the northern governorates of al-Jawf and Saada, saying at least two people had been wounded.

They came a day after Yemen's government said its forces struck Houthi targets around the country, including in the capital Sanaa, the northwestern governorate of Saada and the group's positions near Taiz in the southwest.

The Yemeni government's air capabilities, however, are limited, and the Saudi-led coalition has long been the primary force carrying out airstrikes against the Houthis.

Experts believe the recent operations have most likely been conducted by Saudi warplanes as well.

Yemen is one of the poorest countries in the world and remains gripped by a vast humanitarian crisis that has unspooled since the civil war broke out in 2014.

That year the Houthis seized the capital Sanaa from the Saudi-backed government, before going on to take control of much of the country's north, with Riyadh's international coalition intervening the following year.

World.title: Navy sailor arrested for allegedly leaking classified information to Pakistani intelligence operative
World.content:
The Counter Intelligence Cell of the Andhra Pradesh police has arrested a 31-year-old Navy sailor, Pradeep Mukherjee, for allegedly leaking classified maritime information to a Pakistani intelligence operative through a social media honey trap, sources said on Sunday.

Mr. Mukherjee, who joined the Indian Navy in 2014, is now posted with the Eastern Naval Command in Visakhapatnam. He was undergoing a training programme at Coimbatore when he was arrested on October 3.

Honey trap

Mr. Mukherjee met a female Pakistani intelligence operative on social media a few months ago, according to preliminary information from the Counter Intelligence cell’s probe, sources said. Gradually, the operative developed a relationship with the sailor and allegedly obtained sensitive information from him about the Navy.

It was learnt that the Counter Intelligence Cell first detected suspicious digital activity linked to Mr. Mukherjee. He was subsequently placed under surveillance, before he was arrested. Sources said that Mr. Mukherjee is being brought from Coimbatire in Tamil Nadu to Andhra Pradesh, using a prisoner transfer warrant. He will be produced before the court at Vijayawada on October 5, sources said.

World.title: Trump names national intelligence director Jay Clayton to lead a new federal AI task force
World.content:
U.S. President Donald Trump on Sunday (October 4, 2026) tapped Jay Clayton, his director of national intelligence, to lead a new government task force on artificial intelligence.

Trump is calling it the “Super Intelligence Force,” because he has tried to rebrand AI as “super intelligence.” The announcement comes after Trump hosted top executives of AI companies at the White House last week and said they had signed a voluntary accord that would effectively self-police the development of the technology.

The task force will coordinate the federal effort "to ensure that America continues to lead the World in Super Intelligence, which many say is bigger than the Industrial Revolution, and the Internet, and will protect the interests, and improve the lives, of all Americans,” Trump in a post on social media Sunday.

The task force will reach out to consumers, public interest groups, religious organizations, critical infrastructure providers and AI companies, the Republican president said.

Others on the task force include the Federal Trade Commission's chairman, Andrew Ferguson; Emil Michael, the Pentagon’s chief technology officer; and Scott Kupor, the director of the Office of Personnel Management.

The group will report to Mr. Trump and his chief of staff, Susie Wiles.

World.title: Two furniture shops gutted in early-morning blaze near Medchal checkpost
World.content:
A major fire broke out at two adjoining furniture shops near Medchal checkpost in the wee hours of Sunday (October 4), destroying furniture and other material stored inside the establishments.

The Fire Department received the call at 1.22 a.m., following which two fire tenders, one each from Shamirpet and Jeedimetla fire stations, were rushed to the spot.

The blaze is suspected to have started in one of the furniture shops before rapidly spreading to the adjoining establishment. Thick smoke from the shops alerted residents and passers-by, who informed the fire control room.

Firefighters battled the blaze for about an hour before bringing it under control. No injuries or casualties were reported. A large quantity of furniture and other goods was destroyed in the fire, though officials were yet to assess the value of the damage.

Police also reached the spot and began an inquiry. Preliminary findings indicated that an electrical short circuit could have triggered the fire, but the exact cause was yet to be established by police and fire officials.

World.title: Chaotic traffic on Tiruchi-Karur road irks commuters
World.content:
Chaotic traffic around the Chathiram Bus Stand in the city has irked the commuters.

Driving on the roads around the Chathiram Bus Stand had become a challenge because of poor traffic management, unregulated parking of buses, and lack of proper infrastructure. But the situation turned worse recently with a section of shoppers parking their cars on the busy Tiruchi-Karur Road.

Chathiram Bus Stand, which caters to town bus services and the mofussil terminus functioning on the adjacent roadsides, attracts thousands of commuters every day. Other road users have to cut across bustling roads, amidst buses dropping and picking up passengers all around the bus stand. The mofussil terminus outside Chathiram Bus Stand in the city has been functioning around the overhead tank complex - Kamaraj Statue junction and along the road towards Anna Statue junction without proper bus bays or shelters and other amenities.

Commuters have to jostle for space with vendors, customers to the establishments, vehicles parked on the roadside with a slew of hotels, commercial establishments and a cinema complex in the vicinity. A big new textile showroom and expansion of an old textile showroom have added to the congestion.

What caused chaos is the random parking of cars occupying precious road space. Traffic holds up in the area by the time the shoppers alight from the cars. Those heading to Coimbatore and Karur board the buses at the same spot. The roadside vendors add their part to the chaos.

“The traffic around the Chathiram Bus Stand, especially on the Tiruchi-Karur Road, annoys commuters. We do not know whether the commercial establishments have sufficient space for parking. How can move move past the area when the busy road is used for parking,” asks M. Gunasekaran, a commuter.

Manimaran, Assistant Commissioner, Traffic, Tiruchi, told The Hindu that the traffic on the Tiruchi-Karur Road at Chathiram Bus Stand was being closely monitored. Policemen had been posted in the area to regulate the traffic. The newly opened showroom had shown a space for parking 110 two-wheelers. A list of parking lots for cars visiting the commercial establishments in the area had been sought. The police would straight away impose fines on cars, if they were parked on the road, he said.

World.title: Gandhi’s vast spiritual universe of devotion has gained greater relevance: Prof. Tolpadi
World.content:
Mahatma Gandhi stands among India’s greatest philosophers. His distinctive philosophy and his vast spiritual universe of devotion have gained even greater relevance today than ever before, said Rajaram Tolpadi, retired professor of Mangalore University.

He delivered a special lecture on ‘Gandhiji and Rashtra Kavi Govinda Pai’, organised by Rashtra Kavi Manjeshwara Govinda Pai Memorial Trust at Gilivindu, the residence of Pai in Manjeshwar, Kasaragod district, Keralam, on Friday (October 2).

Speaking about Gandhiji’s devotional depth, he said that the Mahatma’s prayer meetings featured devotional songs such as Vaishnava Janato Tene Kahiye and Raghupati Raghav Rajaram, revealing a profound radiance of bhakti. A sincere devotee of Rama, Gandhiji saw both Eshwar and Allah as manifestations of the divine. Gandhiji represented the finest modern expression of India’s bhakti tradition, simultaneously standing as one of the country’s foremost philosophers, Prof. Tolpadi noted.

‘Gandhiji must return’

S. Sujeesh, assistant professor of Kannada at Manjeshwara Govinda Pai Government College, said that in Govinda Pai’s poem written after India attained Independence — Varusha 14 neenu namage bidugade nidi… Mahatma, you should have lived longer; you lived beyond death, Mahatma, you are blessed… — one finds a yearning for Gandhiji’s return, meaning the return of Gandhian thought.

For Pai, Gandhiji was not merely a leader of the freedom struggle. He was the embodiment of truth, non‑violence, sacrifice, simplicity, social equality, and humaneness, he said.

The poem questions whether the India Gandhi envisioned — an India of Ramarajya, truth, non‑violence, and human values — has truly been built. Freedom, Pai suggests, is not merely liberation from foreign rule; true freedom is when every individual receives dignity, equal opportunity, and the right to live fully, he said.

World.title: Man dies after off-road vehicle crashes into house in Kozhikode
World.content:
A 62-year-old man died after an off-road vehicle, which was being reversed after dropping off a passenger at a house where a funeral was being held, lost control and crashed into the building at Kavumvattam near Koyilandy on Sunday (October 4, 2026) morning.

The deceased has been identified as K. Rajan. The accident occurred around 7.45 a.m. Rajan, who was standing in the courtyard, sustained serious injuries when the vehicle rammed into the house.

He was taken to the Koyilandy taluk hospital and later shifted to the Government Medical College Hospital, Kozhikode, for specialised treatment. He died while undergoing treatment. Another person who had arrived at the house to attend the funeral and the vehicle driver also sustained injuries in the accident.

Several people who were in the courtyard at the time of the accident escaped unhurt after managing to move away when the vehicle suddenly veered out of control. A portion of the house wall was also damaged in the accident.

World.title: Dentist dismissed after joining black flag protest against Minister in Keralam
World.content:
A dentist working temporarily at the Kanhangad District Hospital under the National Health Mission was removed from service after he participated in a black flag protest organised by the Democratic Youth Federation of India (DYFI) against Sports Minister O.J. Janeesh in Kanhangad.

Dr. Sidharth Ravindran was dismissed after authorities concluded that his participation in the political protest violated the terms and conditions of the agreement he had signed while joining the service.

Case registered

The incident occurred on Thursday when Mr. Janeesh arrived in Kasaragod district to attend various programmes. The DYFI organised a black flag protest against the Minister at Kanhangad in which Dr. Ravindran also participated. Photographs showing the doctor taking part in the protest by waving black flag at the Minister’s vehicle subsequently emerged. The Hosdurg police had registered a case against Dr. Sidharth in connection with the protest. Also, Youth Congress activists submitted a complaint, accompanied by photographs showing the doctor’s participation in the protest, to the Health department. Following the complaint, action was initiated against him.

The dismissal order reportedly cited violation of the conditions of the agreement signed by Dr. Sidharth with the District Health and Family Welfare Society at the time of his appointment. According to health authorities, participation in a political protest contrary to the terms of the agreement was the basis for the action.

World.title: 'We are not yes-men': CM Afridi launches PTI long march to Islamabad from Lakki Marwat
World.content:
PESHAWAR/LAKKI MARWAT/DI KHAN: Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Chief Minister Sohail Afridi on Sunday launched the PTI’s long march towards Islamabad from Gandi Chowk in Lakki Marwat, saying the party would “not accept” any policy that was against the interests of the people of KP.

Afridi reached Lakki Marwat by helicopter to lead the PTI’s long march, which is being held to demand the release of jailed party founder and former prime minister Imran Khan. The march was launched from Gandi Chowk on the Peshawar-Karachi Indus Highway.

Addressing thousands of participants, Afridi urged the public to step out of their homes for the sake of Pakistan, saying Imran, along with his wife and sisters, was in prison and they should show the world that they were the “true owners” of the country.

He said the “PTI’s negotiating committee had gone to Islamabad to lower the political temperature, but those making decisions behind closed doors had sabotaged the talks.

“They wanted their will to prevail in KP, but I declared that only Imran Khan’s vision and policies would be implemented here. We do not accept any policy that is not in the interest of the people of KP and the Pashtuns,” he maintained.

The chief minister declared: “We are not ‘yes-men’; we are soldiers of Imran Khan, and we will carry forward his policies.”

He repeatedly asked the crowd whether it supported a military operation, asking those opposed to it to raise their hands.

He questioned the policy being followed to tackle terrorism, saying: “What kind of policy is this, where terrorism has persisted for 22 years?”

KP CM insisted there had been peace during Imran’s government because his policies were sound, but following the “regime change operation”, terrorists were resettled, leading to “infinite terrorism”.

In 2023, after his ouster, Imran had defended his government’s plan to resettle members of the Tehreek-i-Taliban Pakistan.

“We will eradicate terrorism, and if our policy is implemented, we will restore peace within 100 days,” he claimed.

He said the long march was being launched from Gandi Chowk and would conclude at another chowk. At this, the crowd shouted: “D-Chowk.”

“We are a political force and a party, and those who dream of the demise of the PTI can never succeed,” he added.

Afridi said the participants would leave from Gandi Chowk and their next stop would be Karak.

PTI workers had started gathering at Gandi Chowk on the Peshawar-Karachi Highway on Sunday afternoon to participate in the long march. Strict security measures were in place, with a large police contingent deployed at the site along with armoured personnel carriers and bomb disposal squads.

Kundi, Tarar slam use of ‘state helicopter’

A special helipad was prepared near Maidadkhel for Afridi and a video shared on social media platforms earlier showed a crowd of PTI workers gathered around it as KP’s chief executive touched down.

A video shared by the PTI on its X account showed Afridi’s convoy surrounded by a large crowd of party workers and supporters.

Information Minister Attaullah Tarar criticised Afridi for using a “state helicopter for a political march”.

Calling the use of the helicopter a “violation of the Islamabad High Court’s orders”, he wrote on X, referring to a recent ruling that directed provincial governments to ensure that no government resources or machinery was used to facilitate any march or gathering.

“Terrorism is spreading in the province and Nero is playing his flute,” Tarar quipped.

KP Governor Faisal Karim Kundi also said the use of the helicopter amounted to contempt of court by violating the IHC order.

“When the chief minister himself does not uphold the court’s orders and uses state resources for political activities, what expectation can there be for his workers to abide by the law?” Kundi wrote on X.

Special Assistant to the KP CM for Home and Tribal Affairs Tariq Saad told journalists at his residence that, in accordance with the PTI leadership’s decision, the “peaceful long” march would commence from Gandi Chowk today, with convoys from the southern districts joining it.

He said PTI workers from Bannu, DI Khan, Tank, North Waziristan and South Waziristan would gather at Gandi Chowk to participate in the march.

“If workers from some southern districts, especially Tank and Waziristan, could not attend the long march today due to law and order-related curfew and other restrictions, they would join the movement on the way to Peshawar the next day,” he said.

Gandapur leads caravan from DI Khan

Earlier, PTI workers and supporters, led by former KP CM Ali Amin Gandapur, set out from Dera Ismail Khan to join the party’s long march at Lakki Marwat.

The convoy, according to Gandapur, would travel through Yarik and Pezu before reaching Gandi Chowk in Lakki Marwat.

Before departing from DI Khan, the ex-CM stressed that the protest should remain peaceful and urged the participants to maintain discipline and refrain from violence, vandalism and confrontation with law enforcement personnel.

He said the party would follow a policy of “live and let live” during the protest and directed workers not to take the law into their hands.

“Those who block roads or engage in confrontation are not our workers,” Gandapur said, asking the participants to remain peaceful throughout the march.

He further urged the participants to avoid any activity that could lead to clashes or damage to public or private property.

Describing the march as a continuation of the party’s political struggle, Gandapur said it represented a reaffirmation of the party’s commitment to PTI founder Imran.

“We have made sacrifices for Imran Khan before and will not hesitate to make further sacrifices,” he said, adding that the party would continue its “peaceful political struggle” for Imran’s release.

The PTI’s march, being carried out to demand the release of its jailed founder and ex-prime minister Imran Khan, is the latest bone of contention between the two sides.

In August, the PTI announced the long march to Islamabad on Sept 27 against what it called the “illegal imprisonment” of its party founder. However, a couple of days before its scheduled long march, the party postponed the march until Oct 4 (today).

Federal ministers have warned that the Centre would have no option but to impose governor’s rule or an emergency in KP, citing the province’s security situation and the protest call, while PTI has warned of dire consequences if such a step was taken.

After weekend talks, Adviser to the Prime Minister on Political Affairs Rana Sanaullah has further warned that the protesters will not be allowed to enter Islamabad.

Plan for the march

According to the plan for the march shared by the KP CM on X, PTI supporters from the districts of Tank, Dera Ismail Khan, South Waziristan, North Waziristan and Bannu will join the long march from Lakki Marwat’s Gandi Chowk on Oct 4.

The caravan will halt for the night near Karak, from where people will depart at 12:30pm the next day and stay overnight near Kohat.

Then, at 12pm on Oct 6, protesters from Kohat, Hangu, Kurram, and Orakzai will join the convoy, which will move towards Peshawar and spend the night near Mattani.

The caravan will depart from Budh Bair in Peshawar on Oct 7 afternoon. “The remaining constituencies of Peshawar will join us at Kohat Road Bridge and the Motorway Toll Plaza. And we will spend the night near Charsadda Interchange,” the KP CM said.

They would then depart the Charsadda Interchange at 12:30pm on Oct 8 after people from Charsadda and Mohmand join them.

Refraining from detailing the final leg of the trip to the federal capital, Afridi said the people “of entire KP” would gather at Khairabad on Oct 8 and spend the night there. “God willing, the plan for the next phase will be announced there.”

Ahead of the march, movement on several roads on KP has been banned under Section 144.

Section 144 imposed in several KP districts

Section 144 has been imposed in several districts of KP through notifications issued by the respective deputy commissioners, with restrictions on the movement of people and vehicles along specified routes, citing security and public safety concerns.
